grants.duration: Up to 5 years (PhD); PDF and Young Faculty Research Fellowships also supported
grants.description: Supports 1,000 full-time and 150 part-time PhD candidates plus 225 post-doctoral and 50 young-faculty fellowships in ESDM and IT/ITES emerging areas including AI, cybersecurity, quantum, VLSI, and HPC through 2030.

grants.name: Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF), Direct and Lateral Entry
grants.funder: Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Selection runs twice a year (May and December cycles), and the call may come later than those months. Applications go through institute nomination; check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 70,000 to 80,000/month plus INR 2 lakh/year research grant
grants.description: PhD fellowship at IITs, IISc, IISERs, NITs, and select institutions in science and technology. Direct entry from top UG programmes; Lateral entry for early PhD scholars. Distinct from the ANRF-CII PMRF-DR industry-partnered doctoral scheme.

grants.name: Bhaskara Advanced Solar Energy (BASE) Fellowship
grants.funder: Indo-US Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) / DST
grants.deadlineNote: The page shows no open call. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend, international return airfare, and contingency allowance
grants.description: Supports Indian PhD students (up to 32 years) and Indian PhD-holders (up to 40 years) working in solar energy for research stints at US institutions. A parallel US track brings US researchers to India.

grants.name: Indo-US Fellowship for Women in STEMM (WISTEMM)
grants.funder: Indo-US Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) / DST
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. Separate Women Overseas Fellowship and Women Student Internship tracks; check the IUSSTF portal for the current cycle.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend, international airfare, and contingency
grants.description: Sends Indian women scientists and engineers to collaborate at US institutions. Student Internship track for PhD candidates aged 21 to 35; Fellowship track for PhD-holders aged 27 to 45 holding a regular academic or R&D position in India.

grants.name: Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure (FIST)
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Calls are posted on DST's call for proposals page and the onlinedst portal; the most recent FIST call found there was FIST 2024, which closed 30 April 2024. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: INR 1.5 crore (Level 0) to INR 10 crore (Level 3)
grants.description: Departmental infrastructure grants for science, medical, agriculture, and engineering departments (with 3+ years of PG research) in UGC/AICTE-recognised universities and higher educational institutions. Supports equipment, lab modernisation, computational facilities, and networking.

grants.name: Outstanding Postdoctoral Program
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 29 November 2026. Pre-application visits must be completed by 15 January 2027; admission decisions by mid-February 2027.
grants.amount: Tax-free Excellence Fellowship of USD 55,000 per year for three years (paid in NIS)
grants.description: Weizmann fellowship for international postdocs (including CS and mathematics) within four years of their PhD. Open to Indian nationals with a PhD from a non-Weizmann institution. The host lab at Weizmann must be identified before submission.

grants.name: IAS School of Mathematics Membership
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027-28 membership close 1 December 2026 via MathJobs; recommendation letters are due the same day.
grants.amount: Stipend plus housing subsidy; visitor tier available without stipend
grants.duration: One term to a full academic year
grants.description: Open membership for mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists at any career stage; particularly relevant for logic, foundations, and theoretical CS given the annual thematic year. India-based researchers regularly hold memberships.

grants.name: Fields Research Fellowship
grants.funder: Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences, Toronto
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadlines 15 January, 15 May and 15 September; submit at least three months before the proposed start. FY27 funding is fully committed, so applications are now for visits starting on or after 1 April 2027.
grants.amount: Living-expense allowance of up to CAD 4,000 per month of full-time residence
grants.description: Short research visit for faculty and research scientists in mathematical sciences, either in residence at Fields or with a collaborator at a Fields Principal Sponsoring University. India-based mathematicians, logicians, and theoretical CS researchers can apply directly with a cover letter, CV, and short proposal.

grants.name: AI for Math Fund
grants.funder: Renaissance Philanthropy (with XTX Markets and others)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 round closed for abstracts on 30 March 2026, with decisions in August 2026. Seed grants of up to USD 100,000 are reviewed on a rolling basis.
grants.amount: USD 100K to 1M per project; seed grants up to USD 100K
grants.description: USD 31.5M fund supporting projects that apply AI and machine learning to mathematics, including autoformalisation, theorem proving, and mathematical discovery. Open to individuals and teams worldwide including India-based researchers, students, and postdocs. Strong fit for logic, CS, and math researchers.

grants.name: KAUST Global Fellowship Program
grants.funder: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Saudi Arabia
grants.deadlineNote: Call 2027 Stage 1 concept notes closed 1 October 2026. Invited applicants submit full proposals between 15 November 2026 and 15 January 2027.
grants.amount: Full salary plus benefits and an independent research budget
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowship for early-career researchers to pursue independent research at KAUST, with strong CS, AI, and mathematics divisions. Open to applicants from any country including India.

grants.name: Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations accepted year-round. Approximately 20 awards per year, with a six-month review.
grants.amount: EUR 60,000 award money
grants.duration: Research stay of up to 12 months in Germany
grants.description: Mid-career award for internationally recognised researchers up to 18 years post-PhD, to spend up to a year with German collaborators. Nomination-based via a German host academic; India-based CS and logic researchers with strong research profiles are directly eligible.

grants.name: DFG Mercator Fellowship (Mercator Module)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. The Mercator Fellows module is requested within a DFG project proposal, so it follows that programme's deadlines.
grants.amount: Covers travel and residence during German stays plus a lump sum
grants.duration: Flexible; several visits over the project lifetime
grants.description: Enables India-based researchers to join a DFG-funded German project as a long-term collaborator through extended research stays in Germany, awarded via a German PI's proposal. Broadly applicable to CS and logic collaborations with German groups.

grants.name: Toyota Foundation International Grant Program
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call ran from 1 April to 30 May 2026. The 2027 call has not been announced.
grants.region: Asia (India eligible; project must span 2 or more Asian countries)
grants.amount: Up to JPY 10,000,000 (approx USD 65,000) for two-year projects; JPY 5,000,000 for one-year
grants.description: Grants for cross-border Asian collaboration on shared societal issues, including science policy, technology in society, and computational approaches to public problems. India is on the eligible-country list (with Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka); projects must be led jointly across at least two eligible countries.

grants.name: DRDO DIA-CoE Research Problems September 2026
grants.funder: Directorate of Futuristic Technology Management (DFTM), DRDO, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Notice valid through December 2026 for 19 specified research problems. Proposals routed to the relevant DIA-CoE research vertical. No fixed award ceiling or duration stated.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Multi-institutional, multidisciplinary research proposals addressing 19 defence research problems through the DRDO Industry Academia-Centre of Excellence (DIA-CoE) network. Topics include stealth materials, aerospace modelling, radar and signal processing, autonomous navigation, power electronics, semiconductor detectors, and fuzing. Open to Indian academia and national research institutes using the official proposal forms.

grants.name: ASM Future Leaders Mentorship Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 cohort open in February 2027 and are due in March 2027. Exact date not announced.
grants.amount: Structured mentoring, leadership and professional-development training, networking and collaboration opportunities
grants.description: Two-year online programme pairing master's and doctoral students in microbial sciences with experienced mentors across academia, industry, government, and other sectors. Fellows must be ASM members for 2027, hold master's or doctoral student status, show a strong microbial-sciences background, and commit to the full two-year term.

grants.name: DHR Human Resource Development Sub-Scheme for Health Research 2026-27
grants.funder: Department of Health Research (DHR), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals due via DHR e-PMS portal by 5:00 PM on 30 November 2026. Current call restricted to applicants from Northeastern states: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Capacity-building programme for advanced medical and health research. Covers the Women Scientist Fellowship Programme and the NRI/PIO/OCI Research Support Programme under the HRD Sub-Scheme. 2026-27 call limited to applicants from the eight Northeastern states.

grants.name: MCQST Junior Researcher START Fellowship
grants.funder: Munich Center for Quantum Science and Technology (MCQST)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call closed at 23:59 CEST on 24 October 2026; reference letters were due 31 October 2026. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Up to EUR 300,000 (salary, staff, equipment, consumables, travel)
grants.description: Independent-project fellowship for outstanding early-career researchers in quantum science and technology. Applicants must secure an MCQST PI host who provides infrastructure and a support letter.

grants.name: Syngene Early Career Research Grants 2026-27
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 30 November 2026. Three grants awarded. PhD in science and no more than eight years post-PhD as of December 2026. Permanent institutional position required; postdoctoral researchers not eligible. Institution must hold a CSR Registration Number.
grants.amount: INR 50 lakh per grant (excludes institutional overheads); three grantees
grants.description: Early-career research grants for innovative work spanning biology, chemistry, computation, and technology relevant to drug discovery and healthcare. Open to permanently appointed junior faculty, assistant professors, and junior research faculty in life sciences at Indian research institutes or universities.

grants.name: Pfizer Real World Evidence on Early Appropriate Use of Aztreonam-Avibactam (ATM-AVI)
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals due 23:59 EST on 25 November 2026. Projects expected to run June 2027 to December 2028. Applications must come from organisations, not individuals. Indian organisations require a valid FCRA certificate and IRB/IEC approval before project start.
grants.amount: Up to USD 50,000 per project; 2 to 3 awards; indirect costs capped at 28%
grants.description: Real-world clinical studies evaluating the impact of early, appropriate aztreonam-avibactam use guided by rapid diagnostics in adults with suspected or documented CRE or Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infection. PI must be an employee or contractor with an MD, PhD, equivalent research doctorate, advanced nursing, pharmacy, or microbiology degree.

grants.name: World Cancer Research Fund Regular Grant Programme 2026-27
grants.deadlineNote: The letter of intent call ran 5 October to 13 November 2026 (5pm UK time) and is now closed. LOI outcomes in February 2027; final decisions end of September 2027. Open to researchers anywhere in the world.
grants.amount: Investigator-initiated grants up to GBP 500,000; pilot and feasibility grants up to GBP 60,000
grants.duration: Up to 4 years (investigator-initiated); up to 2 years (pilot/feasibility)
grants.description: Research on diet, nutrition, body composition, physical activity, and sleep in cancer prevention or survivorship. Eligible organisations may be located anywhere in the world.

grants.name: ICMR First in the World Challenge Grants 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 5:30 PM on 30 November 2026 via e-PMS. Open to scientists at Indian government medical colleges, INIs, ICMR institutes, universities, recognised R&D laboratories, NGOs (with required registrations), start-ups, MSMEs, and industry. At least one co-PI from the PI's institution is mandatory.
grants.amount: Up to INR 1 crore (proof of concept), 4 crore (prototype), or 8 crore (final product or implementation model)
grants.duration: Up to 2, 3, or 4 years by stage
grants.description: Supports high-risk, high-reward biomedical and health-technology ideas that have not previously been thought of, tested, or tried anywhere. Three stages: proof of concept, prototype development, final product or implementation model. Applicants may apply individually or in teams.

grants.name: UNESCO-Al Fozan International Prize for Young Scientists in STEM
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations close midnight (UTC+1) on 30 November 2026. Eligible institutional nomination required; self-nominations are not accepted.
grants.amount: Prize for recognition of scientific contribution (see nomination page for current prize value)
grants.description: Biennial UNESCO prize recognising five young scientists under 40 for outstanding contributions in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Candidates must be nominated by an eligible institution, government, or professional body.

grants.name: MathWorks Call for Research Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: The 2 November 2026 deadline has passed.
grants.amount: Up to USD 20,000 unrestricted gift
grants.description: One-year research gifts for industry-relevant projects that use MATLAB or Simulink and advance AI-enabled engineering. Priority areas include aerospace and UAV systems, automotive and electric vehicles, wireless and radar, energy, robotics and autonomous systems, medical devices, and semiconductors. Open to current full-time faculty at accredited doctoral institutions.

grants.name: FCDO SRHR Applied Research Centre
grants.deadlineNote: Expressions of interest close 30 November 2026, 17:00 GMT. The centre runs July 2027 to March 2032 and must be led by an eligible LMIC institution, with the core programme covering at least six LMICs.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 12 million
grants.description: Establish an applied research centre addressing evidence gaps in sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). The centre will conduct demand-led research, strengthen capacity, and support evidence use across at least six low- and middle-income countries. A single LMIC institution or LMIC-led consortium may apply.

grants.name: DBT Emerging Frontiers in Biotechnology (EFB) 2026
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: The 6 October to 15 November 2026 window on DBT eProMIS has closed. EFB has run two windows a year; check DBT's call-for-proposals page for the next one.
grants.amount: Up to INR 100 lakh per project
grants.description: Investigator-led competitive research grants under two verticals: Biomedical Sciences (human health and disease, vaccines, diagnostics, drug development, genomics, biosensors) and Biological Sciences (plant, agricultural, and animal biotech, bio-energy, bio-resources, environmental biology). Open to researchers at academic institutions and R&D organisations.

grants.name: CSIR Travel Grant Scheme
grants.funder: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - Human Resource Development Group (CSIR-HRDG)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Applications must arrive 2 to 4 months before the event. No CSIR travel assistance in the prior three years.
grants.amount: Up to full actual airfare from the nearest Indian airport to the event and back
grants.description: Travel support for young Indian researchers, research associates, resident doctors, emeritus scientists, and other non-regular researchers presenting at international scientific events. Applicants need relevant qualifications, refereed publications, an accepted lead- or single-author paper or invited chair/keynote role, and institutional endorsement.

grants.name: Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship India
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 India round closed 20 April 2026. The 2027 India call has not been announced.
grants.amount: INR 10 lakh per winning team per year, renewable once
grants.description: Fellowship for PhD and master's teams at 16 eligible Indian institutes including IISc, IITs, IIITs, and ISI Kolkata, with a Qualcomm research mentor. Covers CS, AI, systems, and signal processing. Requires a short research proposal and faculty endorsement.

grants.name: Simons-Berkeley Research Fellowship
grants.funder: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing, UC Berkeley
grants.deadlineNote: The Fall 2027 call (Diffusion Generative Modeling programme) opened 1 October 2026; applications are due 1 December 2026.
grants.amount: Competitive stipend, housing, and visa support
grants.description: Semester-long fellowship for theoretical computer scientists and mathematicians within five years of their PhD. Fellows participate in a Simons Institute programme on topics such as pseudorandomness, high-dimensional expanders, or symmetry in computation. India-based postdocs are eligible subject to home-institution approval.

grants.name: Dagstuhl Seminar Proposals
grants.funder: Schloss Dagstuhl, Leibniz Center for Informatics
grants.deadlineNote: The 1 November 2026 deadline has passed; the next listed deadline is 15 April 2027.
grants.amount: Full travel and accommodation for invited participants
grants.duration: 5-day on-site seminar for up to 48 participants
grants.description: Teams of three to four computer scientists from different institutions can propose a week-long seminar at Dagstuhl, Germany, around a well-defined research theme. India-based researchers can serve as organisers and name invited participants, with Dagstuhl paying local costs for all invitees. Hybrid proposals require a separate concept section addressing time-zone and remote participation issues.

grants.name: Oberwolfach Workshop Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Annual 31 July deadline for workshops two years later. The next window closes 31 July 2027 for 2029 workshops.
grants.amount: Full lodging and meals at MFO for all participants
grants.description: Mathematicians can propose a full, half-size, or mini-workshop at the Oberwolfach institute. Proposals need a scientific focus, suggested participant list, and organiser team; female participation and representation are strongly encouraged. India-based mathematicians can lead or co-lead proposals. Distinct from the Research in Pairs (OWRF) scheme.

grants.name: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship
grants.deadlineNote: The Summer 2027 student call has closed; for 2027 only listed institutions qualify, IITs are excluded and only B.E./B.Tech students are eligible from India.
grants.amount: Round-trip airfare, housing, and student fees covered
grants.description: Research internship at a Canadian university for Indian BE and BTech students in their third or fourth year, matched to a Canadian faculty host. Students apply to three to ten projects across three or more provinces, with a minimum 70% cumulative GPA. The India track funded through AICTE supports about 300 interns per year.

grants.name: Infosys Prize
grants.deadlineNote: Annual prize; nominations are by invitation and generally open early in the year for about three months. The funder publishes each year's dates a few weeks in advance.
grants.amount: USD 100,000 purse plus medal and citation
grants.description: Annual prize for researchers of Indian origin working anywhere, or any researcher whose work impacts India, aged 40 or under. The Mathematical Sciences category explicitly covers mathematics, statistics, and theoretical computer science. Nominations come from senior researchers, not the candidate; the prize covers six categories including Physical Sciences and Engineering.

grants.name: SNSF Scientific Exchanges (as invited guest)
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals can be submitted at any time through mySNF, at least four months before the event or visit. Each applicant may apply once per calendar year. Revised regulations take effect on 1 January 2027.
grants.amount: Travel, accommodation and meals for visitors; research visits of 1 to 6 months, at CHF 3,500/month for visitors from DAC-list countries
grants.duration: Up to 6 months for a research visit, up to 5 days for an event
grants.description: An India-based researcher cannot apply directly, but Swiss hosts can bring them in as a visiting guest for up to six months or as a speaker at a workshop. Both the host and the visitor must hold a PhD for research visits; PhD students are eligible for event invitations. Useful for India-Switzerland collaborations with an existing Swiss counterpart.

grants.name: Simons Pivot Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 round is under review. Check the funder's site for the next call.
grants.amount: Full academic-year salary plus USD 10,000 research allowance; follow-on award up to USD 1.5M
grants.duration: 1-year training year, with a 5-year follow-on grant for selected fellows
grants.description: Supports faculty with a PhD or MD who want to pivot into a new field in natural sciences, engineering, mathematics, data science, or computer science. The fellow spends a year training with a mentor in the target field; the mentor receives USD 50,000. Open to faculty at institutions worldwide including India, subject to the home institution granting a full year of leave.

grants.name: Isaac Newton Institute Programme Proposals
grants.funder: Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Cambridge
grants.deadlineNote: Two deadlines per year, 31 January and 31 July, for programmes running two to three years later.
grants.amount: Participant travel and subsistence at INI during the programme
grants.description: Mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists can propose a thematic research programme at INI in Cambridge, co-organised with other senior researchers. Proposals cover mathematical sciences and cross-disciplinary mathematics, including statistics, data science, and mathematical biology. India-based researchers can co-organise and visit INI during the programme, which usually hosts around 50 visiting fellows.

grants.name: Global EbA Fund Medium-size Grants
grants.deadlineNote: The call ran 12 October to 16 November 2026 (11:59 pm PST) and is now closed. Check the funder's site for the next call. Projects must qualify as ecosystem-based adaptation, build on existing work, partner with local institutions, and target global, thematic, or ODA-eligible contexts. Government entities may collaborate but cannot receive grant funds.
grants.amount: Up to USD 500,000 per grant
grants.description: Collaborative, innovative projects that scale ecosystem-based adaptation through enabling environments, finance, human security, and policy alignment. Open to universities, research institutes, legally recognised NGOs, INGOs, IGOs, community-based and Indigenous Peoples' organisations, eligible private-sector companies, and consortia.

grants.name: Laura Bassi Scholarship (Winter 2026)
grants.deadlineNote: Winter 2026 deadline extended to 20 November 2026; results due 4 December 2026. Awards editorial assistance (not cash). Open worldwide without institutional, departmental, or national restrictions.
grants.amount: Editorial assistance valued at USD 750 (master's), USD 2,500 (doctoral), USD 500 (junior academics), or USD 5,000 toward open-access charges for eligible book authors and editors
grants.description: Funds editorial assistance for research on neglected topics in any discipline. Open to currently enrolled master's and doctoral candidates, and to academics within five years of starting full-time employment. The separate Bassi Foundation Press award supports eligible book authors and editors through an open-access publication charge.

grants.name: DBT Translational Biotechnology Research Networks
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling advertisement open from 7 September 2026 to 7 September 2027. Submit a Letter of Intent of up to 500 words through eProMIS.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Concise, high-impact biotechnology ideas that either bridge discovery and application through a clear translation pathway, proof of concept, and scale-up potential, or pursue discovery-driven frontier science with transformative potential. Scope includes health and life sciences; agriculture, food, and bioresources; environment, climate, and sustainability; industrial biotechnology; synthetic biology, genomics, engineering biology, and computational biology.

grants.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Applications accepted on a continuing basis. One fellowship awarded annually.
grants.amount: INR 1,00,000 per month plus up to INR 75,000/year for secretarial assistance, travel, and contingencies
grants.description: Two years of freedom to pursue original and creative work. Open to Indian citizens across sciences, humanities, and public life, including scholars in any discipline, writers, journalists, artists, and civil servants.

grants.name: BBSRC Bioinformatics and Biological Resources Fund (26BBR)
grants.funder: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), UK Research and Innovation
grants.deadlineNote: The 26BBR round closed 19 November 2026. Project lead must be at a UK research organisation eligible for BBSRC funding; India-based researchers may join as international project partners only.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 2 million full economic cost; BBSRC funds 80% up to GBP 1.6 million
grants.description: Supports community bioinformatics or biological resources serving UK bioscience, including databases, software, and biological materials. Useful route for Indian collaborators partnering with UK PIs.

grants.name: NQS Mission 2: Components, Systems, and Architectures
grants.funder: EPSRC and STFC, UK Research and Innovation
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 24 November 2026. Latest start date 31 May 2027. An eligible UK research organisation must lead. India-based researchers may participate as international project partners only.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 2.56 million full economic cost; EPSRC funds 80%
grants.description: Research on quantum-networking components, systems, and architectures, including nodes, routers, memories, repeaters, photonics, integration, security, and distributed capability. Part of the UK National Quantum Strategy. Useful route for Indian quantum groups partnering with UK PIs.

grants.name: UKRI Enabling AI Adoption across Science and Engineering
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 1 December 2026, 4:00pm UK time. Fixed start date 26 April 2027; an eligible UK research organisation must lead, and Indian researchers may join as project partners.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 250,000 full economic cost; UKRI funds 80%
grants.description: Exploratory collaborations between AI specialists and domain researchers addressing important scientific and engineering challenges. Useful route for Indian AI or domain-science groups partnering with UK PIs.

grants.name: IBSA Foundation Fellowships 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 31 January 2027. Applicants must be under 40 on that date. Permanent professors are ineligible.
grants.amount: EUR 32,000 per fellowship (seven fellowships)
grants.description: Seven early-career biomedical fellowships across dermatology, endocrinology, fertility and urology, orthopaedics and pain medicine, and healthy ageing. Open to applicants of any nationality holding a degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology, or bioengineering. Eligible categories: PhD students, PhD holders, postdoctoral researchers, and medical residents.

grants.name: AssisTech Foundation Student Innovation Challenge: collaborATe 2026
grants.deadlineNote: Applications closed on 30 October 2026. Listed on the Manthan-Utthan platform (sign-in required to view).
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Student innovation challenge for assistive technologies addressing accessibility and disability. Open to student teams developing hardware, software, or systems that improve quality of life for persons with disabilities.

grants.name: Temasek Foundation Green Future Innovation Challenge
grants.deadlineNote: Submissions close 4 February 2027; the Grand Finale is in Beijing in April 2027.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Challenge for green and sustainable innovation addressing climate, environmental, and ecological problems. Open to applicants worldwide. Delivered in partnership with regional institutions.

grants.name: The Liveability Challenge
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 12 February 2027.
grants.amount: Over SGD 5.5 million in grants, investment and development opportunities across the edition; SGD 1 million grant for the top Oceans solution
grants.description: Global search for solutions addressing urban liveability challenges including energy, food, water, decarbonisation, and the built environment. Finalists receive funding and support to deploy their solutions in Singapore and beyond.

grants.name: CAMPCO Development of All-Season Cocoa Varieties for the Belt
grants.funder: The Central Arecanut and Cocoa Marketing and Processing Co-operative Ltd (CAMPCO)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications closed on 6 November 2026. Listed on the Manthan-Utthan platform (sign-in required to view).
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Agricultural research call for developing suitable all-season cocoa varieties for the Indian cocoa belt. Open to researchers at Indian institutions working in plant breeding, crop science, and agricultural biotechnology.

grants.name: Rohini Nilekani Centre for Brain and Mind Seed Grants
grants.funder: Rohini Nilekani Centre for Brain and Mind, NCBS and NIMHANS
grants.deadlineNote: Ashoka's research office lists a 1 December 2026 deadline; the call is not yet posted on CBM's funding page. Applicants must be faculty at a DSIR-certified institution with at least 5 years of service remaining.
grants.amount: Up to INR 25 lakh
grants.description: Supports research into the biological basis of mental illness and improving diagnosis and clinical management. Open across disciplines as long as the proposal aligns with RN-CBM objectives. Prior experience in stem cells or neuroscience is not required; RN-CBM supports skills and training acquisition during the project.

grants.name: ANRS MIE Emergences PRFI 2026
grants.funder: ANRS Emerging Infectious Diseases (ANRS MIE), France
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 7 January 2027 at 23:59 Paris time. Projects must be co-led by a team in France and a team in a low- or lower-middle-income country; India qualifies as lower-middle-income.
grants.amount: See call details
grants.description: Collaborative research on emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases, especially viral haemorrhagic fevers, respiratory viruses, and arboviruses. Projects may span basic, translational, clinical, public-health, or humanities and social-science approaches.

grants.name: Sonar Research Grant Program
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. Applications accepted while quantities remain available.
grants.amount: In-kind access to SonarQube commercial licences (Cloud Enterprise and Advanced Security). Programme commitment totals USD 2.8M; per-award value not stated.
grants.description: In-kind SonarQube access for academic software-engineering research. Priority topics include code quality and developer productivity, technical debt, and AI-enabled remediation. Open to accredited universities and research institutions, including research leaders, professors, postdoctoral researchers, PhD candidates, and graduate researchers.

grants.name: Science Academies' Summer Research Fellowship Programme 2027
grants.funder: Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc), Indian National Science Academy (INSA) and National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI)
grants.deadlineNote: Online applications close 30 November 2026.
grants.amount: Monthly living stipend plus round-trip train fare
grants.duration: Two months during calendar year 2027, preferably in summer
grants.description: The three national science academies place students and college or university teachers in India with research guides at Indian institutions for a two-month project. Applicants must be studying or teaching at a recognised university or college in India; students need a teacher's recommendation.

grants.name: ICTS Summer Research Program
grants.deadlineNote: Applications due 15 December 2026, 5:00 PM IST; referee details due 31 December 2026.
grants.amount: Stipend and accommodation
grants.duration: About two months, typically mid-May to mid-July
grants.description: Summer research projects at ICTS Bengaluru with faculty in theoretical physics, mathematics, biology and related areas. Open to undergraduates in science, mathematics or engineering who have finished their second, third or fourth year, and to master's students and recent graduates; Indian and foreign nationals may apply.

grants.name: IISc Post-Doctoral Fellowship (IPDF)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications are reviewed at the 30 June and 31 December cut-offs, with decisions about six weeks later.
grants.amount: INR 80,000 per month plus HRA and INR 2 lakh per year research grant (INR 50,000 per month and no grant if selected before thesis defence)
grants.duration: One year, extendable by one year
grants.description: Institute postdoctoral fellowship for early-career researchers to work with an IISc faculty host in any department. Candidates need a PhD (or proof of thesis submission) and should preferably be under 32; Indian nationals, OCI holders and foreign nationals are eligible.

grants.name: IMSc Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.funder: The Institute of Mathematical Sciences (IMSc), Chennai
grants.deadlineNote: The latest Mathematics round closed on 15 November 2026. IMSc otherwise accepts postdoctoral applications year-round, with selection committees meeting two or three times a year.
grants.amount: INR 58,000 to 67,000 per month, plus INR 60,000 per year contingency, medical cover and housing or 30% HRA
grants.duration: One year, extendable by one more year
grants.description: Postdoctoral positions at IMSc in theoretical physics, mathematics, theoretical computer science and computational biology. Applicants must have submitted their PhD thesis by the time of appointment; the defence need not be complete.

grants.name: RRI Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline listed; apply through the RRI careers portal.
grants.amount: INR 58,000 to 67,000 per month plus HRA (INR 48,000 until PhD requirements are met)
grants.description: Postdoctoral positions at RRI in astronomy and astrophysics, light and matter physics, soft condensed matter and theoretical physics, with no teaching duties. Applicants submit a CV, publication list and research statements through the institute portal; RRI also encourages applicants to seek ANRF N-PDF support.

grants.name: NBHM Doctoral and Master's Scholarships
grants.funder: National Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM), Department of Atomic Energy
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 application dates not yet announced; the written test is tentatively scheduled for 30 January 2027. In the 2026 cycle the portal opened on 3 December 2025 and closed on 25 December 2025, so a December 2026 window is likely.
grants.amount: Doctoral stipend INR 37,000 per month for the first two years (2026 rates), rising thereafter
grants.duration: Duration of the PhD or master's programme
grants.description: National scholarships for PhD and master's study in mathematics at Indian institutions, selected by written test and interview. Open to students in India planning doctoral or master's work in mathematics; doctoral scholars work under an approved guide at an institution of their choice.

grants.name: IUCAA Associateship Programme
grants.funder: Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA), Pune
grants.deadlineNote: The call for the 2026-2029 associateships closed on 1 May 2026. The call is annual; the next one is expected around March to May 2027.
grants.amount: Travel and local living expenses for visits to IUCAA
grants.description: Lets faculty at Indian universities and postgraduate college departments make short and long visits to IUCAA to build research in astronomy and astrophysics. Associates keep their duties at their parent institution.

grants.name: IGSTC Industrial Fellowships
grants.funder: Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC), DST and BMBF
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 call closed (results expected around October 2026); next call not yet announced.
grants.amount: EUR 1,500 per month (PhD) or EUR 2,500 per month (postdoc), plus travel, visa and medical insurance
grants.duration: Up to 6 months (PhD) or up to 12 months (postdoc)
grants.description: Places Indian PhD students and fresh PhDs in German industry or industrial research organisations for applied research. PhD students must have completed one year of a PhD in India and be 30 or younger; postdocs must be 35 or younger and within three years of a PhD from an Indian institution. Applicants arrange a German industrial host.

grants.name: Paired Early Career Fellowship in Applied Research (PECFAR)
grants.funder: Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC), DST and BMBF
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 call closed (results expected around October 2026); next call not yet announced.
grants.amount: One-time grant covering travel, accommodation and fellowship
grants.description: Funds a pair of early-career researchers, one Indian and one German, to make short visits to each other's country to build an applied STEM collaboration. The pair submits a joint proposal with acceptance letters from both host institutions.

grants.name: S.N. Bose Scholars Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; next dates not yet posted.
grants.amount: Stipend, health insurance and airfare
grants.description: Sends Indian bachelor's and master's students to US universities for summer research internships. Eligible fields are atmospheric and earth sciences, chemical sciences, engineering sciences, mathematical and computational sciences, and physical sciences; biology students apply to the Khorana Program instead.

grants.name: Khorana Program for Scholars
grants.funder: Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF) and Department of Biotechnology (DBT)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call, previously due in early October; next dates not yet posted.
grants.amount: Round-trip airfare, stipend and health insurance
grants.duration: 10 to 12 weeks, mid-May to end of July
grants.description: Summer research internships at US institutions for Indian students in biotechnology and allied fields. Applicants must be in a pre-final year of a B.Tech, M.Tech, B.Sc, M.Sc, MBBS or similar degree with a CGPA of 8.0 or higher (65% for MBBS); first-year, final-year and PhD students are not eligible.

grants.name: ICTP Associates Programme (Junior, Regular, Senior)
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2028 Associates close 31 January 2027.
grants.region: Italy (Trieste), for scientists in developing countries
grants.amount: Travel fares for visits (Junior and Regular); fixed allocation for living and travel (Senior)
grants.description: Gives PhD scientists working in developing countries, including India, repeated research visits to ICTP. Junior Associates are up to 35, Regular 36 to 45, and Senior 46 to 65; Junior and Regular Associates make three visits of 30 to 60 days each.

grants.name: ICTP Postdoctoral Positions in High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics 2027
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: Apply via AcademicJobsOnline (job 33129) by 22 November 2026 for full consideration.
grants.amount: Salaried postdoctoral position
grants.description: Postdoctoral positions in the ICTP HECAP section, separate from the ICTP mathematics postdocs already listed. The listing sets no nationality restriction, so recent PhDs from India can apply with a CV, research statement, publication list and three letters.

grants.name: ICTP Postgraduate Diploma Programme
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027-28 programme (starting 1 September 2027) close 28 February 2027.
grants.amount: Tuition-free; about 10 scholarships per field for students from developing countries cover travel and living costs
grants.description: A one-year pre-PhD programme in condensed matter physics, high energy physics, mathematics, earth system physics or quantitative life sciences. Applicants should generally be under 28 with an MSc-equivalent degree and come from a UN, UNESCO or IAEA member country, which includes India.

grants.name: EMBO Global Investigator Network
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline 1 May, 14:00 CEST. Open to group leaders in Chile, India, Japan, Singapore and Taiwan within six years of starting their lab.
grants.amount: Funding for networking and travel, plus training, mentoring and EMBO events
grants.description: Supports group leaders in the life sciences within their first six years of running a lab in one of the listed countries. India-based PIs are eligible and join the network of EMBO Young Investigators and Global Investigators.

grants.name: EMBL International PhD Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Two recruitment rounds a year; the next round is expected to open toward the end of January.
grants.amount: PhD position at EMBL
grants.description: PhD positions at EMBL sites in molecular biology, computational biology and related areas. Recruitment is international, with current students from 48 nationalities, so graduates from India can apply.

grants.name: ERC Synergy Grant
grants.deadlineNote: ERC-2027-SyG opens 17 February 2027 and closes 11 May 2027.
grants.region: EU and associated countries; one PI may be outside
grants.amount: Up to EUR 10 million, plus up to EUR 4 million for start-up, equipment or major costs
grants.description: Funds a group of two to four PIs working jointly on an ambitious research problem. One PI in the group may be hosted by an institution outside the EU and associated countries, so an India-based researcher can be a funded co-PI alongside European partners.

grants.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (Research Fellowship and PhD)
grants.funder: Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS), Swiss State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI)
grants.deadlineNote: The listed deadline of 10 November 2026 has passed; next cycle not yet announced.
grants.amount: CHF 2,450 per month
grants.duration: Research fellowship 6 to 12 months; PhD 12 months renewable up to 36 months, from 1 September 2027
grants.description: Swiss Government scholarships for research at Swiss universities, ETH Zurich, EPFL and federal research institutes, in any discipline. Indian applicants may apply for a one-year research fellowship during doctoral studies or a full PhD scholarship, with a Swiss supervisor's support and an age limit of 35.

grants.name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
grants.funder: Gates Cambridge Trust, University of Cambridge
grants.deadlineNote: For non-US applicants, the deadline is 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on the course funding deadline in the Cambridge course directory.
grants.amount: Scholarship for postgraduate study; coverage set out by Gates Cambridge
grants.duration: PhD (up to 4 years) or one-year postgraduate course
grants.description: Postgraduate scholarships at the University of Cambridge for citizens of any country outside the UK, including India, across all subjects including the sciences. Fundable courses are the PhD, the MLitt and one-year postgraduate courses.

grants.name: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2026 have closed. The 2027 call is not yet posted; the 2026 call ran from mid-February to 31 March 2026.
grants.region: Top universities in the US, UK and Europe (for Indian residents)
grants.amount: Up to USD 120,000 covering tuition, living costs, travel, visa and health
grants.description: Scholarships for Indian passport holders resident in India to pursue master's or PhD study at leading overseas universities. Mathematics, the sciences and environment are eligible; computer science, engineering (except at Imperial College London) and medicine are excluded.

grants.name: Max Planck Partner Groups
grants.deadlineNote: No fixed call; proposed by the Max Planck Institute where the researcher worked.
grants.amount: MPG funding for the partner group
grants.description: Supports early-career researchers who, after a stay at a Max Planck Institute, set up a group at a partner institution, preferably in their home country, keeping links with the Max Planck host. India-based researchers with a recent Max Planck stay are eligible; MPG lists a regional contact for India.

grants.name: CERN Doctoral Studentship Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Positions are posted on the CERN careers site through the year; no position open at the time of checking.
grants.amount: CHF 3,907 per month net allowance
grants.description: Lets PhD students enrolled at a university do their doctoral research at CERN in physics, engineering or computing. Applicants must be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State; India is an Associate Member State, so Indian PhD students are eligible.

grants.name: ICGEB Arturo Falaschi PhD, Postdoctoral and SMART Fellowships
grants.funder: International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB)
grants.deadlineNote: Next call opens January 2027 with a final deadline of 31 March 2027. A second call usually runs in the second half of the year.
grants.region: ICGEB Member States (includes India); research at ICGEB Trieste, New Delhi or Cape Town
grants.amount: Monthly stipend plus travel and health insurance (amount varies by fellowship type)
grants.duration: Short-term (up to 12 months) to long-term (PhD and postdoctoral, about 2 years)
grants.description: Pre-doctoral and postdoctoral fellowships for nationals of ICGEB Member States to do life-science research at ICGEB laboratories, plus SMART fellowships for South-South mobility. India is an ICGEB Member State and hosts the New Delhi component, so Indian nationals can apply.

grants.name: TDR Implementation Research Leadership Fellowship Programme for Public Health Impact
grants.funder: WHO Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR), hosted at Universitas Gadjah Mada
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. The 2026/2027 call closed on 13 February 2026 (extended from 30 January 2026). No 2027/2028 call has been announced yet; the previous call was issued in December 2025.
grants.region: Nationals and residents of LMICs in the WHO South-East Asia, Western Pacific and Eastern Mediterranean Regions (includes India)
grants.amount: Fully funded in-person fellowship
grants.description: Leadership training in implementation research for researchers and public health practitioners under 40, focused on infectious diseases of poverty, antimicrobial resistance, epidemics and climate effects on health. The 2026/2027 call was open to LMICs in the WHO South-East Asia Region, which includes India; eligible regions vary by cycle.

grants.name: BBRF Young Investigator Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 window ran 4 February to 4 March 2026. The 2027 dates are not yet announced.
grants.region: Worldwide; no citizenship or location restriction
grants.amount: Up to USD 35,000 per year (USD 70,000 total)
grants.description: Supports early-career researchers in psychiatry and brain and behaviour research who hold a doctoral degree and a research position. Applicants may be based anywhere in the world, so researchers at Indian institutions can apply.

grants.name: BrightFocus Macular Degeneration Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; FY27 letters of intent were due 30 July 2026 and invited full proposals are due 10 December 2026. The next LOI window is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Postdoctoral USD 200,000; New Investigator up to USD 450,000; Standard up to USD 300,000
grants.description: Funds research on the causes and treatment of age-related macular degeneration through postdoctoral, new investigator and standard awards. BrightFocus funds both US and international researchers, so applicants at Indian institutions can apply.

grants.name: BrightFocus National Glaucoma Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; the FY27 proposal window closed 24 September 2026. The next window is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Postdoctoral up to USD 125,000; Standard up to USD 150,000
grants.description: Funds research on the causes, prevention and treatment of glaucoma through standard and postdoctoral awards. The programme accepts US and international researchers, so applicants at Indian institutions can apply.

grants.name: Thrasher Research Fund Early Career Award
grants.deadlineNote: Two concept-paper cycles in 2027: spring due 16 March 2027 and fall due 30 August 2027, both at noon Mountain Time.
grants.region: Worldwide; institutions inside and outside the US
grants.amount: Up to USD 25,000 direct costs plus 7% indirect
grants.description: Small grants for early-career physicians and postdocs doing paediatric health research, with a mentor. There are no citizenship restrictions and institutions outside the US are eligible, so researchers in India can apply.

grants.name: Worldwide Cancer Research Grant Round
grants.deadlineNote: One grant round a year; the next round is in 2027 (the 2026 round closed 2 April 2026). Dates are not yet announced.
grants.region: Worldwide; PI at a not-for-profit research institution
grants.amount: Project grant (amount set in the annual handbook)
grants.description: Funds discovery research on any cancer type at not-for-profit institutions anywhere in the world. Principal investigators based in India can apply.

grants.name: Cancer Grand Challenges
grants.funder: Cancer Research UK and the National Cancer Institute (US)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the current gastroesophageal cancer challenge close 24 November 2026. No further round is announced.
grants.region: International teams; no more than 70% of activity in one country
grants.amount: Up to USD 34 million per team
grants.description: Funds international, interdisciplinary teams to tackle defined challenges in cancer research. Teams need not be UK or US led, so researchers in India can lead or join a team, provided no single country accounts for more than 70% of the work.

grants.name: CRI Irvington Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Deadlines on 1 March and 1 September each year, 11:59 pm US Eastern.
grants.amount: Stipend USD 74,000 to 78,000 per year plus USD 5,000 annual allowance
grants.description: Supports postdoctoral research in immunology and cancer immunology. The fellowship can be held in the US or abroad at a non-profit institution with no citizenship restrictions, so it can be held at an Indian institution.

grants.name: CRI Immuno-Informatics Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Deadlines on 1 March and 1 September each year, 11:59 pm US Eastern.
grants.amount: Stipend USD 74,000 to 78,000 per year plus USD 5,000 annual allowance
grants.description: Supports early-career scientists building joint expertise in immunology and data science for cancer immunotherapy. The fellowship can be held in the US or abroad at a non-profit institution with no citizenship restrictions, so it can be held in India.

grants.name: IBRO Rising Stars Awards
grants.deadlineNote: Annual window; the 2026 window ran 15 March to 15 April 2026 and the next is expected around the same time in 2027.
grants.region: IBRO regions including Asia-Pacific (India is in the APRC region)
grants.amount: Up to USD 10,000 for Asia-Pacific applicants
grants.description: Start-up grants for neuroscientists setting up their first independent laboratory. India falls in IBRO's Asia-Pacific region; priority goes to researchers who trained abroad and have returned to a faculty post in their home country.

grants.name: IBRO Parenthood Grants
grants.deadlineNote: The next call opens in February 2027; the 2026 window was 1 July to 15 August.
grants.amount: Up to USD 2,000 for Asia-Pacific applicants
grants.description: Supports early-career neuroscience principal investigators (up to 7 years as PI) who are expecting or have recently welcomed a child, to keep their lab running. The programme is open to international applicants, and India is in IBRO's Asia-Pacific region.

grants.name: Jane Coffin Childs Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.funder: Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research
grants.deadlineNote: Applications opened 1 October 2026 and close 1 February 2027 at 3:00 pm US Eastern.
grants.region: Any citizenship; non-US citizens must hold the fellowship at a US institution
grants.amount: Stipend and research allowance (see Terms of the Award)
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships in the basic medical and biological sciences related to cancer. Citizens of any country may apply, but non-US citizens, including Indian PhD graduates, must take up the fellowship in a US laboratory.

grants.name: Helen Hay Whitney Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline in mid-June (15 June in 2026). The 2027 date is not yet posted.
grants.region: Any citizenship; foreign citizens only for research in US laboratories
grants.amount: Stipend USD 73,000 to 77,000 per year plus USD 1,500 research allowance and child allowance
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships in the biomedical sciences for early-stage postdocs. Indian citizens can apply but must hold the fellowship in a US laboratory.

grants.name: Life Sciences Research Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; the portal opens 15 August and applications close 1 October (the 2026-27 deadline has passed).
grants.region: Any citizenship; non-US citizens must work in a US laboratory
grants.amount: USD 85,000 per year (USD 79,000 salary plus USD 6,000 research allowance)
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships across the life sciences, sponsored by companies, foundations and HHMI. Indian citizens can apply but must hold the award in a US laboratory.

grants.name: Boehringer Ingelheim Fonds PhD Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Three deadlines a year: 1 February, 1 June and 1 October. The portal opens about one month before each deadline.
grants.region: European citizens anywhere, or non-European citizens doing their PhD in Europe
grants.amount: Monthly stipend (basic EUR 1,650 plus country premium) and travel allowances
grants.duration: 24 months, extendable by up to 18 months
grants.description: Fellowships for PhD students doing experimental basic biomedical research. Indian nationals are eligible if their PhD project is carried out in Europe, and must apply near the start of the PhD.

grants.name: EMBL EIPOD-LinC Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET; referee letters by 2 February.
grants.region: All nationalities; hosted at EMBL with a partner lab in an EMBL Member State
grants.amount: Fully funded postdoctoral fellowship
grants.description: Interdisciplinary postdoctoral fellowships studying life in context, co-supervised by EMBL and a Member State partner laboratory. The programme is open to researchers of all nationalities with up to eight years post-PhD, so researchers in India can apply.

grants.name: NIHR Global Advanced Fellowships
grants.funder: National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), UK
grants.deadlineNote: Opens once a year in April; the Cohort 2 round ran 14 April to 30 June 2026. The 2027 dates are not yet announced.
grants.region: Researchers employed at LMIC institutions in sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia (includes India), or UK institutions
grants.amount: Up to GBP 750,000
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships for researchers who are not yet independent, for global health research that primarily benefits ODA-eligible countries. Applicants employed at Indian universities or research institutes are eligible and LMIC-based applicants receive strategic priority.

grants.name: Global Brain and Nervous System Disorders Research Across the Lifespan (R21 Exploratory Grants)
grants.funder: Fogarty International Center, NIH (with NINDS, NIMH, NIA, NICHD and other institutes)
grants.deadlineNote: Forecast opportunity PAR-26-144. The estimated due date of 15 November 2026 has passed and the notice is still listed as forecast, not posted; check Grants.gov for the final dates.
grants.region: US institutions and LMIC institutions (includes India); each application needs a US and an LMIC partner
grants.amount: Not stated in the forecast
grants.duration: R21 exploratory grant (typically up to 2 years)
grants.description: Supports collaborative research on brain and nervous system disorders relevant to low- and middle-income countries across the lifespan. Institutions in India, as a lower-middle-income country, can apply as the LMIC partner organisation.

grants.name: CIPHER Research Grant Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026/2027 letter-of-intent deadline was 30 September 2026. The next call is not yet announced.
grants.region: Nationals of low- and middle-income countries (includes India)
grants.amount: Up to USD 140,000
grants.description: Grants for early-stage investigators (terminal degree within 10 years) leading a project as principal investigator for the first time, on paediatric and adolescent HIV. Applicants need a passport from an LMIC, so Indian nationals are eligible.

grants.name: Keystone Symposia Global Health Awards
grants.funder: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology
grants.deadlineNote: Per meeting. Upcoming in-person Global Health Award deadlines: Plant and Microbe Engineering for Sustainability (May 2027) 1 December 2026; Vaccinology and Ending HIV (16-19 May 2027) 15 December 2026; Progress in Antibiotic Discovery and Development (June 2027) 19 January 2027. Open to students, fellows, scientists and clinicians from and based in LMICs (India eligible).
grants.region: Scientists from and living or working in low- and middle-income countries (includes India)
grants.amount: Travel award covers registration, lodging and airfare; virtual registration also offered
grants.description: Travel awards and virtual registration for students, fellows, scientists and clinicians from LMICs to attend Keystone Symposia meetings. Researchers based in India are eligible.

grants.name: IUBMB Wood-Whelan Research Fellowships
grants.funder: International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB)
grants.deadlineNote: Two deadlines a year: 15 March (travel July to December) and 15 September (travel January to June).
grants.region: Members of IUBMB adhering societies; India's adhering body is INSA, representing the Society of Biological Chemists (India)
grants.amount: Up to USD 7,000 for travel and living costs
grants.description: Short research visits for PhD students and researchers within five years of the PhD to work in another laboratory. Indian applicants are eligible through membership of the Society of Biological Chemists (India).

grants.name: ADDF Drug Development, Biomarker and Prevention RFPs
grants.deadlineNote: Letters of intent for the current round have closed; invited full proposals are due 7 December 2026. Future rounds are not yet dated.
grants.region: Academic centres and biotech companies worldwide
grants.amount: Programme-related investment (amount by project)
grants.description: Funds drug development, neuroimaging and CSF biomarker, and prevention studies for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. ADDF funds academic centres and biotechs around the world, so Indian institutions can apply.

grants.name: CEPI Calls for Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Calls open and close throughout the year on specific vaccine and preparedness topics; check the page for the current list.
grants.region: Worldwide; CEPI encourages applicants from the Global South
grants.amount: Varies by call
grants.description: Funds vaccine development and epidemic preparedness research through topic-specific calls. CEPI invites innovators worldwide and is particularly interested in developers and researchers in the Global South, including India.

grants.name: Eppendorf and Science Prize for Neurobiology
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline of 15 June in recent years; the 2027 date is not yet posted.
grants.amount: USD 25,000 grand prize
grants.description: Prize for an early-career neurobiologist aged 35 or under with an MD or PhD from the last 10 years, judged on a 1,000-word essay about their recent research. The prize is open worldwide, so researchers in India can enter.

grants.name: CURE Epilepsy Research Grants (CURE Epilepsy Award, Catalyst Award)
grants.funder: CURE Epilepsy (Citizens United for Research in Epilepsy)
grants.deadlineNote: Letters of intent are usually due in January (Award) and June (Catalyst and partnership awards). 2027 dates are not yet posted.
grants.amount: Varies by mechanism
grants.description: Funds research toward cures for epilepsy through several award mechanisms. International applicants are welcome, so researchers at Indian institutions can apply; postdoctoral fellows cannot apply for the main award.

grants.name: Lady Tata Memorial Trust International Awards for Research in Leukaemia
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026-27 window ran 1 April to 31 May 2026. The 2027-28 dates are not yet announced.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 36,000
grants.description: Personal support awards for research on the treatment, epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunology and genetics of leukaemia, for researchers usually within six years of the PhD. Awards are open to investigators of any nationality, with priority to those moving to another centre.

grants.name: Lady Tata Memorial Trust Indian Awards (Junior Scholarship and Post-Doctoral Fellowship)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; applications for the 2026-27 year closed in February 2026. The next dates are not yet announced.
grants.region: Scholars working at Indian universities and institutes
grants.amount: Fellowship stipend (amount set by the Trust)
grants.duration: Junior Scholarship 5 years; Post-Doctoral Fellowship 2 years
grants.description: Scholarships for research in India on diseases of the blood, with special reference to leukaemia. The Junior Scholarship supports PhD study and the Post-Doctoral Fellowship supports early postdoctoral work at Indian institutions.

grants.name: Sun Pharma Science Foundation Research Fellowships and Science Scholar Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual nominations; the 2026 window ran 15 May to 15 July 2026 (Clinical Research Fellowship 15 July to 15 September). 2027 dates are not yet announced.
grants.region: Indian scientists (including non-resident Indians with an Indian passport for Research Fellowships)
grants.amount: Research Fellowships INR 5 lakh each with trophy and citation
grants.description: Nominated awards for original research in medical and pharmaceutical sciences by Indian scientists, plus Science Scholar Fellowships for young researchers under 30 and a Clinical Research Fellowship for early-career clinicians in India. Nominations come from heads of institutions.

grants.name: Alzheimer's Association International Research Grant Program
grants.deadlineNote: Each programme has its own dates. Upcoming: ZENITH Fellows Award letter of intent 1 December 2026 (full application 30 March 2027); Bridge Funding letters of intent 29 January and 30 April 2027. ISTAART conference grants are reviewed on a rolling basis until 30 June 2027. Some programmes are restricted by region.
grants.region: Most programmes open to US and international researchers
grants.amount: Varies by programme
grants.description: Funds Alzheimer's and dementia research at all career stages through a set of programmes with their own calls. Most grants are open to international researchers, so applicants in India can apply to programmes without a regional restriction.

grants.name: ICGEB Collaborative Research Programme (CRP) Research Grants
grants.funder: International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB)
grants.deadlineNote: The next call opens at the beginning of 2027 with a submission deadline of 30 April 2027. Applications need endorsement by the national Liaison Officer.
grants.region: PIs at universities or research institutes in ICGEB Member States (includes India; excludes Italy)
grants.amount: Up to EUR 25,000 per year
grants.description: Research grants for projects on scientific problems of relevance to the host country in life sciences and biotechnology, including an Early Career Return Grant track. Principal investigators at Indian universities and institutes are eligible since India is an ICGEB Member State.

grants.name: ERS Short-Term Research Training Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: The ERS fellowship page lists the next Short-Term Research Training Fellowship deadline as 1 April 2027 (call currently closed).
grants.region: ERS members of all nationalities, based in Europe or overseas
grants.amount: Monthly allowance for the training stay
grants.duration: Short-term visit (set in the call guidance)
grants.description: Short research visits to a host institution for early-career respiratory scientists and clinicians. The programme is open to ERS members of all nationalities based in Europe or overseas, so members in India can apply.

grants.name: ISN Fellowship Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual window; the 2026 window ran 1 July to 16 October 2026. The 2027 dates are not yet posted.
grants.region: ISN members living and working in low- and middle-income countries (includes India)
grants.amount: Training stipend and travel (set in programme guidelines)
grants.description: Hands-on nephrology training at a host centre for young doctors from LMICs, who then return home to apply the skills. Applicants must be ISN members working in a World Bank low- or middle-income country, which includes India.

grants.name: ASH Global Research Award
grants.deadlineNote: Letters of intent for the 2027 cycle closed 31 August 2026. The next LOI window is expected to open in March 2027.
grants.region: ASH members based outside the US and Canada
grants.amount: Up to USD 100,000 (one year) or USD 150,000 (longer projects)
grants.description: Research awards for haematology researchers based outside the US and Canada, with a local mentor and a global mentor. Researchers in India who are ASH members are eligible.

grants.name: Science and SciLifeLab Prize for Young Scientists
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline in mid-year (15 July in 2026). The 2027 call is not yet posted.
grants.amount: USD 30,000 grand prize; USD 10,000 for each category winner
grants.description: Essay prize for recent PhD graduates in cell and molecular biology, genomics and systems biology, ecology and environment, and molecular medicine, based on their thesis work. The prize is open to researchers from all countries, including PhD graduates from Indian institutions.

grants.name: Grass Fellowship
grants.funder: Grass Foundation (at the Marine Biological Laboratory, Woods Hole)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027 are due 1 December 2026; recommendation letters by 15 December 2026.
grants.region: International applicants accepted (valid US visa required for the fellowship)
grants.amount: Funded summer research residency
grants.description: Summer residency at the MBL in Woods Hole for late-stage PhD and MD students, postdocs and early faculty to run an independent neuroscience project. International fellows are accepted if they hold a valid visa, so researchers from India can apply.

grants.name: Pratiksha Trust EMSTAR (Extra-Mural Support for Transformational Aging Brain Research)
grants.funder: Pratiksha Trust (coordinated by the Centre for Brain Research, IISc)
grants.deadlineNote: Calls are annual and announced on the programme page; no current deadline is posted.
grants.region: Lead investigators with salaried posts at eligible Indian institutions
grants.amount: Up to INR 5 crore
grants.description: Large grants for research on dementia and the aging brain, including cohort studies, AI and data science, the gut microbiome and neuroimmunology. The lead investigator must hold a post at an Indian institution; co-investigators can be abroad.

grants.name: UICC Technical Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 call ran 3 April to 4 June 2026. UICC says 2027 dates will be published soon.
grants.region: Cancer professionals worldwide (no regional restriction for this scheme)
grants.amount: Living costs and economy travel, calculated from UICC scales
grants.description: Short visits to a host institution abroad for cancer professionals with at least a Master's degree (or medical or nursing equivalent) and five years of experience in cancer. UICC fellowships support applicants from all over the world, so professionals in India can apply; PhD and medical students are not eligible.

grants.name: TCS Research Scholar Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle through invited institutes; the 2026 cycle closed 16 January 2026. Next call not yet posted.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend (about Rs 91,000 in years 1-2, rising in years 3-4) plus research contingency; package stated by TCS as over Rs 47 lakh per scholar
grants.description: PhD fellowship for full-time computer science and related PhD scholars at invited Indian institutes, with mentoring from TCS Research. Applications go through the scholar's institute, not directly to TCS. Open only to scholars registered at Indian institutions.

grants.name: AI2050 Fellowships (Early Career and Senior)
grants.deadlineNote: Closed nominations; there is no open application.
grants.amount: Early Career: up to USD 300,000
grants.description: Fellowships for researchers working on hard problems in making AI beneficial to society, awarded to early-career and senior researchers. Selection is by closed nomination only. Fellows are drawn from around the world, and past cohorts include researchers at Indian institutions.

grants.name: MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars)
grants.deadlineNote: Fellow applications for the Winter 2027 cohort are closed; later fellow cohorts not yet announced.
grants.region: Global (in person in Berkeley or London)
grants.amount: USD 1,250 per week stipend, USD 2,000 per week compute, housing, meals, travel and J1 visa covered if needed
grants.duration: 12 weeks, with a funded 6-12 month extension available
grants.description: Mentored research programme in AI alignment, interpretability, security and governance, held in Berkeley and London. Travel and visa costs are covered, so applicants based in India can take part in person.

grants.name: ACM India Anveshan Setu Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: 2026-27 cycle announced for visits between November 2026 and March 2027; check the official page for the application date.
grants.amount: Stipend for travel and living costs during the visit (reported as up to Rs 60,000 for 2026-27)
grants.description: Funds PhD students in computer science and IT at Indian institutions to spend a research visit with a host faculty member at another Indian institution. Up to about 50 students are supported per cycle. Open only to PhD students in India who have not yet submitted their thesis.

grants.name: Microsoft Research Asia StarTrack Scholars Program
grants.deadlineNote: The last cycle opened 15 October 2025 and closed 15 December 2025, with visits from March 2026 to January 2027; next cycle dates are not yet posted.
grants.amount: Funded three-month research visit with compute, tools and data support
grants.description: Invites young faculty worldwide, within 7 years of the PhD, for a full-time three-month research visit to Microsoft Research Asia. Applicants must be at a university that collaborates with Microsoft Research and need recommendation letters. Faculty at Indian institutions are eligible.

grants.name: ACM SIGHPC Computational and Data Science Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations open 15 March 2027 and close 30 April 2027.
grants.amount: USD 20,000 per year, adjusted by country of degree
grants.description: Fellowships for graduate students in computational or data science who are women or from groups underrepresented in computing in their country, with preference for disciplines other than computer science. Faculty advisors nominate. Open to students at institutions anywhere in the world, including India.

grants.name: ICTP-IMU Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries
grants.deadlineNote: Call listed as to be announced; past deadlines fell between February and March.
grants.description: Prize for a mathematician under 45 from a developing country who has done outstanding research in a developing country, in any branch of the mathematical sciences. Nominations are made online. Researchers based in India are eligible.

grants.name: ELLIS PhD Program
grants.funder: European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELLIS)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 call (for 2027 starts) closed 31 October 2026. The central application portal usually opens each October.
grants.amount: Funded PhD positions at participating institutions (terms set by the host)
grants.duration: Length of the PhD, including a 6-month exchange
grants.description: Central recruiting for machine learning PhD positions at 50 to 100 European institutions, with dual supervision across two countries and a research exchange. One application covers many labs. Applicants from India apply through the central portal.

grants.name: Institut Mittag-Leffler Junior Fellowships
grants.funder: Institut Mittag-Leffler, Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
grants.deadlineNote: The call for the spring 2028 programme on subelliptic and magnetic operators closed on 15 November 2026. No other junior fellowship call is open; calls are posted per semester programme.
grants.amount: Monthly grant, free accommodation and one return trip
grants.description: Fellowships for advanced graduate students and postdocs within 5 years of the PhD to join a semester programme in mathematics in Stockholm. Research interests must match the programme theme. Travel for one return trip is covered, so applicants from India can take part.

grants.name: TPU Research Cloud (TRC)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; submit an expression of interest.
grants.amount: Free access to a cluster of over 1,000 Cloud TPU devices
grants.description: Gives machine learning researchers free Cloud TPU access in exchange for sharing results publicly and giving feedback to Google. Researchers apply through an expression-of-interest form. No country restriction is stated, and researchers in India can apply.

grants.name: Gemini Academic Program
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications reviewed monthly.
grants.region: Global (Gemini API supported regions, including India)
grants.amount: Gemini API credits and higher rate limits
grants.description: Provides Gemini API credits to academic researchers, with interest in evaluations, benchmarks and AI for scientific discovery. Applicants must be affiliated with an academic institution in a supported country. India is on the list of supported regions.

grants.name: Anthropic External Researcher Access Program
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications reviewed on the first Monday of each month.
grants.amount: USD 1,000 in API credits (more in rare cases)
grants.description: Free Claude API credits for researchers working on AI safety and alignment topics. Research groups submit one application for a shared organisation account. Available in countries where Claude is offered, which includes India.

grants.name: Lambda Research Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; no closing date listed.
grants.amount: Up to USD 5,000 in GPU cloud credits
grants.description: Cloud GPU credits for AI researchers, with some projects featured by Lambda. Applications go through an online form. No country restriction is stated.

grants.name: Cisco Research Open RFPs (Research Gifts)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; proposals reviewed as received.
grants.amount: Not stated on the official page
grants.description: Research gifts on open topics including generative AI, LLM agents, AI security, post-quantum cryptography, quantum networking and networking systems. The PI must be full-time faculty or research staff; non-US institutions must show non-profit equivalency, so Indian universities can apply.

grants.name: Unitary Foundation Microgrants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling.
grants.amount: Small grants (amount not stated on the page)
grants.description: Small grants for open-source quantum computing software, education materials and related projects, with a short form and video application. No institutional affiliation is required. Grants have gone to recipients in more than 31 countries.

grants.name: IMS Hannan Graduate Student and New Researcher Travel Awards
grants.deadlineNote: Both awards close 1 February 2027.
grants.amount: Typically USD 400 to 1,000
grants.description: Travel funding to present at an IMS-sponsored or co-sponsored meeting, for graduate students (Hannan award, IMS members) and researchers within 5 years of the PhD (New Researcher award). IMS membership is international, so statisticians in India can apply.

grants.name: IMU-Simons Research Fellowship Program
grants.funder: International Mathematical Union (CDC) and Simons Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: 15 January 2027 call is for visits starting 1 June 2027 to 1 June 2028; the page calls it the programme's last call.
grants.description: Funds research visits by mathematics faculty with a PhD who work in developing countries to institutions abroad. Applicants need a host contact and a research plan. India is listed as a Priority 2 developing country, so faculty in India are eligible.

grants.name: Abel Visiting Scholar Program for Graduate Students
