grants.funder: International Mathematical Union (CDC) and Niels Henrik Abel Board
grants.deadlineNote: Application system opens 15 November 2026; deadline 1 June 2027 for visits between February and December 2028.
grants.amount: Up to USD 5,000
grants.description: Funds a one-month research visit abroad for mathematics PhD students under 35 in developing countries who have completed at least 24 months of the PhD. Conference attendance alone does not qualify. Students in India are eligible.

grants.name: IMU Graduate Research Assistantships in Developing Countries (GRAID)
grants.deadlineNote: Online form expected to open early 2027.
grants.amount: Up to USD 3,500 per year per team
grants.description: Supports emerging mathematics research groups in developing countries to fund graduate research assistants. The applicant is a mathematics professor leading a group with an active international partner. India is a Priority 2 country, so groups in India can apply.

grants.name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 18 January to 30 April 2027 cohort in London have closed; the next round is not yet announced.
grants.amount: GBP 15,000 (GBP 18,000 senior) plus GBP 1,800 per month housing and travel
grants.description: Full-time mentored AI safety research fellowship at the London Initiative for Safe AI. Visa sponsorship may be available through a partner, and travel to London is covered. Applicants from India can apply.

grants.name: ERA:AI Fellowship (Cambridge)
grants.deadlineNote: Winter 2027 applications closed; next round not yet dated.
grants.amount: Stipend, compute budget, meals, transport and visa costs
grants.description: Research fellowship in technical AI safety and AI governance where fellows lead a project with mentor support. ERA covers transport and visas and welcomes applicants from around the world, including India.

grants.name: LASR Labs AI Safety Research Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Next cohort runs June to September 2027; application dates not yet posted.
grants.amount: GBP 15,000 stipend plus food, office space and travel
grants.description: Full-time programme in which teams of three or four take an AI safety research project from proposal to publication under a supervisor. Runs three times a year. The page states no nationality restriction; visa matters should be checked with LASR.

grants.name: MBZUAI Graduate Admissions and Scholarships
grants.funder: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)
grants.deadlineNote: Fall 2027 intake; final deadline 15 December 2026, 5 p.m. GST.
grants.amount: Funding depends on programme and assistantship; PhD students supported in the first year
grants.description: Graduate admissions for MSc and PhD programmes in AI fields at MBZUAI in Abu Dhabi, with funding tied to programme, standing and assistantships. Open to international applicants, including students from India.

grants.name: Max Planck Institute for Mathematics Guest Program and Postdoc Positions
grants.funder: Max Planck Institute for Mathematics, Bonn
grants.deadlineNote: The selection committee meets twice a year (summer and fall). The next application deadline is 4 June 2027; both recommendation letters must be uploaded by then.
grants.amount: Funded visits and postdoc positions (terms not stated on the page)
grants.duration: Weeks to several months (guests); up to 2 years (postdocs)
grants.description: Hosts about 700 visiting mathematicians a year, plus postdocs with a mentor. Applications need two recommendation letters. Open to mathematicians worldwide, including India.

grants.name: AAAI-27 Student Scholar and Volunteer Program
grants.funder: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
grants.deadlineNote: Application opens 30 November 2026 and closes 4 December 2026, 11:59 PM ET.
grants.amount: Partial travel support; limited free registration for volunteers
grants.description: Partial travel support for full-time students who are AAAI members and have submitted a paper, with priority for accepted papers. Students at universities anywhere, including India, can apply.

grants.name: ACM India Early Career Researcher Award
grants.deadlineNote: The 2025 cycle closed 15 September 2025; next nomination date not yet posted.
grants.amount: Rs 15 lakh
grants.description: Award for early-career computing researchers in India, roughly 6 to 12 years past their PhD. Self-nominations are not allowed. Open to researchers working in India.

grants.name: New Horizons in Mathematics Prize
grants.deadlineNote: Public nominations for the 2027 prizes ran April to July 2026; the next cycle is not yet dated.
grants.amount: USD 100,000 (up to three prizes)
grants.description: Prize for early-career mathematicians, generally within 10 years of the PhD. Anyone may nominate a candidate online; self-nomination is not allowed. Mathematicians in India are eligible.

grants.name: SASTRA Ramanujan Prize
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026 deadline was 31 July 2026; the 2027 call is not yet posted.
grants.description: Annual prize for mathematicians under 32 working in areas influenced by Ramanujan. Nominations include a CV, papers and three support letters. Open to mathematicians in any country, including India.

grants.name: ICTP Training and Research in Italian Laboratories (TRIL)
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: Call listed as open with a 31 December 2027 deadline; stays are arranged with the host Italian laboratory.
grants.amount: EUR 1,300-1,600 per month depending on career stage, plus travel and health insurance
grants.duration: A few months to one year; up to 24 months with extensions
grants.description: Fellowships for scientists from developing countries to train and do research in Italian laboratories in physics and related fields. Applicants need at least a Master's degree and must live in a developing country when selected. Indian nationals resident in India qualify as developing-country applicants under ICTP rules.

grants.name: APS-EPS-ICTP Travel Award Fellowship Programme (ATAP)
grants.funder: American Physical Society, European Physical Society and ICTP
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 round closed 31 March 2026; the call is annual and the 2027 round is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Travel and subsistence for a two-month lab visit (three grants in 2026)
grants.description: Supports physicists from developing countries for a two-month research visit to a host laboratory to build collaborations. Candidates should preferably be under 45 and within 10 years of the PhD, and must plan to return home. Indian nationals working in India are eligible as developing-country applicants.

grants.name: ICTP Condensed Matter and Statistical Physics Postdoctoral Positions
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 call closed 28 February 2026; the call is annual and the next round is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Internationally competitive salary and benefits (amount not published)
grants.duration: Two years, renewable for one more year
grants.description: Postdoctoral positions in ICTP's Condensed Matter and Statistical Physics section for applicants with a PhD in physics. Applicants of any nationality may apply, so researchers from India are eligible. ICTP's other science sections post separate postdoctoral calls on the same opportunities pages.

grants.name: ICTP Schools, Workshops and Conferences (participant support)
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: Each of the 72 activities in the 2027 calendar has its own application deadline on its event page; several close between November 2026 and early 2027.
grants.amount: No registration fee; limited financial support for participants from developing countries
grants.duration: Typically one to three weeks per activity
grants.description: ICTP runs schools, colleges and workshops in physics, earth system science, quantitative life sciences and related areas, free of charge, with some financial assistance for participants from developing countries. Researchers and students based in India can apply to individual activities through the ICTP portal.

grants.name: IAU Gruber Foundation Fellowship
grants.funder: International Astronomical Union and the Gruber Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 call published 31 August 2026; applications and two reference letters due 22 March 2027, 23:59 Paris time.
grants.amount: USD 25,000 each (three fellowships)
grants.description: Fellowships for early-career astronomers within three years of the PhD, including final-year PhD students with a postdoc offer. The host institution must be in a different country from the PhD or previous postdoc institution. There are no nationality restrictions, and preference may go to candidates from countries in difficult economic situations, so Indian astronomers can apply.

grants.name: CERN Summer Student Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 programme (Member and Non-Member State) close on 21 January 2027 at 23:59 Geneva time.
grants.amount: CHF 94 net per calendar day; travel may be covered
grants.description: Summer placements at CERN for Bachelor's and Master's students in physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics with at least six semesters of study. India is a CERN Associate Member State, so Indian students can apply; non-member-state placements may be limited to 8 weeks.

grants.name: Fulbright-Nehru Doctoral Research Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027-28 competition closed on 1 July 2026. The next cycle usually opens in spring with a July deadline.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend, round-trip airfare, J-1 visa support, accident and sickness cover
grants.description: Research stays at US institutions for Indian citizens registered for a PhD at an Indian institution. Priority fields include critical minerals, energy security, space (astrophysics, planetary science), semiconductors, quantum computing and aerospace engineering. Researchers at CSIR, ICAR, DRDO, ISRO, IISc and IITs are eligible, but central and state government employees are not.

grants.name: Inlaks-Ravi Sankaran Grant for Field Biology, Ecology and Conservation
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 round closed; annual call, past rounds closed around late May. 2027 dates not yet posted.
grants.amount: Up to INR 300,000 per year
grants.duration: Up to one year, with possible follow-up funding
grants.description: Seed grants for young people starting a short research or implementation project in field biology, ecology or conservation in India. Applicants must be Indian citizens living in India with a Bachelor's degree and born on or after 1 January 1996 (2026 rule).

grants.name: Inlaks-Ravi Sankaran Internship for Field Biology, Ecology and Conservation
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 round closed; shortlisting was in April and interviews in May. 2027 dates not yet posted.
grants.amount: Up to USD 10,000 total for living allowance, fees and airfare
grants.description: Funds an overseas placement at a recognised conservation institution for young Indian conservationists. Applicants must be Indian passport holders living in India, hold a Bachelor's degree and show prior field involvement in wildlife ecology or conservation.

grants.name: ALMA Call for Proposals (observing time)
grants.funder: Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ESO, NRAO, NAOJ)
grants.deadlineNote: Cycle 13 closed 23 April 2026; the Cycle 14 call is expected in early 2027 but dates are not yet announced.
grants.amount: Telescope time (no cash award)
grants.description: Annual competitive call for observing time on ALMA. Under ALMA's open-skies policy, astronomers at institutions outside the partner regions, including India, can submit proposals as PI. Proposals go through distributed peer review.

grants.name: ESO Call for Proposals (observing time)
grants.deadlineNote: ESO issues one call per year. The Period 118 call is closed; ESO says the next call will be released in July 2027.
grants.amount: Telescope time on VLT, VLTI, APEX and other ESO facilities
grants.description: Competitive call for observing time on ESO telescopes, reviewed through distributed peer review. Astronomers outside ESO member states, including those based in India, can submit proposals.

grants.name: GMRT Call for Observing Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Cycle 51 proposals closed on 15 July 2026. The standing tentative schedule puts the Cycle 52 announcement around 15 December 2026 and the proposal deadline around 15 January 2027 (for April to September 2027); the October to March cycle has proposals due around 15 July.
grants.amount: Telescope time on the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope
grants.description: Twice-yearly call for observing time on the GMRT near Pune, one of the largest low-frequency radio telescopes. Proposals are reviewed by the GMRT Time Allocation Committee and are open to astronomers in India and abroad.

grants.name: ESO Studentship Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year, 20 April and 20 October; apply through recruitment.eso.org.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend and benefits (see ESO remuneration page)
grants.description: Research stays at ESO for PhD students enrolled at an external university, working with ESO staff. Positions are open to students preferentially but not necessarily from ESO member states, so PhD students at Indian universities can apply.

grants.name: EGU Roland Schlich Travel Support (EGU General Assembly 2027)
grants.deadlineNote: Apply with abstract submission by 1 December 2026, 13:00 CET; decisions by 9 January 2027. EGU27 is 4-9 April 2027 in Vienna.
grants.amount: Registration waiver, abstract charge refund and up to EUR 400 travel
grants.description: Travel support for on-site presenters at the EGU General Assembly. Early-career scientists from low- and middle-income non-European countries, and established scientists from low-, lower-middle and upper-middle income countries, are target groups, which includes researchers based in India. Applicants must be EGU members and first and presenting author of an abstract.

grants.name: IAS Postgraduate and Postdoctoral Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year, closing 31 March and 30 September at midnight CEST. Institutional grants for economies spending under 1% of GDP on R&D share the same dates.
grants.amount: Postgraduate grants up to EUR 1,000; postdoctoral grant amounts in guidelines
grants.description: Research grants for PhD students (student members) and early-career postdocs (ordinary members) working in sedimentology, for fieldwork, lab analyses and similar costs. There is no nationality restriction, so members based in India can apply; conference travel and equipment are not covered.

grants.name: Future For Nature Award
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 award applications closed 23 August 2026; annual call, 2028 round not yet announced.
grants.amount: EUR 50,000 per winner (three winners)
grants.description: Prize for young conservationists aged 18 to 35 working to protect threatened species. Applicants from all over the world can apply, including those based in India.

grants.name: SPIE Optics and Photonics Education Scholarships
grants.funder: SPIE, the international society for optics and photonics
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 applications are open and close 15 February 2027.
grants.amount: USD 3,000-11,000 (named awards up to USD 11,000; 70+ awards of USD 3,000-5,000)
grants.description: Scholarships for students around the world studying optics, photonics or related fields. Applicants must be active SPIE student members, which students in India can join.

grants.name: IEEE Photonics Society Graduate Student Scholarship
grants.deadlineNote: Society page lists 30 May as the annual application deadline.
grants.amount: Up to USD 10,000 awarded annually
grants.description: Scholarships for graduate students in photonics, normally in the penultimate year of study, based on research excellence. Applicants must be IEEE Photonics Society student members; recent honorees come from several countries, and students in India can join and apply.

grants.name: IEEE Electron Devices Society PhD Student Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual nomination cycle; the 2027 deadline is not yet posted on the EDS site.
grants.region: Global (one award intended per region, including Asia and Pacific)
grants.amount: USD 5,000 plus travel to IEDM if needed
grants.description: Fellowships for full-time PhD students in electron devices, with at least one award intended for the Asia and Pacific region. Candidates must be EDS student members with a sponsor who is an EDS member, so PhD students in India can be nominated.

grants.name: IUPAC-Solvay International Award for Young Chemists
grants.funder: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) and Solvay
grants.deadlineNote: Online applications for the 2027 award close 31 January 2027; awards presented at the IUPAC Congress in Montreal, July 2027.
grants.amount: USD 1,000 cash plus up to USD 1,000 travel to the IUPAC Congress
grants.description: Up to five prizes for the best PhD theses in the chemical sciences completed in 2026. The PhD must be granted by an institution in an IUPAC member country; India is a member, so recent Indian PhDs can apply.

grants.name: ECS Summer Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: ECS lists 15 January as the annual deadline; submission opens in mid-September.
grants.amount: Up to USD 5,000 each (up to four awards)
grants.description: Summer research support for graduate students in electrochemistry and solid-state science who will continue their studies after the summer. Awards are made without regard to citizenship; applicants must be ECS members, so students in India can apply.

grants.name: OPCW Programme for Support of Research Projects
grants.funder: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2027 round closed 30 September 2026 (Note S/2526/2026). The next deadline is set in the following year's Technical Secretariat note.
grants.region: OPCW member states with developing or transition economies
grants.amount: Small-scale research grants to the host institution
grants.description: Funds small-scale research in chemistry for peaceful purposes in developing and transition-economy member states. Applications go through the National Authority of the country where the research is done; for India this is the National Authority Chemical Weapons Convention.

grants.name: APN Call for Proposals (CRRP and CAPaBLE)
grants.funder: Asia-Pacific Network for Global Change Research (APN)
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 call open: Stage 1 summary proposals due 30 November 2026, 23:59 Japan Standard Time, via APNIS. Invited full proposals due 29 March 2027.
grants.amount: Project grants (amount set per call)
grants.description: Funds collaborative regional research on global change and sustainability (CRRP, at least three member countries) and science capacity building (CAPaBLE). India is an APN member country, so researchers at Indian institutions can lead or join proposals.

grants.name: International Climate Protection Fellowship
grants.funder: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (funded by Germany's International Climate Initiative)
grants.deadlineNote: Next call opens 7 December 2026 and closes early once 120 applications are received (90 prospective leaders, 30 postdocs). Apply promptly after opening.
grants.region: Germany (applicants from non-European developing and transition countries)
grants.amount: EUR 2,500-3,000 per month plus allowances; host receives EUR 800 per month for science and engineering projects
grants.description: Fellowships for prospective leaders and postdocs working on climate protection or climate adaptation to carry out a project with a host in Germany. Applicants must be citizens of a non-European developing or transition country who have lived and worked mainly there, which includes India.

grants.name: IGSTC 2+2 Industrial R&D Projects
grants.funder: Indo-German Science and Technology Centre (IGSTC; DST and BMFTR)
grants.deadlineNote: Thematic calls roughly once a year; the most recent (Advanced Materials, 2025) had a first-stage deadline of 18 September 2025. Next call not yet posted.
grants.amount: Up to INR 350 lakh for Indian partners and up to EUR 450,000-500,000 for German partners
grants.description: Joint R&D projects of industrial relevance with at least one academic institution and one company from each of India and Germany. Indian principal investigators must hold regular positions; Indian companies must be majority Indian-owned.

grants.name: TWAS-FAPESP Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme
grants.funder: UNESCO-TWAS and the São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP)
grants.deadlineNote: Host supervisors submitted projects by 1 November 2026; the list of supervisors is published after 1 December 2026. Full proposals due 1 April 2027; results August 2027.
grants.amount: FAPESP postdoctoral fellowship (see call document)
grants.description: Postdoctoral stays at São Paulo State institutions for researchers from developing countries with a PhD from the last seven years, in fields including physics, chemistry, engineering, and astronomy, space and earth sciences. India is on TWAS's list of developing countries, so Indian researchers can apply.

grants.name: RIKEN Special Postdoctoral Researcher (SPDR) Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the FY2027 call ran 10 February to 2 April 2026 (registration), with documents due 9 April 2026. FY2028 dates are not yet posted.
grants.amount: JPY 550,000 per month plus allowances; research budget JPY 1,000,000 per year
grants.description: Independent postdoctoral positions at RIKEN laboratories for early-career researchers with a recent PhD in the natural sciences, engineering or mathematics. Applicants contact a RIKEN host lab before applying; the call sets no nationality restriction, so Indian researchers can apply.

grants.name: DESY Summer Student Programme
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 programme in preparation; past rounds closed 31 January.
grants.amount: EUR 28.50 per day, free hostel accommodation, partial travel reimbursement
grants.description: Summer research and lecture programme for undergraduate students in physics and related fields such as scientific computing and engineering. The programme is international and does not restrict nationality, so students from India can apply.

grants.name: Save Our Seas Foundation Small Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Closed; applications reopen mid-May 2027.
grants.amount: Up to USD 10,000
grants.description: Annual grants for early-career scientists, educators and conservationists working on threatened marine megafauna, especially sharks, rays and skates. Projects must combine at least two of research, conservation and education. The grants page sets no nationality restriction, so researchers in India can apply.

grants.name: JN Tata Endowment Loan Scholarship
grants.funder: The J.N. Tata Endowment for the Higher Education of Indians
grants.deadlineNote: Annual window; for Fall 2026-Spring 2027 forms were available 5 January to 29 March 2026. The next window is not yet posted.
grants.amount: Loan scholarship (amount set per award)
grants.description: Merit-based loan scholarships for Indian citizens with an Indian undergraduate degree going abroad for Master's, PhD or postdoctoral study in any field. Selection includes an aptitude test and expert interviews.

grants.name: K.C. Mahindra Scholarships for Post-Graduate Studies Abroad
grants.deadlineNote: 2026 round closed 30 April 2026; the next round is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Interest-free loan scholarship up to INR 10 lakh (top three) or INR 5 lakh
grants.description: Interest-free loan scholarships for Indian citizens with a first-class degree admitted to postgraduate programmes abroad, in any field including the sciences and engineering. At least 50 awards are made each year.

grants.name: Narotam Sekhsaria Foundation Postgraduate Scholarship
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are invited each January; the 2026 round closed in March 2026.
grants.amount: Interest-free repayable financial assistance
grants.description: Merit-based interest-free loan scholarships for Indian students pursuing postgraduate study at institutions in India or abroad. Science and engineering students are eligible.

grants.name: Oriental Bird Club Small Conservation Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year, 1 March and 1 September; email the application form to the club.
grants.amount: Typically GBP 1,000-2,000; up to GBP 3,000 in exceptional cases
grants.description: Small grants for bird conservation projects in Asia, prioritising threatened species, Important Bird Areas and community work, with preference for applicants from the project country. Projects in India fall within the club's region.

grants.name: British Ecological Society Small Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year; Round 2 of 2026 ran 8 June to 8 September 2026. 2027 round dates not yet posted.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 5,000
grants.description: Grants for ecological research, especially for early-career researchers, open to BES members from all countries for projects anywhere. BES aims to direct at least 51% of grant funding to ecologists who are citizens of and work in Global South countries, which includes India.

grants.name: Reliance Foundation Postgraduate Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: 2026-27 round closed 5 October 2026; the next annual round is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Up to INR 6 lakh over the degree
grants.description: Scholarships for first-year postgraduate students in India in engineering, technology, energy (including renewable and new energy) and life sciences. Applicants must be resident Indian citizens with a GATE score of 550-1,000 or undergraduate CGPA of 7.5 or above.

grants.name: Nexa Lighthouse Funding Opportunity: Asia and the Pacific
grants.funder: Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN, with Nexa Lighthouse funding partners
grants.deadlineNote: Deadline extended: applications close 8 December 2026, 2:00 PM ET (19:00 UTC), through the Grand Challenges Canada Fluxx portal.
grants.amount: Approximately USD 250,000–2,000,000 per innovation
grants.description: Transition to Scale funding for proven climate-and-health innovations that help health actors respond to mosquito-borne infections, extreme heat, or poor air quality, through climate-informed early warning and monitoring or climate-responsive patient care. Organisations may be incorporated in any country but must implement in an eligible country in Asia or the Pacific.

grants.name: AI Alignment Foundation Research Support
grants.deadlineNote: No deadline stated; applications accepted through the foundation's form.
grants.amount: Not stated; funding plus access to dedicated engineering teams
grants.description: Support for high-risk, high-reward research on new directions in AI alignment, including ideas from fields such as cognitive neuroscience, mathematics, or physics. Individuals and teams may apply; institutional affiliation is optional.

grants.name: Theodore Millon Grant in Personality Psychology
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 program year open 1 November 2026 and close 14 December 2026.
grants.amount: One grant of USD 2,000
grants.description: Research grant in personality psychology, including personality theory, personality disorders, and personality assessment, with preference for work on how personality assessment is studied, developed, or delivered. Open to graduate students and psychologists holding an EdD, PsyD, or PhD.

grants.name: Microbiota & Women's Health International Call for Projects
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 January 2027, 24:00 CET. Decision expected May 2027.
grants.description: Clinical or fundamental research on male–female genital microbiome interactions and their role in vaginal dysbiosis, including bacterial vaginosis; STI projects other than bacterial vaginosis are excluded. Open to MDs, PhDs, and Pharm-Ds worldwide, applying through a university, hospital, or research institution; overhead capped at 10%.

grants.name: WSDM Cup 2027: Writing Agents for Community Notes
grants.funder: ACM WSDM 2027, with the Community Notes team at X
grants.deadlineNote: Registration is open; the qualifying round runs 18 November to 8 December 2026 and official scoring runs 12 December 2026 to 5 February 2027 (dates tentative).
grants.amount: USD 10,000 prize pool (USD 4,000 first place, open-weight model bonuses), plus USD 500–1,000 in X API credits and USD 200+ in Grok API credits per team
grants.description: Competition to build fully automated agents that propose Community Notes on real posts on X; agents that meet minimum performance criteria are deployed and evaluated on-platform with real human ratings. Individuals or teams; each participant needs an X account that is not already a Community Notes contributor.

grants.name: INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: The INSPIRE-SHE (2025) call opened on 7 November 2026 and closes on 7 December 2026 at 23:59 IST.
grants.amount: Rs 60,000 per year, plus a mentorship grant of Rs 20,000 per year in the third and fourth years
grants.description: Scholarships for students aged 17 to 22 enrolled in B.Sc., B.S., B.S.-M.S. or integrated M.Sc. programmes in the natural and basic sciences. Eligibility is through the top 1% of a Class XII board (2025 pass-outs for this call), a JEE or NEET rank within 10,000, or qualifying national talent schemes and olympiads.

grants.name: Focus Area Science Technology Summer Fellowship (FAST-SF) 2027
grants.funder: Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc), Indian National Science Academy (INSA) and National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI)
grants.deadlineNote: Online applications close on 30 November 2026; selections are communicated around March to April 2027.
grants.region: India (applicants from the North-Eastern states, Andaman, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Uttarakhand)
grants.amount: Round-trip train fare and a monthly fellowship for living expenses
grants.description: About 200 fellowships for students and teachers from colleges and universities in the listed states to work on a short project with a scientist associated with the three academies anywhere in India. It runs alongside the academies' Summer Research Fellowship Programme but is reserved for the focus regions.

grants.name: INSA Young Associates (IYA) 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations must reach INSA by email (iya.iaf@insa.nic.in) on or before 30 November 2026 for consideration in 2027.
grants.amount: One-time travel support of up to Rs 1.5 lakh to attend an international conference abroad
grants.duration: Recognition; travel support usable within two years
grants.description: Recognition for up to 36 Indian scientists under 40 on 31 December 2026 (43 for women), selected for their research contributions; OCI/PIO card holders working in India for at least 5 years are also eligible. Candidates must be nominated by a head of institution or department, a vice-chancellor, registrar or dean, or an INSA Fellow.

grants.name: IIT Madras Institute Post-Doctoral Fellowship (IPDF)
grants.deadlineNote: Selection runs throughout the year; applications go by email to the proposed faculty mentor.
grants.amount: Rs 1,30,000 per month (Rs 70,000 from the Institute plus at least Rs 60,000 from the mentor's project funds) and Rs 2,00,000 per year contingency
grants.duration: 1 year initially, extendable by up to 2 more years
grants.description: Fellowships for PhD holders within five years of their PhD and aged 32 or under at joining (relaxations apply), with at least two Q1 journal papers as primary contributor. Applicants need a faculty mentor at IIT Madras who commits project funds and must submit a research proposal that is not an extension of their PhD work.

grants.name: IIT Madras Post-Doctoral Fellowship for Women with a Break in Career
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are accepted throughout the year by email to resipdf@smail.iitm.ac.in.
grants.amount: Rs 58,000 per month consolidated, plus train fare and campus accommodation if available
grants.duration: 2 to 6 months over 2 or 3 visits, extendable to a total of one year
grants.description: Fellowships for women with a PhD who have had a break of at least two years after the PhD and are not currently employed, with no upper age limit. Fellows work in engineering, science, humanities or management departments at IIT Madras.

grants.name: DST-DFG Joint Call on International Research Training Groups (IRTG)
grants.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DST), India and Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), Germany
grants.deadlineNote: Open throughout the year with two deadlines for joint draft proposals, 1 February and 1 August. Review of the draft takes about 6 to 8 months; if approved, a full proposal is invited and submitted to DST and DFG at the same time.
grants.amount: Not stated on the DST portal
grants.duration: Up to 9 years in two funding periods, with a mid-term evaluation
grants.description: Joint DST-DFG support for Indian research groups partnering with German universities on International Research Training Groups, which run structured doctoral training across both countries. Indian partners submit through the DST e-PMS portal (International Cooperation Division).

grants.name: Branco Weiss Fellowship - Society in Science
grants.funder: Branco Weiss Foundation (administered by ETH Zurich)
grants.deadlineNote: The annual submission deadline is 15 January (5 p.m. CET); applicants must hold a PhD by then, obtained at most five years earlier.
grants.region: Global (any nationality, host institution anywhere in the world)
grants.amount: Up to CHF 600,000
grants.description: Independent postdoctoral fellowship in any scientific field for researchers who also want to engage with the social, political or cultural side of science. Fellows choose their own project and host institution.

grants.name: Simons Fellows-to-Faculty Award (2027)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are due 13 January 2027 at 12 p.m. ET; this is the last call for the SCPAB track.
grants.region: Global (no citizenship requirement; awards can be held inside or outside the United States, not in China)
grants.amount: USD 600,000 faculty research award plus an optional postdoctoral award of USD 110,000 per year
grants.duration: 3-year faculty award, preceded by up to 2 years of optional postdoctoral support
grants.description: Supports postdocs in autism research (SFARI), the aging brain (SCPAB) or ecological neuroscience (SCENE) who will apply for tenure-track faculty jobs in September 2027. Applicants must be in a mentored position and not yet hold PI-level funding.

grants.name: Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology (2027)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are due 3 December 2026 at 12 p.m. ET, with decisions on 1 May 2027.
grants.amount: Up to USD 360,000 (USD 85,000 annual stipend plus up to USD 35,000 annual allowance)
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships for basic research in plant biology, held with one or two sponsors at a U.S. nonprofit research institution. Applicants must have received the PhD no more than three years before the deadline.

grants.name: Simons Targeted Grants to Math+AI Institutes (2027)
grants.deadlineNote: Full proposals are due 1 December 2026 at 12 p.m. ET; this is a one-time call.
grants.region: Global (U.S. and foreign institutes and research centers, excluding China)
grants.amount: Up to USD 500,000
grants.description: Funds established mathematics institutes or centers with a physical space to run workshops and initiatives on AI in mathematics, such as evaluating AI-assisted results and setting community standards. Anthropic and OpenAI may make additional awards from the same applications.

grants.name: Simons Scientific Software Research Faculty Award (2027-2028)
grants.deadlineNote: Letters of intent are due 21 January 2027 at 12 p.m. ET; selected awardees must then secure a U.S. host position starting by 1 September 2028.
grants.region: United States host (no citizenship or country requirement for applicants)
grants.amount: Salary support (100% for 2 years, 50% for 3 years) plus USD 50,000 per year research allowance
grants.description: Creates research faculty positions at U.S. PhD-granting institutions for people who lead development of scientific software in mathematics, astronomy or theoretical physics. Applicants need a PhD in one of those fields.

grants.name: SFARI New Ideas Award
grants.deadlineNote: Letters of intent are accepted on a rolling basis.
grants.region: Global (faculty-level researchers at research institutions, excluding China)
grants.amount: Up to USD 300,000 per year
grants.description: Early-stage funding for exploratory research that tests new hypotheses about autism and related neurodevelopmental disorders, from any scientific discipline. Applicants must hold a faculty position or equivalent.

grants.name: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan (Short-term)
grants.funder: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
grants.deadlineNote: The Japanese host institution must submit to JSPS by 23 April 2027 for the second FY2027 short-term round; host internal deadlines are earlier.
grants.region: Japan (invited researchers from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan, including India)
grants.amount: Round-trip airfare, JPY 18,000 per day, travel insurance, and up to JPY 150,000 research support
grants.description: Lets a researcher in Japan invite an overseas faculty-level researcher for short visits for discussions, lectures and joint work. The application is filed by the Japanese host, not the visitor.

grants.name: Transformative AI Fund
grants.deadlineNote: The fund is always open to applications.
grants.amount: Typically USD 10,000-150,000, rarely above USD 300,000
grants.description: Early-stage grants to individuals and new projects working on transformative AI, mainly on reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI, including research, training and field-building. It replaced the Long-Term Future Fund.

grants.name: ETH Zurich Student Summer Research Fellowship 2027
grants.funder: ETH Zurich, Department of Computer Science
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are open 1 November to 16 December 2026, 13:00 CET, through SiROP.
grants.amount: CHF 4,000 stipend plus travel and visa costs
grants.description: Summer research placement in an ETH computer science group for bachelor's and master's students in computer science or a related field who have completed at least two years of study and graduate in 2028 or later.

grants.name: Summer@EPFL Research Internship 2027
grants.funder: EPFL School of Computer and Communication Sciences
grants.deadlineNote: The next deadline is 29 November 2026 (Anywhere on Earth); applications may open only a couple of weeks before it.
grants.amount: CHF 1,800 per month plus travel refund
grants.duration: 2 to 3 months, usually May to September 2027
grants.description: Funded summer research internship in an EPFL computer science or communication systems lab for bachelor's students in their second year or later and master's students in computer science, computer engineering and related fields.

grants.name: EPFL School of Life Sciences Summer Research Program 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 programme (5 July to 27 August 2027) closed on 15 November 2026. The next call is expected around autumn 2027.
grants.region: Global (held in Lausanne and Geneva, Switzerland)
grants.amount: CHF 3,600 stipend for two months plus travel up to CHF 1,000
grants.description: Eight-week lab placement at EPFL for international bachelor's and first-year master's students in biology, biophysics, chemistry, bioengineering, bioinformatics and related fields; housing is arranged near campus.

grants.name: CERN openlab Summer Student Programme 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close on 21 January 2027 at 23:59 Geneva time.
grants.region: Global, all nationalities (held in Geneva, Switzerland)
grants.amount: CHF 94 per day subsistence allowance
grants.description: Summer placement in a CERN computing team for bachelor's and master's students in computer science or IT who will have completed at least six semesters of study, with lectures and site visits alongside the project.

grants.name: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships 2027/28
grants.funder: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close at 16:00 GMT on 8 December 2026; candidates must also apply to the participating UK university course.
grants.region: Eligible low and middle income Commonwealth countries, including India
grants.amount: Full tuition, return airfare, and a stipend of GBP 1,712 per month (GBP 2,000 in London)
grants.description: Funds a one-year master's degree at a participating UK university for candidates from eligible Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK.

grants.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: Each programme sets its own deadline, usually between October and January for study starting the following autumn.
grants.region: Global (study at two or more European universities)
grants.amount: Full scholarships covering participation costs, travel, visa and a living allowance (programme dependent)
grants.description: Joint master's programmes run by university consortia across Europe, some of which award full scholarships to top-ranked applicants worldwide; students apply directly to the programme through the Erasmus Mundus catalogue.

grants.name: Schwarzman Scholars
grants.deadlineNote: For the Class of 2028-2029, the window runs April to September 2027 for U.S. and global applicants and March to May 2027 for applicants with Chinese citizenship; exact closing dates are not yet posted.
grants.amount: Fully funded
grants.description: Fully funded one-year master's in global affairs at Tsinghua University for applicants aged 18 to 28 with an undergraduate degree in any field.

grants.name: Jane Street Graduate Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 round closed on 13 November 2026; dates for the 2028 round are not yet announced.
grants.region: PhD students at universities in the US, Canada, UK, Europe, Australia, New Zealand or Singapore; international students eligible
grants.amount: Full tuition and fees plus USD 50,000 stipend
grants.description: Supports PhD students in electrical engineering and computer science, mathematics, physics or statistics with at least one year remaining, or those committed to start a PhD the following autumn.

grants.name: ACM-W Scholarships for Attending Research Conferences
grants.deadlineNote: Six rounds a year; the 15 December 2026 round covers conferences held 1 February to 31 March 2027.
grants.amount: Up to USD 600 (same continent) or USD 1,200 (intercontinental)
grants.description: Travel support for women undergraduate and graduate students in computing to attend any computer science research conference; presenting a paper is not required and an advisor letter is needed.

grants.name: Google Summer of Code
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 timeline is not yet published; in 2026 contributor applications ran 16 to 31 March.
grants.amount: Stipend scaled by country and project size
grants.description: Paid remote programme in which new contributors, including students, work on an open source project with mentors from a participating organisation.

grants.name: Outreachy Internships
grants.deadlineNote: Dates for the May 2027 cohort are not yet announced; initial applications for past May cohorts opened in early February.
grants.duration: 3 months (May to August or December to March)
grants.description: Paid remote internships in open source and open science for people who face underrepresentation, systemic bias or discrimination in the technology industry of their country.

grants.name: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Entries close at 11:59 p.m. CST on 28 February 2027.
grants.amount: Student Prize USD 25,000 cash plus USD 250,000 Azure credits; overall First Prize USD 250,000
grants.duration: Competition runs to the World Championship in May or June 2027
grants.description: Startup competition for early-stage software startups registered as a legal entity on or after 2 November 2024; teams whose founders are all enrolled students can enter a separate Student Startup category.

grants.name: Vesuvius Challenge 2027 Prizes
grants.deadlineNote: Monthly progress prizes (next deadline 30 November 2026); the 2027 Grand Prize and First Letters prizes close on 25 June 2027.
grants.amount: USD 1,000,000 Grand Prize pool, USD 50,000 per scroll First Letters prizes, monthly prizes up to USD 20,000
grants.description: Open machine learning and computer vision competition to read carbonised Herculaneum scrolls from X-ray scans; winners must release their methods under a permissive open source licence.

grants.name: Apart Research AI Safety Sprints
grants.deadlineNote: Weekend sprints run regularly; upcoming ones are on 4 to 6 December and 11 to 13 December 2026.
grants.amount: Team prizes vary by sprint
grants.description: Free weekend research hackathons on AI safety topics such as threat modelling and agent attribution; top teams may be invited to continue their work with Apart.

grants.name: BioCARe - Biotechnology Career Advancement and Re-orientation for Women Researchers (2026-27)
grants.funder: Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026-27 call is no longer listed as open. Check DBT's call-for-proposals page for the next round.
grants.amount: Up to INR 60 lakh (Cat-I) or INR 40 lakh (Cat-II) including fellowship
grants.description: First extramural research grant for women scientists in biotechnology and allied areas to advance or re-establish research careers. Category I: PhD in Biotechnology / Life Sciences / allied or interdisciplinary areas, or MD / MDS / M.V.Sc. Category II: M.Tech in Biotechnology / allied areas, M.Pharma, or equivalent.

grants.name: Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2026
grants.funder: Ministry of Education, Government of India / AICTE
grants.deadlineNote: SIH 2026 launched in August 2026; team nomination and idea submission closed on 9 October 2026 (extended). Check the funder's site for later stages and the next edition.
grants.amount: Rs 1 lakh per winning team per problem statement
grants.description: Nationwide initiative by the Ministry of Education engaging Higher Education Institution students to solve problem statements submitted by government ministries, PSUs, industries and NGOs. 16 themes including Smart Automation, MedTech/BioTech, Agriculture, Robotics, Blockchain & Cybersecurity, Smart Education, and Disaster Management.

grants.name: IndoML Datathon 2026 - Indic Speech Noise Detection & Removal
grants.funder: IndoML (Heritage Institute of Technology, IIT Kharagpur, IISc Bangalore, Inception - G42)
grants.deadlineNote: Registration closed 9 September 2026 and final submissions closed 17 October 2026. Top teams present at IndoML 2026 at IIT Kharagpur in December 2026.
grants.amount: INR 2,00,000 total prize pool
grants.description: Research-oriented data-science competition on noise event detection and removal in real-world Indic speech. Two tracks: (1) identify noise events with precise timestamps, (2) suppress detected noise while preserving speech intelligibility. Uses ~150 hours of real-world Indic audio from the Vaani corpus. At least one team member must be affiliated with an Indian university or research institution.

grants.name: India AMR Co-Development Programme (I-AMR-CDP)
grants.deadlineNote: The expression-of-interest window closed on 31 October 2026. Selected innovators enter a co-development agreement with Venus Remedies via a mutually agreed value-sharing model.
grants.amount: INR 10 lakh upfront award on entering a co-development agreement, plus Venus-led development investment
grants.description: Co-development call for promising Indian anti-infective innovations at proof-of-concept or preclinical stage: novel antibiotics, beta-lactamase inhibitors, or adjunctive/potentiator therapies. Selected teams receive end-to-end development, R&D infrastructure, manufacturing, commercialisation, IP, and publication support. Open to academic institutions, industry researchers, startups or spin-outs, and independent investigators in India.

grants.name: TNQ Inspiring Science Awards (ISA) 2027
grants.deadlineNote: The ISA 2027 call closed on 31 October 2026. The next call is expected around mid-2027.
grants.amount: Apple laptop, medal, and citation for eight finalists; winner also receives a conference travel fellowship
grants.description: Annual award recognising the best full-length life-sciences research paper by a student from India. Open to PhD researchers and postdoctoral fellows within four years of their postdoctoral programme, where the work was conducted at an India-based institution.

grants.name: ICMR Centres for Advanced Research (CAR) Special Calls 2026
grants.deadlineNote: The two special calls (Priority Medical Devices and Diagnostic Technologies; NIRMAN-AT Assistive Technology) closed on 13 November 2026 and are no longer listed on ICMR's call page. Check that page for future CAR calls.
grants.amount: Up to INR 15 crore per centre
grants.description: ICMR funds multi-technology Centres for Advanced Research that take medical devices, diagnostics and assistive technologies to translation. The medical devices call is limited to regular faculty at the top 25 NIRF 2025 institutions; the assistive technology call is open to institutions eligible for ICMR extramural support. A Co-PI from the PI's institute is mandatory.

grants.name: The Alignment Project
grants.funder: UK AI Security Institute with OpenAI, Microsoft and other partners
grants.deadlineNote: Applications currently closed; next round not yet dated.
grants.amount: GBP 50,000 to 1,000,000, plus compute credits and support from AISI researchers
grants.description: Funds research on AI alignment and control across disciplines, as an international coalition with over GBP 27 million committed. The first round funded projects in eight countries. The page does not restrict applicants by country, so researchers in India can apply when the next round opens.

grants.name: Saroj Chandrasekhar Memorial Young Researcher Award 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 December 2026. The award is presented at IIT Kanpur on National Science Day, 28 February 2027.
grants.amount: INR 3.5 lakh cash prize, certificate, travel and lodging for the ceremony
grants.description: Recognises an early-career woman scientist in biosciences, biotechnology, life sciences or medical sciences, at assistant-professor level or above and within five years of starting an independent position. The winner gives an honorary lecture at IIT Kanpur.

grants.name: Gut Microbiota International Call for Projects 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 30 November 2026, 24:00 CET. Decision expected May 2027.
grants.amount: EUR 200,000 (VAT included), paid to the institution
grants.description: Clinical or fundamental research on diet-microbiome interactions that shape immune function in the treatment of human disease. Projects must include microbiome analysis, immunophenotyping and a dietary component, mainly in humans and in a disease context; observational studies of healthy subjects alone are excluded. Open to MDs, PhDs and PharmDs in any country, applying through a university, hospital or research institution.

grants.name: Housing Reform: From Policy to Lasting Outcomes
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 19 February 2027. Decisions expected 2 April 2027.
grants.amount: Up to USD 20,000; larger awards possible for exceptional projects
grants.description: Supports research on how the design and implementation of housing reforms shape housing supply, access and other outcomes, leading to peer-reviewed papers, policy white papers or research databases. Open to faculty, graduate students and policy researchers. Covers research travel, collaboration, data, materials and publishing; excludes living costs, hardware, retroactive costs and overhead.

grants.name: SVRI Early Career Research Fellowships
grants.funder: Sexual Violence Research Initiative, supported by the Kering Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 January 2027.
grants.amount: Doctoral: USD 17,000; postdoctoral: USD 20,500
grants.description: Two doctoral and two postdoctoral fellowships for locally led research on the overlap between violence against women and violence against children. Open to nationals of low- and middle-income countries enrolled full-time at an in-person academic institution in an LMIC; PhD applicants need an approved or defended dissertation proposal.

grants.name: BIRAC Femtech Call for Women Founders
grants.funder: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close on 23 November 2026.
grants.amount: Not stated in the call guidelines; support is described as investment opportunities and market and technology linkages
grants.description: Support for DPIIT-recognised Indian startups with a woman founder, co-founder or CXO and at least 51% Indian ownership, working on women's health. Areas include reproductive and sexual health, maternal care, menopause, women's health diagnostics, gynaecological cancers, and digital health and AI for women.

grants.name: Request for Proposals: Incubation
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 18 December 2026.
grants.amount: USD 20,000 to USD 7.5 million
grants.description: Funds incubators and accelerators that find founders and launch cost-effective organisations in areas such as global health, high-impact policy, animal welfare and global catastrophic risks. Open to existing incubators and accelerators, and to individuals or teams starting a new incubator.

grants.name: NII Shonan Meeting Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Two closing dates a year (15 June and 15 December); proposals can be submitted any time and are reviewed after the next closing date. Results take about 4-6 months; meetings are held 8 months to 2 years later (new organisers should plan for May 2029 or later).
grants.amount: Hosted 4-day seminar for 25-35 invited participants
grants.description: NII hosts small Dagstuhl-style seminars on any topic in informatics at the Shonan Village Center. A proposal needs at most three organisers, at least one based in Asia, and an invitee list of more than 50 people.

grants.name: Lorentz Center Workshops
grants.deadlineNote: Three rounds a year on the last Thursday of January, May and September. The January round covers workshops from September of the same year to April of the next.
grants.amount: In-kind support (venue, breaks, social events, organisational help) worth about EUR 25,000-30,000 per workshop; no registration fees. Participant travel and hotel are generally not covered.
grants.description: Peer-reviewed, interactive research workshops of up to a week in any discipline, with strong mathematics and computer science representation. Proposals list 3-5 organisers and a plan for any external funding.

grants.name: NBHM Travel Grants for Mathematicians
grants.funder: National Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM), Department of Atomic Energy
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling. The application must reach NBHM at least three months before the date of travel. One grant per two financial years.
grants.region: India-based mathematicians; travel within India or abroad
grants.amount: Partial or full travel cost; living expenses not covered
grants.description: NBHM supports travel by mathematicians to conferences, symposia, summer schools and short collaborative visits in India or abroad. Applications are emailed to NBHM on the prescribed form.

grants.name: ASL Student Travel Awards
grants.deadlineNote: For ASL-sponsored meetings, apply at least three months before the meeting; late applications are not accepted. Check the ASL Newsletter for meeting-specific dates.
grants.region: Worldwide (ASL membership required for sponsored meetings; awards for the North American Annual Meeting and Logic Colloquium are limited by NSF rules to US citizens, residents and students at US universities)
grants.amount: Typically USD 200-600 per sponsored meeting
grants.description: Travel grants for students, mainly graduate students, to attend ASL and ASL-sponsored logic meetings such as the Asian Logic Conference. Apply by email with a one-page letter and a supervisor's recommendation.

grants.name: SIAM Student Travel Awards
grants.funder: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM)
grants.deadlineNote: Each SIAM conference has its own deadline, usually about three months before the meeting. Listed dates are for MS27, DS27/LA27, GS27, FM27, AG27 and CT27.
grants.region: Full-time students worldwide (early-career awards limited to US-based researchers); most 2027 conferences are in the US
grants.amount: Partial travel and registration support (varies by conference)
grants.description: SIAM offers travel support to full-time students attending its conferences, including those on applied linear algebra, applied algebraic geometry and dynamical systems. Applications are made separately for each conference.

grants.name: IndiaAI Compute Portal (subsidised GPU access)
grants.funder: IndiaAI Mission, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling monthly window: compute requests accepted from the 1st to the 25th of each month. Requests under 5,000 GPU hours are auto-approved; larger ones go to a committee. Approvals are valid for 30 days.
grants.region: India (login via DigiLocker, e-Pramaan or Jan Parichay)
grants.amount: Subsidised GPU hours from empanelled providers; user pays costs beyond the subsidy
grants.description: Researchers, faculty, students and early-stage researchers in AI/ML can request subsidised GPU compute. Researchers need an h-index of 5 or more, 150+ citations, or ML/AI publications in journals with impact factor above 2.5; students need an AI/ML project.

grants.name: Oberwolfach Seminars (participation for PhD students and postdocs)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 seminar topics are usually announced in early December 2026; each seminar has its own application deadline. Apply by email to seminars@mfo.de.
grants.amount: Free board and lodging; travel reimbursed up to about EUR 150 on average
grants.description: One-week courses for up to 25 PhD students and postdocs (PhD within the last 10 years) on current topics in mathematics. Participation is by invitation from the Director after application.

grants.name: IMU Breakout Graduate Fellowships
grants.funder: International Mathematical Union, Commission for Developing Countries (IMU-CDC)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 call closed 30 May 2026 and the next call is expected to open in early 2027. Students must be nominated by a mathematics professor.

grants.amount: Up to USD 10,000 per year
grants.duration: Up to 4 years or until PhD completion
grants.description: Covers tuition, travel, housing and living costs for excellent students pursuing a mathematics PhD in a developing country. Cannot be combined with another scholarship; joint programmes with institutions in non-developing countries are not eligible.

grants.name: Microsoft Research India Research Fellows Program
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 cycle opened 7 January 2026 and closed 15 February 2026; a similar January-February window is expected for 2027.
grants.description: Paid pre-doctoral research positions at MSR India for graduates with a BS/BE/BTech or MS/ME/MTech in computer science or a related field. PhD students and PhD holders are not eligible; non-CS backgrounds may apply.

grants.name: Wellcome Leap: Autoimmune in Menopause and Pregnancy Transitions (AMPT)
grants.deadlineNote: Abstract portal opens 25 November 2026; 7-page abstracts due 2 December 2026, 11:59pm ET. Abstract feedback 17 December; full proposal portal opens 14 January 2027; decisions 20 February 2027.

grants.amount: USD 50M programme; multiple projects
grants.description: A new USD 50M programme on why autoimmune disease risk rises and falls with hormone transitions in women, using rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis and lupus as index cases. Universities, research institutes, companies and non-profits may propose, alone or as small teams, in one or more of the programme's thrust areas.

grants.name: Anthropic Economic Futures Research Fund
grants.deadlineNote: Open request for proposals via an application form linked from the announcement (22 July 2026); no closing date stated.
grants.amount: Mostly USD 5-30 million per project; nothing below USD 1 million

Proposals must come from universities, independent research institutes, policy research organisations or nonprofits with experience running field experiments at scale; individuals may be PIs only through their institution.

grants.name: OpenAI Cybersecurity Grant Program

grants.amount: Increments of USD 10,000 in API credits, direct funding or equivalents
grants.description: Funds practical applications of AI to defensive cybersecurity, such as automated vulnerability patching, incident triage, malware detection and secure code analysis. Offensive-security projects are not considered, and outputs should be shared for public benefit.

grants.name: IBM Quantum Credits
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling applications via the form linked from the programme post (August 2025); no cycle deadline stated.
grants.amount: Free access to IBM quantum hardware (typically 5-10 hours of QPU time)
grants.description: Gives free access to IBM quantum computers and software for utility-scale research projects (roughly more than 30 qubits). Applicants must be tenure-track or permanent academic staff at a research institute and must not already have IBM Quantum access beyond the Open Plan.

grants.name: Samsung Global Research Outreach (GRO)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. The 2026 cycle ran 22 June to 23 August 2026 and has closed; the 2027 call is expected around June 2027. India contact: gro.asia@samsung.com.
grants.amount: Typically up to about USD 150,000 per project per year
grants.description: Samsung's annual call inviting university researchers to propose projects in topics set each year, recently including scientific AI, quantum computing, next-generation computing, advanced devices and sustainability technology. Selected projects are funded for one year and may be extended; multi-university proposals are accepted.

grants.name: ICSSR Senior Fellowship 2026-27 (2nd Call)
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Online applications close 20 November 2026, 6:00 PM IST; forwarded through the affiliating institution.

Proposals must fall within ICSSR's listed thematic areas for 2026-27, which include economics, governance, gender, history and heritage, language and culture, and environment.

grants.name: ICHR Post-Doctoral Fellowship and Senior Academic Fellowship 2026-27
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026-27 round closed on 16 November 2026 (extended from 30 October 2026). The next call is expected around September to October 2027.
grants.amount: PDF: Rs 33,880 per month plus Rs 24,200 per year contingency. SAF: Rs 48,400 per month plus Rs 48,400 per year contingency.
grants.description: Full-time research fellowships in history and allied subjects. The Post-Doctoral Fellowship (10 awards) is for PhD holders affiliated with a university or research institute; the Senior Academic Fellowship (up to 14 awards) requires age 50+ (45+ for SC/ST/PwD), 15 years of experience, 10 peer-reviewed articles and a book.

grants.name: ICPR Research Project Grants
grants.funder: Indian Council of Philosophical Research (ICPR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Apply via the online form linked in the guidelines by 22 November 2026, 11:59 PM. A separate SC/ST special drive is also listed on icpr.ac.in.
grants.amount: Not fixed; budget capped at 30% each for books, domestic travel and research assistance, 10% contingency
grants.description: Funding for research projects in philosophy, including translations of classical texts, submitted by individuals affiliated with Indian universities, colleges, government-funded research institutes or registered non-profits. International travel and asset creation are not funded.

grants.name: Gerda Henkel Foundation Research Scholarships and Research Projects
grants.deadlineNote: Two deadlines a year. 20 November 2026 is for the April 2027 committee meeting (funding from May 2027 at the earliest); the May 2027 date will be announced after the November deadline. Since 1 July 2026 all scholarship applications go through these regular deadlines; the simplified procedure for short-term scholarships has ended.
grants.region: International (any nationality or place of work)
grants.amount: Scholarships EUR 2,760 per month (postdoc) or EUR 3,720 (post-habilitation), plus travel and material costs
grants.description: Individual research scholarships and group research projects in history, archaeology, art history, history of law, historical Islamic studies and history of science, or neighbouring fields with a historical core question. Postdoc applicants must be within ten years of the PhD and have published their thesis as a monograph.

grants.name: Wenner-Gren Dissertation Fieldwork Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Twice yearly: 1 May (projects starting January to June of the following year) and 1 November (July to December). Portal opens two months before each deadline.
grants.amount: Up to USD 25,000
grants.description: Supports dissertation fieldwork in anthropology (sociocultural, linguistic, biological and archaeology). Applicants must be enrolled in a doctoral programme with an anthropology connection and complete all non-dissertation requirements before the grant starts.

grants.name: Wenner-Gren Post-PhD Research Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline of 1 May for grants starting January to December of the following year.
grants.amount: Up to USD 25,000
grants.description: Research grant for scholars holding a doctorate in anthropology, or a related doctorate with an appointment in an anthropology department. Open to independent and senior scholars; no overhead is paid.

grants.name: Wenner-Gren Wadsworth International Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: 1 March for fellowships beginning the following academic year; home and host sponsor letters due by the same date.
grants.region: Applicants from countries with limited anthropology training opportunities (not high-income countries); study must be abroad
grants.amount: USD 20,000 per year
grants.duration: Up to 3 years, plus an optional write-up year
grants.description: Supports doctoral training in anthropology at a university outside the applicant's home country. Applicants need a pending doctoral application, a home sponsor and a host sponsor, and cannot already hold an anthropology doctorate.

grants.name: Charles Wallace India Trust Research Grants
grants.region: Indian citizens resident in India, aged 25 to 45
grants.amount: GBP 1,900 towards UK stay costs (international travel not covered)
grants.description: Short research visits to the UK, mainly for archival work, in history, literature, archaeology, history of art, philosophy and the performing and creative arts. Doctoral candidates in their final stages may apply; economics, anthropology, development studies, law and science are not covered.
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 28 February 2027. Final-stage Indian doctoral students at UK universities receive GBP 700.

grants.name: CWIT Visiting Curatorial Research Fellowship 2027 (V&A and Alkazi Foundation)
grants.funder: Charles Wallace India Trust, Victoria and Albert Museum and Alkazi Foundation for the Arts
grants.deadlineNote: The call closed on 16 November 2026. Results are due February 2027 and the fellowship starts April 2027. The next call is expected around late 2027.
grants.region: Indian citizens domiciled in India, aged 25 to 45
grants.amount: GBP 1,600 per month stipend, GBP 800 towards airfare, visa costs covered
grants.description: Residency at the V&A in London for mid-career artists, scholars, writers, editors and curators to research a curatorial project. Individual applicants only.

grants.name: Charles Wallace India Trust Visiting Fellowships (UK universities)
grants.deadlineNote: No general deadline; each UK host (CRASSH Cambridge, Durham IAS, Edinburgh IASH, King's India Institute, Leeds, Queen's Belfast, UEA, Kent, Stirling, V&A) advertises its own call through the year. Check the CWIT page for current links.
grants.region: Indian citizens resident in India, aged 25 to 45 (no upper limit for translators)
grants.amount: Varies by host; typically a monthly stipend plus a travel contribution
grants.description: Around a dozen hosted fellowships at UK universities for Indian historians, social scientists, writers and translators. Applicants need a postgraduate degree or five years of professional or academic experience and no CWIT grant in the previous five years.

grants.name: South Asia Institute Heidelberg / Max Weber Forum Delhi Research Fellowship 2027
grants.funder: South Asia Institute, Heidelberg University, with the Max Weber Forum for South Asian Studies (Max Weber Stiftung), New Delhi
grants.deadlineNote: Online portal only; closes 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET, with selection by the end of 2026. Fellowship starts between April and June 2027. Applicants should hold a doctorate.
grants.region: Young researchers from India, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka or Bangladesh
grants.amount: EUR 1,200 per month, rent paid, up to EUR 1,500 for travel
grants.description: Short residency at Heidelberg's South Asia Institute to start or develop a research collaboration. Open to PhD holders in ethnology, history, political science, economics, geography, modern South Asian languages and literatures, and cultural and religious history.

grants.name: Japan Foundation Japanese Studies Fellowship (FY2027)
grants.funder: The Japan Foundation (applications for India via JF New Delhi)
grants.deadlineNote: JF New Delhi deadline is 1 December 2026, 1:00 PM JST. Arrival in Japan must fall between 20 June 2027 and 20 March 2028.
grants.region: International (citizens or residents of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan)
grants.amount: Return airfare plus monthly stipend and allowances
grants.duration: PhD candidates 4 to 12 months; researchers 21 to 89 days or 4 to 12 months
grants.description: Funds research visits to Japan for doctoral candidates and researchers working on Japan-related topics, including comparative work, in the humanities and social sciences. Natural sciences, medicine and engineering are excluded, and affiliation in Japan must be arranged before applying.

grants.name: Ministry of Culture Senior and Junior Fellowships in the Field of Culture
grants.funder: Ministry of Culture, Government of India (administered by CCRT)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026-27 batch accepted offline applications until 31 July 2026; the next batch is expected around June to July 2027.
grants.amount: Senior: Rs 20,000 per month; Junior fellowships also offered
grants.description: Up to 200 senior (age above 40) and 200 junior fellowships each year for research projects in performing, visual and literary arts and in newer areas such as Indology, epigraphy, sociology of culture and cultural economics. Graduation is the minimum qualification for the newer research areas.

grants.name: IFA Arts Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. The 2026 call closed 10 August 2026; the next call is expected in mid-2027.
grants.region: Indian nationals only (PIO and OCI holders not eligible)
grants.amount: Up to Rs 5,00,000
grants.description: Grants to individuals (or joint applicants) for research on the arts in India, across disciplines and forms. Organisations cannot apply, and honoraria are capped at 35% of the budget.

grants.name: SANDEE Research Grants (Environmental and Climate Economics)
grants.funder: South Asian Network for Development and Environmental Economics (SANDEE), ICIMOD
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call for concept notes. The 2026 cycle closed 31 December 2025; shortlisted applicants attend a proposal workshop. Watch for the next call.
grants.region: South Asia and the Hindu Kush Himalaya
grants.amount: Typically USD 20,000 to 30,000
grants.description: Research grants on the economics of climate risk, natural resource use, ecosystem management and greener development policy. Open to academics, researchers and practitioners in South Asia, with priority for multidisciplinary and transboundary projects.

grants.name: CSIR Emeritus Scientist Scheme
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling: online applications accepted at any time of the year; the standing committee generally meets twice a year.
grants.amount: Scientist allowance of Rs 20,000 per month, plus contingency grant and research fellows/associates
grants.duration: 3 years, extendable by 2 (up to age 65; up to 70 for SSB awardees and fellows of INSA, IASc, NASI, INAE)
grants.description: Support for superannuated scientists who have been active in research in the five years before retirement to continue research at a host institution in India. Proposals are submitted through the host institution's executive authority.

grants.name: CSIR Senior Research Fellowship (SRF-Direct)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications are invited once a year through a press advertisement and the CSIR-HRDG website; no dated call for 2026-27 found yet.
grants.amount: CSIR SRF stipend plus HRA and contingency
grants.description: Direct award of a Senior Research Fellowship, without the NET route, to candidates with an MSc/BE/BTech plus research experience and an SCI publication, or an MTech/ME, MBBS/BDS or equivalent. Upper age limit 32 years, with relaxations for women and reserved categories. Tenable at universities and recognised institutions in India.

grants.name: Keystone Symposia Scholarships
grants.funder: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology
grants.deadlineNote: Each meeting has its own scholarship deadline, listed on the meeting page. Examples: Vaccinology (19 Jan 2027), Host-Pathogen Interactions (23 Feb 2027).
grants.amount: Up to USD 1,500 (reimbursement of airfare, ground transport, lodging and part of registration)
grants.description: Travel support for graduate students and postdocs (within 8 years of PhD/MD/DVM) to attend a Keystone Symposia conference in person and present a poster. No nationality restriction is stated; a mentor letter and abstract are required.

grants.name: GRC Carl Storm Opportunity Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Per conference; chairs select fellows at least two months before each meeting. Apply through a myGRC account.
grants.amount: Full registration support (one fellow per conference)
grants.description: Registration support for researchers attending a Gordon Research Conference for the first time who can show how attending would advance their career or access to opportunities in their field. No nationality restriction is stated.

grants.name: Biochemical Society General Travel Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Four rounds a year (1 March, 1 June, 1 September, 1 November) for events starting a month after each deadline.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 500 (national) or GBP 1,000 (international) events
grants.description: Travel and accommodation support for members to attend conferences or training events with a molecular bioscience focus. Open to Postgraduate, Early Career, Full and Emeritus members of at least 12 months' standing anywhere in the world; an accepted abstract is required.

grants.name: Biochemical Society Lab Visit Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Four rounds a year (1 March, 1 June, 1 September, 1 November); apply up to six months before the visit.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 2,000
grants.description: Travel and accommodation for members visiting another laboratory for molecular bioscience research or training. Open to members of at least 12 months' standing anywhere in the world.

grants.name: Boehringer Ingelheim Fonds Travel Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling: apply no later than six weeks and no earlier than six months before departure.
grants.region: Global (non-European citizens must use the grant to work in Europe)
grants.amount: Lump sum for travel, lodging and course fees; extra living costs possible for applicants from very low-income countries
grants.description: Support for PhD/MD students and postdocs in experimental basic biomedical research to visit another laboratory or attend a hands-on methods course. Indian researchers are eligible for stays in European labs; eligibility also depends on years since university entrance (11 years for students, 13 for postdocs).

grants.name: ICTP/IAEA Sandwich Training Educational Programme (STEP)
grants.funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) and IAEA
grants.deadlineNote: Applications open in November and close 28 February 2027; candidate and home-supervisor parts are both due by the deadline.
grants.region: Developing countries (India eligible as a developing country; confirm with step@ictp.it)
grants.amount: EUR 1,400 per month stipend during host stays, plus travel and medical insurance
grants.duration: Several months per year for up to three years
grants.description: Sandwich fellowships for PhD students enrolled at a home university in a developing country to spend research periods at a host institute abroad, in ICTP research areas (including mathematics and condensed matter physics) or IAEA areas such as medical radiation physics and nuclear sciences.

grants.name: Gruber International Prizes in Cosmology, Genetics and Neuroscience (2027 nominations)
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations for all 2027 prizes close 15 December 2026.
grants.amount: USD 500,000 per prize
grants.description: Nominations are invited for researchers whose work in cosmology, genetics or neuroscience has produced fundamental shifts in knowledge. Nominations are submitted online.

grants.name: NOSTER & Science Microbiome Prize 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Application period 15 October 2026 to 14 February 2027.
grants.amount: Cash prize and essay publication in Science
grants.description: Essay prize for early-career researchers (MD and/or PhD awarded within the last 10 years) for microbiome research. Entrants submit an essay describing their research.

grants.name: Kavli Prize (Astrophysics, Nanoscience, Neuroscience) nominations
grants.funder: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters / Kavli Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: Biennial open call; the 2026 call closed 1 October 2025. The next call (for the 2028 prizes) is expected in 2027.
grants.amount: USD 1 million per field
grants.description: Anyone may nominate living scientists whose basic research has transformed astrophysics, nanoscience or neuroscience; self-nominations are not accepted. Nominations carry over for two further cycles.

grants.name: Breakthrough Prizes and New Horizons Prizes in Fundamental Physics and Life Sciences (nominations)
