grants.deadlineNote: Nominations accepted only during the annual open nominations period announced on the Breakthrough Prize site.
grants.amount: Breakthrough Prize and New Horizons Prize amounts as set by the Foundation (New Horizons in Physics: USD 100,000)
grants.description: Anyone may nominate candidates for the Breakthrough Prizes in Fundamental Physics and Life Sciences; the New Horizons in Physics Prize targets researchers generally within 12 years of PhD. Self-nominations are not allowed and a third-party letter is required.

grants.name: Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar, Vigyan Team)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual nominations on the National Awards Portal; the 2026 window ran 28 March to 11 May 2026. Next cycle expected in early 2027.
grants.description: National science awards that replaced the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize and other ministry awards. The Vigyan Yuva-SSB award has an age limit of 45; self-nominations were accepted in 2026.

grants.name: NIVEA CONNECT 2026 Gen Z Research
grants.funder: NIVEA CONNECT and Social Connection Institute
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 11 December 2026.
grants.amount: EUR 20,000-30,000 per award
grants.description: Seed grants for early-stage research on social connection among Gen Z (roughly ages 14-29), including pilot, exploratory and feasibility studies, methodological development, and targeted additions to existing research programmes.

grants.name: Understanding, Modelling and Prediction of Extreme Events in a Changing Climate (MoES-EU Horizon Europe)
grants.funder: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, with the European Union (Horizon Europe)
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals close 4 March 2027. Indian entities join an EU consortium as Associated Partners.
grants.amount: Up to INR 2 crore per project (MoES share)
grants.description: Research on past and present climate extremes and their cascading impacts, high-resolution modelling and attribution, and multi-hazard prediction and early warning using integrated datasets, digital twins and AI. Open to Indian academic and research institutions, private R&D institutions with three years of research experience, and research-focused non-profits; links with Copernicus, Destination Earth and the EU Mission on Adaptation are encouraged.

grants.name: IEA Research and Policy Grant for Early Career Researchers
grants.funder: International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA) and European Commission (DG EAC)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 1 December 2026.
grants.amount: EUR 20,000 per project
grants.description: Supports comparative secondary analysis of IEA international large-scale assessment data on basic skills, teacher preparedness, or learning outcomes and inequalities, with EU policy relevance. Open to PhD candidates and researchers of any nationality within five years of their first doctorate; PhD candidates and applicants new to these datasets need a supervisor.

grants.name: Sea Level Investigation and Management Program Call for Proposals
grants.funder: Salata Institute for Climate and Sustainability, Harvard University
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals close 11 January 2027.
grants.amount: Exploratory: up to USD 50,000; project: USD 100,000-400,000; instrumented experiment: up to USD 1 million
grants.description: Funds research on storing water on or within land to slow sea-level rise, covering technical feasibility, geologic and freshwater storage, environmental impacts, economics, governance, law, politics and ethics. Faculty at universities and non-profit research institutions may apply, with external awards made as Harvard subawards; postdocs and graduate students may lead exploratory proposals with a faculty co-signature.

grants.name: CASI Sangam Grants for Collaborative Penn-India Research
grants.funder: Center for the Advanced Study of India (CASI), University of Pennsylvania
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals close 1 February 2027.
grants.amount: USD 2,000-8,000 per project
grants.description: Seed or self-contained collaborative projects such as pilot experiments, original surveys and focused studies. Each proposal needs a Penn-based PI and an India-based PI working at an Indian university or research organisation; projects on climate and energy, urbanisation, inclusive governance, or AI and technology get a small preference.

grants.name: Biswas Family Foundation Fast Grants (AI and Health)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 December 2026.
grants.description: Fast, high-risk seed funding at the intersection of AI and health, including models of biomedical data, datasets, AI tools or agents, and pilot experiments. Open to academic researchers worldwide at any career stage; non-US institutions must qualify as the equivalent of a US public charity or receive funds through a US 501(c)(3) intermediary, and undergraduates are limited to the USD 25,000 tier.

grants.name: ANRF Translational Research and Innovation (ATRI) Centres
grants.deadlineNote: Pre-proposal call extended to 23 November 2026, 5 pm IST, per the ANRF Online news ticker. Shortlisted teams are invited to submit full proposals.
grants.amount: Mode I(a): projects of INR 50-200+ crore with ANRF paying up to 50% or INR 100 crore; Mode I(b): INR 10-50 crore with ANRF paying up to 70% or INR 25 crore
grants.description: Co-funded centres that take a technology from TRL 4 to TRL 7 with at least one committed industry partner. The lead PI must hold a regular position at a recognised academic institution or national laboratory, and the balance of the cost comes from industry or other non-ANRF sources.

grants.name: ANRF Financial Assistance for Seminars, Symposia and Workshops (SSY)
grants.deadlineNote: Open all year. Apply online between 150 and 30 days before the event's start date.
grants.amount: INR 1-2 lakh (small meetings), INR 2-5 lakh (standard meetings), INR 5-10 lakh (major meetings, up to INR 20 lakh for flagship workshops and top international conferences in India)
grants.description: Partial support for scientific conferences, schools, workshops and focused meetings held in India. Applicants must be Indian citizens with a regular position at a recognised academic institution or R&D organisation; at most two events per person per year.

grants.name: ICHR Grants for Seminars, Workshops and Conferences
grants.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline; applications in the prescribed form are placed before ICHR's Research Projects Committee as they arrive.
grants.amount: Up to INR 3.5 lakh per event for individual coordinators (up to INR 5 lakh for registered associations of historians)
grants.description: Support for seminars, workshops and academic conferences on themes in history, paid through the coordinator's host institution. One grant per department or individual per financial year, with preference for history departments.

grants.name: ICHR Research Project Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Applications accepted on a rolling basis; presentation-cum-interviews are held twice a year, in June and December.
grants.amount: Up to INR 5 lakh
grants.description: Two-year project grants for research in history undertaken in India, awarded to a PhD-holding project director (individual category) or to institutions with a record of historical research (institutional category).

grants.name: Promotion of Science Education (POSE) Scholarship 2026-27
grants.funder: Haryana State Council for Science, Innovation & Technology (HSCSIT)
grants.deadlineNote: Online portal open 12 November 2026 to 12 January 2027 on the Har-Chhatravratti portal.
grants.amount: INR 4,000/month in years 1-3 and INR 6,000/month in years 4-5, plus a one-time mentorship grant of INR 12,000-22,000 (2025-26 rates)
grants.duration: Up to the end of the undergraduate or integrated master's programme
grants.description: Scholarship for first-year students in BSc, BS or integrated MSc/MS programmes in basic and natural sciences. Applicants must have passed Class X and XII from a school in Haryana (80% Haryana Board or 85% CBSE/ICSE in Class XII) or hold a Haryana Residence Certificate; 250 awards.

grants.name: ASEAN-India Collaborative R&D Scheme
grants.funder: ASEAN-India Science & Technology Development Fund (DST, Ministry of External Affairs and ANRF)
grants.deadlineNote: The portal accepts online proposals with no deadline currently stated; an older 1 April to 30 September annual window appears only in retired page text.
grants.amount: Travel (economy airfare and INR 7,000/day hospitality), up to INR 5 lakh/year for consumables and equipment add-ons, one postdoc salary, and 5% overheads to the Indian institution
grants.description: Joint R&D projects between an Indian PI and PIs from at least two ASEAN member states, in priority areas such as AI and HPC, marine science, materials, agriculture and food technology, and cyber-physical systems. PIs must hold a PhD and a regular post at a UGC-recognised university or publicly funded lab and be 60 or younger.

grants.name: MoSPI Grant-in-Aid for Research Studies and Seminars on Official Statistics
grants.funder: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
grants.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline; proposals in the prescribed formats go to MoSPI under the Capacity Development Scheme and are reviewed by a screening committee. Travel grant applications must reach MoSPI at least six months before the event.
grants.amount: Research studies up to INR 50 lakh (up to INR 1 crore in exceptional cases); seminars up to INR 10 lakh (national) or INR 20 lakh (international)
grants.description: Funds studies and surveys that fill data gaps in official statistics, plus seminars and workshops on official statistics and travel grants to present papers abroad. Applicant institutions must have worked in official statistics for at least three years with qualified statisticians, economists or social scientists.

grants.name: Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Science Program 2027
grants.funder: Weizmann Institute of Science (Feinberg Graduate School), Israel
grants.deadlineNote: Online application opens 20 December 2026 and closes 20 January 2027; results usually in March.
grants.amount: USD 1,100 stipend, flight subsidy up to USD 400, free dormitory housing, partial meals and medical insurance
grants.description: Eight-week summer research placement in a Weizmann lab for bachelor's and master's students in the physical, chemical and life sciences, mathematics or computer science who have finished at least their first year. Requires GPA of 3.6/4.0 or equivalent; PhD students are not eligible.

grants.name: OIST Research Internship Program (Fall 2027 round)
grants.funder: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University (OIST), Japan
grants.deadlineNote: Fall 2027 round closes 15 April 2027, 23:59 JST (internship between 1 October 2027 and 31 March 2028). The spring 2027 round closed on 15 October 2026. Schedule marked tentative.
grants.amount: Daily internship allowance and support set by OIST; 5,000 JPY application fee
grants.description: Research internship in an OIST research unit for students in the last two years of a bachelor's degree, master's students, and recent bachelor's or master's graduates. Current or former PhD students are not eligible, and enrolled students need approval from their home institution.

grants.name: MSCA Staff Exchanges 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Call HORIZON-MSCA-2027-SE-01-01 opens 15 December 2026; proposals due 13 April 2027; results July 2027.
grants.region: EU and Horizon Europe associated countries; Indian institutions can join as associated partners
grants.amount: Unit costs per person-month of secondment (see call text)
grants.duration: Up to 4 years per project; secondments of 1 to 12 months
grants.description: Funds consortia of universities, research organisations and companies to exchange research and innovation staff across borders and sectors. Indian organisations can take part as associated partners hosting or sending staff, but India is not automatically eligible for EU funding, so the consortium must be led and funded through European beneficiaries.

grants.name: Safe Operating Space for Antarctica and the Southern Ocean (MoES-EU Horizon Europe)
grants.funder: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, with the European Union (Horizon Europe)
grants.deadlineNote: Horizon Europe topic HORIZON-CL6-2027-02-CLIMATE-04 opens 20 April 2027 and closes 23 September 2027, 17:00 CET.
grants.region: India (as associated partners in EU consortia)
grants.amount: MoES grant-in-aid up to INR 2 crore per project for the Indian side
grants.description: Second theme of the India-EU co-funding initiative on climate and polar research, covering the Antarctic cryosphere and Southern Ocean systems. Indian institutions join an EU consortium as associated partners and are funded by MoES rather than the EU; they may lead work packages but not coordinate.

grants.name: Mozilla Foundation Fellowships 2027-2028
grants.deadlineNote: Letter of intent due 17 December 2026, 11:59 PM Pacific. Invited full applications due 12 March 2027.
grants.region: Global, subject to legal eligibility to receive Mozilla funding
grants.amount: Up to USD 125,000 per fellowship (about 10 awards)
grants.description: Fellowships for technologists, researchers and builders working toward a more trustworthy and open technology future, in an Embedded or an Independent track. Most review happens at the letter of intent stage; applications must be in English.

grants.name: A*STAR Research Attachment Programme (ARAP)
grants.funder: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), Singapore
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations close 1 June and 1 December each year; the attachment starts at least 6 months after the deadline.
grants.region: International (Singapore); open to overseas PhD students, including those at Indian universities (past awardees include IIT Bombay)
grants.amount: S$3,600 monthly stipend, S$300 housing allowance, airfare, settling-in, IT and conference allowances; tuition not covered
grants.description: Lets PhD students at overseas universities spend 1 to 2 years doing part of their doctoral research in an A*STAR institute, co-supervised by an A*STAR scientist. Students are jointly nominated by the home university and the A*STAR supervisor; students at non-partner universities go through the ARAP-Individual route, so the A*STAR supervisor must be found first.

grants.name: Yenching Academy Scholars Program (September 2027 intake)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the September 2027 intake close 30 November 2026; the Peking University graduate application must also be completed.
grants.region: International (China; open to international candidates including Indian nationals)
grants.amount: Full fellowship (tuition, accommodation and stipend)
grants.duration: Master's programme in China Studies (about 2 years)
grants.description: Fully funded interdisciplinary master's programme in China Studies at Peking University for graduates from any discipline. Open to international candidates and applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan.

grants.name: Clarendon Scholarships (University of Oxford, 2027-28 entry)
grants.deadlineNote: No separate application; applicants who submit their Oxford graduate application by the course's December 2026 or January 2027 funding deadline (for many courses 12 midday UK time on 7 January 2027) are considered. Some courses have earlier December deadlines.
grants.region: International (UK; open to all nationalities including India)
grants.amount: Full course fees plus a living-costs grant
grants.duration: Full length of the graduate course
grants.description: Merit scholarships for graduate study (master's and DPhil) at Oxford in all subjects, with over 100 new awards each year. Selection is based on academic excellence and potential, and is automatic for applicants who meet their course's funding deadline.

grants.name: Felix Scholarships for Indian Students (SOAS, 2027 entry)
grants.funder: Felix Trust, with SOAS University of London (also offered at Oxford and Reading)
grants.deadlineNote: SOAS scholarship application closes 11:59 AM UK time on 26 February 2027; a firm offer of admission is needed. Oxford and Reading run their own Felix deadlines.
grants.region: India only (Indian nationals living in India)
grants.amount: Full tuition, living costs and return airfare
grants.description: Scholarships for Indian nationals with a first-class bachelor's degree and financial need to take a full-time master's or PhD at SOAS. Applicants who have studied outside India for a year or more, or hold a non-Indian degree, are not eligible.

grants.name: Cambridge Trust and University of Cambridge Postgraduate Scholarships (2027-28 entry)
grants.funder: Cambridge Trust and University of Cambridge
grants.deadlineNote: Main University funding deadlines are 8 December 2026 and 6 January 2027 (23:59 GMT, references included); the course page states which applies. Applicants are considered for most Cambridge Trust awards through the graduate application.
grants.region: International (UK; Indian nationals eligible, including India-specific Cambridge Trust awards)
grants.amount: Full-cost and part-cost scholarships (fees and maintenance)
grants.duration: Full length of the master's or PhD course
grants.description: Cambridge Trust and departmental scholarships for master's and PhD study at Cambridge, awarded through the main graduate application by the funding deadline. Separate from Gates Cambridge, which is listed on its own.

grants.name: IKI Small Grants 8th Call (Nature-based Solutions)
grants.funder: International Climate Initiative (IKI), German Federal Ministry for the Environment, implemented by GIZ
grants.deadlineNote: Call open 15 November 2026 to 8 January 2027, 23:59 CET.
grants.region: Non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible developing and emerging countries (India is on the OECD DAC list)
grants.amount: EUR 60,000 to 200,000 per project
grants.description: Grants to local and national non-profit organisations for nature-based solutions that protect, manage or restore ecosystems while benefiting people and biodiversity. Applicants need at least three years of experience and annual revenue of EUR 60,000 to 500,000, so it suits university-linked NGOs and field partners rather than universities themselves.

grants.name: ICSSR Doctoral Fellowships (Full-Term, Short-Term and Contingency Grant)
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. The 2026-27 call opened 15 June 2026 and closed on 31 July 2026 after extensions; the next call is expected around June 2027.
grants.amount: Full-Term: Rs 20,000 per month plus Rs 20,000 per year contingency; Short-Term: six months of the same; Contingency Grant: Rs 62,500 one-time
grants.description: Fellowships for full-time PhD students in the social sciences registered at UGC-recognised universities, deemed universities, Institutes of National Importance or ICSSR institutes. Applicants must be 40 or younger (relaxation for reserved categories) with at least 55% in their master's degree.

grants.name: ICSSR Post-Doctoral Fellowship
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. The 2026-27 call ran from 22 June to 12 August 2026; the next call is expected around June 2027.
grants.region: India (Indian citizens, 45 or younger); fellow must affiliate with a publicly funded university, deemed university, INI or government research institute, so a private university cannot host
grants.amount: Rs 31,000 per month plus Rs 25,000 per year contingency
grants.description: Two-year fellowship for Indian social scientists with a PhD to work on research themes listed by ICSSR under a senior supervisor. The 2026-27 guidelines list priority themes across economics, governance, law, international affairs, education and culture.

grants.name: ICSSR Major and Minor Research Projects
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call, usually around April to June.
grants.region: India (faculty at UGC-recognised universities under 2(f) or 12(B), ICSSR institutes and INIs)
grants.amount: Minor: up to Rs 15 lakh; Major: up to Rs 30 lakh
grants.description: Research grants for permanently employed or retired faculty with a PhD to carry out social science research projects alongside their normal duties. Contractual researchers and independent scholars with strong publication records may join as co-project directors.

grants.name: ICSSR Research Programmes and Special Calls for Research Studies
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Research Programme calls are usually issued around April to June; special thematic calls appear through the year.
grants.region: India (Indian social scientists at eligible institutions)
grants.amount: Varies by call
grants.description: Larger collaborative, interdisciplinary research programmes on national issues, plus thematic calls such as longitudinal studies, women-led development, family systems and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups. Check each call for eligibility and budget.

grants.name: ICSSR Grants for National, International and Collaborative Seminars
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; apply online at least three months before the event.
grants.region: India (institutions including UGC-recognised universities under 2(f)/12(B); convener must be regular faculty with a PhD)
grants.amount: National up to Rs 8 lakh; International up to Rs 12 lakh; Collaborative Rs 5-10 lakh
grants.description: Partial support for institutions to organise social science seminars and conferences in India. International seminars need at least five foreign scholars as resource persons or paper contributors.

grants.name: ICSSR Participation in International Conference Abroad
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; apply at least three months before the conference.
grants.region: India (Indian scholars). Faculty must be at publicly funded institutions; postgraduate, PhD and postdoctoral scholars are eligible without that restriction.
grants.amount: Faculty: up to 50% of costs; students and postdocs without salary: full travel, visa, insurance, stay and registration up to USD 200
grants.description: Travel support for Indian social scientists invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad. A formal invitation letter is required, and repeat applications are considered only after three years.

grants.name: ICSSR Financial Assistance for Data Collection Abroad
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications accepted online throughout the year.
grants.region: India (Indian faculty at ICSSR institutes, INIs or UGC 12(B) institutions; Indian PhD and postdoctoral scholars)
grants.amount: Economy airfare, visa, insurance and maintenance at government norms
grants.description: Support for Indian social science scholars at an advanced stage of research to collect data or consult archives abroad. The visit must be academically justified for the ongoing research.

grants.name: ICSSR Yuva Shodh Pratibha Scheme (undergraduate research)
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026-27 call opened 6 June 2026 and closed 14 August 2026; the next call is expected around June 2027.
grants.region: India (students in four-year undergraduate programmes under NEP 2020)
grants.amount: Up to Rs 3 lakh per project
grants.description: Research grants for teams of two or three undergraduates in the sixth or seventh semester of a four-year programme, mentored by a regular faculty member. Each year has a theme; 2026-27 was Youth and Decolonisation.

grants.name: ICSSR Research Methodology Courses and Capacity Building Programmes
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Proposals invited through ICSSR calls; check the page for the current cycle.
grants.region: India (ICSSR institutes, INIs, UGC-recognised universities and colleges under 2(f)/12(B))
grants.amount: Varies by programme type
grants.description: Grants to social science departments to run research methodology courses for postgraduate, PhD and postdoctoral scholars, or capacity building programmes for early-career faculty.

grants.name: ICSSR Publication Grant / Subsidy for Publication
grants.funder: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Applications considered through the year; check the page for current guidelines.
grants.amount: Publication subsidy; amount set by ICSSR
grants.description: Financial subsidy to Indian nationals for publishing manuscripts of research work in any social science field.

grants.name: ICHR Junior Research Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Awarded through a periodic entrance examination and interview; no call is open now. Watch the ICHR notifications page.
grants.amount: Rs 17,600 per month plus Rs 16,500 per year contingency
grants.duration: 2 years, extendable by 1 year without funding
grants.description: Full-time fellowship for PhD students registered in History or allied subjects, selected through an entrance test followed by a presentation and interview.

grants.name: ICHR Contingency (Study-cum-Travel) Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling.
grants.region: India (Indian citizens and non-Indians researching history within India; Indians registered at foreign universities and NRIs are not eligible)
grants.amount: Up to Rs 60,000 for PhD students; larger sums by committee decision
grants.description: Grants for travel and contingency expenses for research on history within India, for PhD students (after six months of registration), postdocs, independent researchers and university teachers not receiving other support for the same work.

grants.name: ICHR Foreign Travel Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; apply at least three months before departure.
grants.amount: Travel and maintenance abroad
grants.description: Support for Indian historians to consult archives, museums and libraries abroad (PhD and MPhil scholars and above) or to present a paper at a conference abroad (PhD holders only). Archive visits need proof that the material is not available in India.

grants.name: ICHR Publication Subsidy
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling.
grants.amount: Subsidy set by the Research Projects Committee
grants.description: Subsidies for publishing works on history, including doctoral theses, monographs, conference proceedings, critical editions, translations of source material and journals.

grants.name: ICPR Fellowships (Junior Research, Post-Doctoral, Senior and National)
grants.funder: Indian Council of Philosophical Research (ICPR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call. Registration for the 2025-26 cycle closed on 17 January 2026; the next call is expected around December to January.
grants.amount: Varies by fellowship category
grants.description: Full-time fellowships for research in philosophy and related disciplines at four levels: Junior Research Fellowship, Post-Doctoral, Senior and National. ICPR lists priority areas including logic, philosophy of language, ethics, political philosophy and comparative philosophy.

grants.name: ICPR Grants for Seminars, Conferences and Workshops
grants.funder: Indian Council of Philosophical Research (ICPR), Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; application form and guidelines on the page.
grants.region: India (philosophy departments of Indian universities and research institutions)
grants.amount: Partial assistance; ICPR supports 25 to 50 seminars a year
grants.description: Partial funding for philosophy departments to organise seminars, symposia, workshops and dialogues. Selected papers may be published by ICPR or in its journal JICPR.

grants.name: IIAS Shimla Fellowships (Regular, Tagore and National Fellows)
grants.funder: Indian Institute of Advanced Study (IIAS), Shimla
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications accepted throughout the year and the selection committee usually meets twice a year.
grants.region: India and abroad (applications invited from all parts of India and from abroad)
grants.amount: Independent scholars: Rs 61,100 per month; in-service government fellows keep their pay. Rent-free accommodation and a study on campus.
grants.description: Residential fellowships for advanced, non-empirical research in the humanities, social sciences and foundational questions in the sciences at Rashtrapati Nivas, Shimla. Proposals involving fieldwork or data collection are not considered, and fellows are expected in residence from March to mid-December.

grants.name: PMML Fellowships and Scholar in Residence Programme
grants.funder: Prime Ministers' Museum and Library (PMML), New Delhi
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 call was advertised in early February with a deadline of 28 February 2026; expect the next call around January to February 2027.
grants.region: India (Scholar in Residence open to scholars worldwide)
grants.amount: Varies by fellowship; Scholar in Residence Rs 1 lakh lump sum
grants.description: Fellowships for research on modern and contemporary India, including post-independence domestic issues, India in the global context and democracy and statecraft, plus the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Fellowship on Prime Ministers of India. Applications are sent by email as a single PDF.

grants.name: Tagore National Fellowship for Cultural Research
grants.funder: Ministry of Culture, Government of India
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026-27 call was advertised in June with a deadline of 15 July 2026; expect the next call around June 2027.
grants.region: India (open to Indian and foreign nationals)
grants.amount: Tagore National Fellows: Rs 80,000 per month; Tagore Research Scholars: Rs 50,000 per month
grants.description: Up to 15 fellowships and 25 scholarships a year for research projects using the collections of Ministry of Culture institutions such as museums, archives, IGNCA and the Archaeological Survey. Applications go to the nodal institution whose resources the project depends on.

grants.name: Scholarships to Young Artistes in Different Cultural Fields (SYA)
grants.funder: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), Ministry of Culture
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026-27 batch closed on 31 July 2026 (offline applications by post); expect the next call around June 2027.
grants.amount: Rs 5,000 per month
grants.description: 400 scholarships a year for advanced training within India in Indian classical music and dance, theatre, mime, visual arts, folk and traditional arts, and light classical music, under a guru or institution.

grants.name: IFA Arts Practice Grants (Explorations, Productions and Arts Platforms)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle of separate calls: Explorations (deadline 30 April in 2026), Productions (5 June in 2026) and Arts Platforms (31 August in 2026).
grants.region: India (practitioners based in India; check each call)
grants.amount: Explorations up to Rs 1 lakh; Productions up to Rs 5 lakh; honorarium capped at 35% of budget
grants.duration: Up to 6 months (Explorations); up to 18 months (Productions)
grants.description: Grants for artists, writers and curators to experiment beyond their current practice, from early-stage explorations to full productions and collective platforms such as workshops and residencies. Proposals may be written in any Indian language.

grants.name: IFA Archives and Museums Programme (Creative and Scholarly Projects)
grants.funder: India Foundation for the Arts (IFA), with partner museums and archives
grants.deadlineNote: Calls are issued for specific partner collections through the year; the 2026 Folk Culture Museum, Bhimtal call closed 11 September 2026.
grants.amount: Varies by call
grants.description: Grants for arts practitioners and researchers to create new critical and creative public engagements with a named archive or museum collection in India.

grants.name: NIF Translation Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: NIF states the next round will open in 2027. Round 3 ran from 1 August to 31 December 2025.
grants.region: Indian citizens and PIOs fluent in English and one of the listed languages
grants.amount: Rs 6 lakh per fellow
grants.description: Fellowships to translate significant non-fiction works on India published from 1850 onwards from Assamese, Bangla, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Marathi, Malayalam, Odia, Tamil or Urdu into English.

grants.name: Ishibashi Foundation / Japan Foundation Fellowship for Research on Japanese Art (FY2027)
grants.funder: The Japan Foundation and Ishibashi Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: 1 p.m. Japan Standard Time, via the JF online portal; applicants in India apply through JF New Delhi.
grants.region: Individuals living outside Japan (nationals of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan)
grants.amount: Round-trip airfare plus stipend and allowances
grants.duration: 21 to 59 days in Japan, starting between 20 June 2027 and 31 March 2028
grants.description: Short research stays in Japan for curators, researchers, educators and conservators working on Japanese visual arts, with emphasis on contemporary art. Priority goes to projects that plan exhibitions or publications abroad.

grants.name: Japan Foundation Grant Program for Japanese Studies Projects (FY2027)
grants.deadlineNote: 1 p.m. Japan Standard Time, via the JF online portal.
grants.region: Non-profit universities and research institutions outside Japan
grants.amount: Partial support for travel, meetings, honoraria and materials
grants.description: Grants to overseas universities and research institutions for Japanese studies projects run between April 2027 and March 2028, such as conferences, research, guest lectures and library acquisitions. Natural sciences and arts activities are not eligible.

grants.name: Japan Foundation Japanese-Language Program for Specialists in Cultural and Academic Fields (FY2027)
grants.deadlineNote: 1 p.m. Japan Standard Time; applications through the JF online portal.
grants.region: Researchers, librarians and curators employed outside Japan, and master's or PhD students at universities outside Japan writing a thesis on Japan
grants.amount: Training in Japan (programme covers participation)
grants.description: Six-month Japanese-language course in Osaka for researchers, graduate students, librarians and curators who need Japanese for their research or specialist work.

grants.name: Korea Foundation Fellowship for Field Research
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027 round ran from 19 August to 14 October 2026; expect the next round around August to October 2027.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend (KRW 2.3 million for doctoral candidates in 2026) plus entry allowance and insurance
grants.description: Fellowships for PhD candidates writing their dissertations (Type A) and faculty or PhD holders (Type B) in Korean studies or related humanities and social science fields to do field research in Korea.

grants.name: MOFA Taiwan Fellowship
grants.funder: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan); administered by the Center for Chinese Studies, National Central Library
grants.deadlineNote: Annual, open 1 May to 30 June each year; the 2028 round is expected in May to June 2027.
grants.region: Foreign scholars and doctoral students at universities and institutions outside Taiwan
grants.amount: NT$60,000 per month (professors and research fellows) or NT$50,000 per month (assistant professors, postdocs, doctoral students), plus airfare and insurance
grants.description: Research residencies in Taiwan for work on Taiwan studies, cross-strait relations, the Asia-Pacific region and Sinology, with emphasis on the humanities and social sciences.

grants.name: Sumitomo Foundation Grant for the Protection of Cultural Properties Outside Japan (FY2026)
grants.deadlineNote: Application period 1 October to 30 November 2026, through the foundation's website.
grants.region: Outside Japan (owners or administrators of cultural properties, or researchers conducting preliminary surveys)
grants.amount: JPY 35 million in total for about 15 projects
grants.description: Grants for the protection, preservation and restoration of tangible cultural properties such as fine arts, murals, sculptures and excavated archaeological materials outside Japan, and for preliminary surveys linked to such work. Digital preservation projects and whole-site restoration are not covered.

grants.name: Sumitomo Foundation Grant for Japan-Related Research Projects
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The FY2026 round ran from 1 September to 30 October 2026; expect the next round in September to October 2027.
grants.region: Researchers of Asian (non-Japanese) nationality living outside Japan
grants.amount: JPY 50 million in total for about 70 projects
grants.description: Grants for individual or group research in the social sciences or humanities related to Japan, aimed at mutual understanding between Asian countries and Japan. Applications may be in English or Japanese.

grants.name: J-PAL South Asia Indian Scholars Program
grants.funder: Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) South Asia
grants.deadlineNote: Funding is offered through periodic requests for proposals; no round is listed as open now. Register in J-PAL's South Asian Scholars Database for notices.
grants.region: India (PhD holders with a research or teaching position at an Indian university)
grants.amount: Varies by RFP (proposal development, pilot and rapid evaluation grants)
grants.description: Support for India-based researchers in economics, public policy, public health and related empirical fields to develop and run randomised evaluations, including proposal development grants, pilots and rapid RCTs, plus training and mentoring.

grants.name: Serendipity Arts Residency
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 open call ran from 3 February to 11 March 2026; expect the next call around February 2027.
grants.region: India (Indian citizens aged 35 or under who have lived in India for the past two years)
grants.amount: Production grant Rs 80,000 plus Rs 12,000 per month allowance and furnished accommodation
grants.duration: 3 months (May to August) in New Delhi
grants.description: Studio residency in New Delhi for young Indian artists across disciplines, with mentorship, accommodation and a production grant. Applicants who attended any residency in the past year are not eligible.

grants.name: Prince Claus Fund Seed Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual open call; the 2026 call closed on 8 January 2026. Watch the page for the next call.
grants.region: Individuals from, living and working in eligible countries in Africa, Asia (India included), Latin America, the Caribbean and Eastern Europe
grants.description: Awards for 100 early-career artists and cultural practitioners (1 to 5 years of practice) whose work addresses pressing social and political issues in their local context. Mid-career artists can apply to the separate Fellows Award (EUR 10,000).

grants.name: Lalit Kala Akademi Scholarships for Young Artists
grants.funder: Lalit Kala Akademi (National Academy of Art), Ministry of Culture
grants.deadlineNote: Awarded annually; no current call is posted. Watch the Akademi's notices.
grants.amount: Rs 20,000 per month
grants.description: Up to 75 scholarships a year for young visual artists, who work at one of the Akademi's regional centres and submit monthly records of their work.

grants.name: UGC-NET Junior Research Fellowship (humanities and social sciences)
grants.funder: University Grants Commission (UGC), via the National Testing Agency (NTA)
grants.deadlineNote: Exam held twice a year (June and December cycles). Registration for the December 2026 cycle closed in late October 2026; the June 2027 cycle usually opens for registration around April to May.
grants.region: India (Indian nationals with a master's degree or in the final year)
grants.amount: UGC Junior Research Fellowship, upgraded to Senior Research Fellowship, at UGC rates
grants.description: National exam that awards the Junior Research Fellowship for PhD study and certifies eligibility for assistant professorships and PhD admission across humanities, social sciences, languages, commerce and related subjects. The fellowship can be held at UGC-recognised universities.

grants.name: Maple Bridge Research Fellowship 2026-27 (Canada-India youth policy research)
grants.funder: Swasti with Public Policy India and STRIDE, supported by the High Commission of Canada (CFLI); promoted by the Shastri India Canada Institute
grants.deadlineNote: Apply through the form linked on the page.
grants.region: Undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in institutions in India (20 places) or Canada (5 places)
grants.amount: No stipend stated; policy briefs are published and presented at the Maple Bridge Summit
grants.description: Virtual research fellowship in which teams of students co-author policy briefs on AI-linked themes such as trade, inclusive growth, energy, governance and student mobility. Open to students of any discipline.

grants.name: Asian Cultural Council Fellowships and Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027 cycle accepted applications from 1 October to 10 November 2026; expect the next cycle around October to November 2027.
grants.region: Eligible Asian countries including India (Indian applicants apply through ACC New York), and the United States
grants.amount: Individual Fellowship up to USD 35,000; New York Fellowship USD 38,000; Graduate Fellowship USD 15,000; Organization Grant up to USD 50,000
grants.description: Travel-based fellowships for research, creative work and exchange in the arts, covering fields such as art history, archaeology, conservation, curation, ethnomusicology, film, literature, museum studies, music, theatre and visual art. The Graduate Fellowship supports US-based graduate coursework.

grants.name: Kyoto University CSEAS Fellowship (Visiting Research Scholars)
grants.funder: Center for Southeast Asian Studies (CSEAS), Kyoto University
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027 call closed on 30 April 2026; expect the next call around spring 2027 for fellowships starting in 2028.
grants.region: No nationality restriction; established scholars under 65 (current graduate students and postdocs cannot apply)
grants.amount: Stipend for travel and living costs in Kyoto, plus research and domestic travel funds
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Kyoto for scholars and practitioners working on Southeast Asian area studies, including comparative and cross-regional projects. Fellows give a public lecture.

grants.name: Jamnalal Kaniram Bajaj Visiting Research Fellowship (Harvard Mittal Institute, Fall 2027)
grants.funder: Lakshmi Mittal and Family South Asia Institute, Harvard University
grants.deadlineNote: Applications and recommendation letters due Tuesday 8 December 2026.
grants.region: PhD holders; priority to scholars educated mainly in South Asia without past access to Harvard resources, working on India
grants.amount: Stipend prorated from USD 68,000 per year for the semester
grants.duration: Fall semester 2027 (about August to December) in Cambridge, MA
grants.description: One-semester residency at Harvard for a scholar researching India, ending in a seminar presentation. Applicants submit a research plan, CV and writing sample.

grants.name: Raghunathan Family Fellowship (Harvard Mittal Institute, AY 2027-28)
grants.funder: Lakshmi Mittal and Family South Asia Institute, Harvard University
grants.deadlineNote: The AY 2027-28 posting is open on Harvard's academic positions site but does not state a deadline; Mittal Institute fellowships in this cycle close in early December, so check the page soon.
grants.region: Early-career PhD holders (PhD within the past five years and by February 2027); priority to scholars educated mainly in South Asia
grants.amount: USD 68,000 for 12 months (prorated)
grants.description: Year-long residential fellowship at Harvard for an early-career scholar working on South Asia, with priority to those who have not previously had access to Harvard resources.

grants.name: NTICVA UK Visiting Fellowship (Indian art and heritage)
grants.funder: Nehru Trust for the Indian Collections at the Victoria and Albert Museum (NTICVA)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027-28 awards open in November 2026 with a closing date in February 2027, to be announced on the site.
grants.region: Indian citizens studying or early in their careers in the arts and heritage sector
grants.amount: Return airfare, visa and insurance, plus about GBP 1,850 per month maintenance
grants.description: Up to three fellowships a year for graduate students, PhD students, scholars and museum professionals based in India to study, research or train (including conservation) with Indian art collections at the V&A and other UK institutions. Some are jointly funded with the Charles Wallace India Trust.

grants.name: NTICVA UK Travel Award
grants.funder: Nehru Trust for the Indian Collections at the Victoria and Albert Museum (NTICVA)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027-28 awards open in November 2026 with a closing date in February 2027.
grants.region: Indian citizens who are students or work at museums, galleries or other arts and heritage institutions
grants.amount: Up to GBP 1,500 towards airfare and maintenance
grants.description: Up to three awards a year for India-based students, scholars and museum professionals to present at conferences or do short research visits in the UK on Indian art and cultural heritage.

grants.name: NTICVA Small Study and Research Grant (India)
grants.funder: Nehru Trust for the Indian Collections at the Victoria and Albert Museum (NTICVA)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027-28 awards open in November 2026 with a closing date in February 2027.
grants.region: Indian citizens (postgraduate students, scholars or professionals)
grants.amount: Up to Rs 50,000
grants.description: Small grants for short fieldwork within India and for research materials, for work on Indian art, archaeology, architecture, design, fashion and photography.

grants.name: IKS Division Competitive Research Proposals Program
grants.funder: Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) Division, Ministry of Education
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026-27 round closed on 30 January 2026; expect the next call around December 2026 to January 2027.
grants.amount: Up to Rs 25 lakh per project
grants.description: Catalytic grants, about 20 per round, for young and established researchers to start projects on Indian knowledge systems, including philosophical, linguistic, historical and scientific traditions. The Division also runs separate calls for IKS centres, internships and textbook writing.

grants.name: Pro Helvetia New Delhi Residencies and Research Trips (South Asia to Switzerland)
grants.funder: Pro Helvetia, Swiss Arts Council (New Delhi office)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual residency call; the call for 2027 residencies closed on 1 March 2026 and selections were announced in July 2026. Expect the next call in early 2027.
grants.region: Professional artists and cultural practitioners in India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Vietnam
grants.amount: Residency costs covered by Pro Helvetia
grants.description: Residencies and research trips in Switzerland for artists, curators and cultural practitioners from South Asia, plus support for exchange projects between the region and Switzerland.

grants.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Research Students (Embassy recommendation, India)
grants.funder: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan, via the Embassy of Japan in India
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027 round's preliminary applications ran from 20 April to 15 May 2026; expect the next round around April to May 2027.
grants.amount: Full tuition, monthly stipend and airfare
grants.description: Government scholarship for master's, doctoral or non-degree research study at Japanese universities in any field, including the humanities and social sciences. Selection is a two-step process: an online preliminary form, then a full application for shortlisted candidates.

grants.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) for Graduate Degrees (Embassy track, India)
grants.funder: Government of the Republic of Korea (NIIED), via the Embassy of Korea in New Delhi
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 graduate call was posted 3 February 2026 with a deadline of 25 February 2026; expect the 2027 call around February 2027.
grants.amount: Full scholarship for master's or doctoral study in Korea
grants.description: Korean government scholarship for graduate degrees at Korean universities in any field, applied for online through Study in Korea. A separate university track is also available.

grants.name: JF-Nichibunken Fellowship Program (2027-28)
grants.funder: The Japan Foundation and International Research Center for Japanese Studies (Nichibunken)
grants.deadlineNote: Submit the signed form by email to the Japan Foundation Japanese Studies Department by 1 December 2026 (JST).
grants.region: Post-doctoral researchers in Japanese studies outside Japan
grants.amount: Japan Foundation fellowship support; Nichibunken provides office, library and optional paid housing
grants.duration: More than 6 months up to 24 months, starting between 1 September 2027 and 1 March 2028
grants.description: About three fellowships for early-career post-doctoral researchers in Japanese studies to do full-time research at Nichibunken in Kyoto, while helping run workshops and meetings.

grants.name: Azim Premji University Health Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rounds were held in 2023 and 2025 (concept notes due 30 April 2025); no new round has been announced.
grants.region: India (researchers at public institutions and non-profit organisations; Azim Premji Foundation members are not eligible)
grants.amount: Rs 5 to 40 lakh (indicative)
grants.description: Grants for research on the health realities of vulnerable communities in India, with themes such as urban and rural poverty, public health systems and programmes, and gender and health. Social science and interdisciplinary teams are eligible.

grants.name: Consortium for History of Science, Technology and Medicine Research Fellowship
grants.funder: Consortium for History of Science, Technology and Medicine (CHSTM)
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year, 1 October and 1 April.
grants.region: Open to any nationality; research is carried out at CHSTM member collections, mostly in the United States
grants.amount: USD 1,000 plus USD 750 per collection visited
grants.description: Short research visits to the libraries and archives of CHSTM member institutions for work in the history of science, technology and medicine. There is no nationality or student-status requirement.

grants.name: Newberry Library Long-Term and Short-Term Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Long-term fellowships close 20 November 2026; short-term fellowships close 4 December 2026 (2027-28 cycle).
grants.region: Open to non-US citizens; the Newberry issues DS-2019 forms for J-1 visas
grants.amount: Monthly stipend (amount set by the Newberry)
grants.duration: Long-term 4-9 months; short-term up to a few months
grants.description: Residential fellowships for research in the Newberry's collections in history, literature, cartography, music and related humanities fields. Long-term fellowships require a PhD by the deadline; short-term fellowships are open to PhD holders and ABD doctoral candidates.

grants.name: Folger Institute Fellowships (Short-Term and Long-Term)
grants.deadlineNote: Long-term fellowships due 15 December 2026; short-term and artistic research fellowships due 15 January 2027 (11:59 pm ET).
grants.region: Short-term fellowships explicitly accept international equivalents of the terminal degree or ABD status; check the FAQ for long-term eligibility
grants.amount: Short-term USD 5,000 per month in residence (USD 4,000 virtual); long-term USD 35,000 (5 months) or USD 70,000 (9 months)
grants.description: Fellowships for research using the Folger's collections on early modern British and European history, literature, theatre and culture. Short-term fellowships can be held onsite, virtually or in combination.

grants.name: Science History Institute Beckman Center Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Deadline for 2027-28 fellowships is 15 January 2027; travel grants are reviewed on a rolling basis.
grants.region: Short-term, distinguished, dissertation and postdoctoral fellowships are open to any nationality
grants.amount: Monthly stipend
grants.duration: From one month (short-term) to 9-12 months (dissertation and postdoctoral)
grants.description: Residential fellowships for research on the history of science, technology, chemistry and medicine using the Institute's library, archives and museum collections. Postdoctoral applicants must defend by the end of July 2027.

grants.name: Linda Hall Library Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: All materials, including letters, due 19 January 2027 for 2027-28.
grants.region: Open to non-US citizens who can secure travel documents (the NEH fellowship requires US citizenship or three years' US residence)
grants.amount: USD 3,000 per month (doctoral students) or USD 4,200 per month (postdoctoral)
grants.description: Fellowships for research in the history of science, technology, engineering and medicine using the Linda Hall Library's collections. Doctoral students who have completed coursework and postdoctoral scholars may apply.

grants.name: Harry Frank Guggenheim Emerging Scholar Awards
grants.deadlineNote: Letter of interest opens 1 January and is due 1 February 2027; invited full applications due 15 March 2027.
grants.region: Citizens of any country studying at a university in any country
grants.description: Dissertation-completion awards for PhD candidates in their final year whose research addresses the causes, manifestations and control of violence and aggression. Social sciences, history and allied fields are eligible.

grants.name: Harry Frank Guggenheim Distinguished Scholar Awards
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. In 2026 the letter of interest was due 31 July and invited full applications 11 September; expect similar dates in 2027.
grants.region: Open to researchers of any nationality
grants.amount: Most awards USD 15,000-75,000 a year
grants.description: Research grants (formerly HFG Research Grants) for projects that advance understanding of violence and aggression, such as war, crime, terrorism and political extremism. Policy relevance is weighed heavily.

grants.name: APS Franklin Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year (1 October and 1 December); the 1 December 2026 round is decided in March 2027.
grants.region: Foreign nationals without a US affiliation may apply only for research carried out in the United States
grants.amount: Up to USD 7,000
grants.description: Small grants toward research costs such as travel to archives, libraries and field sites, in all scholarly fields including the humanities and social sciences. Applicants need a doctorate or equivalent published work; PhD candidates are not eligible.

grants.name: John Templeton Foundation Open Grants (Online Funding Inquiry)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle. The 2026 OFI deadline was 15 July 2026; the 2027 cycle will be announced early in 2027.
grants.amount: Small grants up to USD 234,800; larger grants above that
grants.description: Open grant cycle for research in the Foundation's areas, including philosophy and theology, religion, science and society, character virtue development, and individual freedom. Applicants submit a short Online Funding Inquiry and may be invited to a full proposal.

grants.name: Kluge Fellowships at the Library of Congress
grants.funder: John W. Kluge Center, Library of Congress
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 round (Kluge Fellowship, Digital Studies, Philip Lee Phillips Society) opened 15 April and closed 15 September 2026.
grants.region: Open to US citizens and foreign nationals (H-1B holders are not eligible; other visa types reviewed case by case); the Larson fellowship is US-only
grants.amount: Monthly stipend
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Washington, DC for research in the humanities and social sciences using the Library of Congress collections. The main Kluge Fellowship is for scholars who hold a PhD.

grants.name: Wilson Center Research Fellowship
grants.funder: Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027-28 competition closed 30 September 2026; the 2028-29 call is expected in summer 2027.
grants.region: Open to scholars, practitioners, journalists and public intellectuals from around the world
grants.amount: USD 10,000 per month (2027-28 terms)
grants.duration: Up to 12 months in Washington, DC
grants.description: Residential fellowships for research and writing on public policy, history and international affairs. Applications require a project proposal, CV and two references, all in English.

grants.name: NIAS Fellowship (Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study)
grants.funder: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study in the Humanities and Social Sciences (NIAS-KNAW)
grants.deadlineNote: Open call for 2028-29 runs 15 January to 15 March 2027 (12:00 noon CET). Each category closes early once 72 eligible applications are received.
grants.region: Open to scholars from the Netherlands and abroad
grants.amount: Residential fellowship (see 'What NIAS offers')
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Amsterdam for researchers in the humanities and social sciences. Applicants need at least three years of academic experience after the PhD; a permanent position is not required.

grants.name: Collegium Helveticum Early-Career Fellowship
grants.funder: Collegium Helveticum (ETH Zurich, University of Zurich, Zurich University of the Arts)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications open 16 November 2026 and close 11 February 2027, 17:00 CET, for 2027-28.
grants.region: International applications invited; applicants need an associate fellow at ETH Zurich, UZH or ZHdK
grants.amount: About CHF 75,000-85,000 for ten months (ETH postdoc salary) plus up to CHF 2,000 research expenses
grants.description: Ten-month fellowships in Zurich for early-career researchers and artists working on interdisciplinary projects across the humanities, social sciences, sciences and arts. Applicants must be within five years of academic age and eight years of their doctorate.

grants.name: CASBS Residential Fellowship
grants.funder: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, Stanford University
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027-28 deadline was 30 October 2026; expect a late-October deadline in 2027. The practitioner fellowship has a separate December deadline.
grants.region: International scholars welcome if eligible for a J-1 scholar visa
grants.amount: Academic-year stipend for first-time fellows, supplementing sabbatical pay
grants.description: Residential fellowships for scholars in the social and behavioral sciences and humanities working on their own projects. Applicants should be at least three to four years past the doctorate; CASBS does not offer postdoctoral fellowships.

grants.name: National Humanities Center Residential Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: 2028-29 applications open 1 July 2027 and close 1 October 2027; letters due 8 October 2027.
grants.region: Open regardless of citizenship; international fellows are sponsored on J-1 visas
grants.amount: Stipend set individually, with travel expenses
grants.description: Residential fellowships for advanced humanities research. Applicants need a PhD received at least five years before the deadline (by 30 September 2022 for the 2028-29 cycle).

grants.name: IAS School of Historical Studies Membership
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027-28 deadline was 15 October 2026; expect mid-October in 2027.
grants.region: Open to scholars of all nationalities
grants.amount: Stipend and housing
grants.duration: One or two terms in Princeton
grants.description: Residential memberships for historians and humanists working on any period or region, including art history, classics, philosophy and the history of science. Applicants need a PhD and a substantial record of publication.

grants.name: IAS School of Social Science Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027-28 deadline was 15 October 2026; the 2028-29 call opens around 1 August 2027.
grants.region: Open to scholars of all nationalities
grants.amount: Stipend and housing
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Princeton for social scientists, organised each year around a theme with open places for other topics. The doctorate must be conferred by the deadline.

grants.name: FIAS Fellowship Programme (French Institutes for Advanced Study)
grants.funder: French Network of Institutes for Advanced Study (Paris, Aix-Marseille, Lyon, Nantes and others)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027-28 call closed 25 June 2026; the next call is expected in spring 2027.
grants.amount: Monthly allowance, accommodation and research budget
grants.description: Ten-month residencies at French institutes for advanced study, mainly for the humanities and social sciences. Applicants need a doctorate plus two years of full-time research experience after it.

grants.name: Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Regular fellowships have no deadline (selection about two years ahead). The Early Career Call in humanities and social sciences closes on 1 September each year.
grants.amount: Stipend, housing and travel
grants.duration: Up to one academic year in Berlin
grants.description: About 40 fellowships a year for researchers to work on projects of their own choice in Berlin, free from teaching and administration. A separate annual early-career call is reserved for humanities and social sciences.

grants.name: FRIAS Early Career and Senior Fellowships (Freiburg Institute for Advanced Studies)
grants.funder: Freiburg Institute for Advanced Studies, University of Freiburg
grants.deadlineNote: Next calls for all programmes expected to open in summer 2027; past calls closed in mid-September.
grants.region: Open to researchers from Freiburg, Germany and worldwide; applicants need at least six months of research experience in a country other than that of their first degree
grants.amount: Fellowship funding for the residency period
grants.description: Residential fellowships at the University of Freiburg in all disciplines, including the humanities and social sciences. Early Career fellows need a PhD within the last eight years; Senior fellows need eight years of postdoctoral experience.

grants.name: Notre Dame Institute for Advanced Study Faculty Fellowships
grants.funder: University of Notre Dame Institute for Advanced Study (NDIAS)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual, usually closing in late September or early October for the following academic year, on a yearly research theme.
grants.region: No citizenship requirement; scholars from outside the US are welcome
grants.amount: Stipend, housing subsidy and research allowance
grants.description: Eight to ten residential fellowships a year for scholars, practitioners and postdoctoral researchers whose projects address the Institute's annual research theme.

grants.name: Leverhulme Visiting Professorships
grants.deadlineNote: The latest round closed 1 September 2026. The Trust lists the next round as opening 1 May 2027 with an autumn 2027 closing date.
grants.region: Visiting academic based overseas; the application is made by the UK host institution
grants.amount: Visitor's maintenance and travel costs
grants.description: Enables UK universities to invite an eminent researcher based overseas to spend time in the UK to enhance the knowledge and skills of the host's staff and students. Any discipline, including the humanities and social sciences.

grants.name: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme (Oxford)
grants.funder: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust and University of Oxford
grants.deadlineNote: Apply to an eligible Oxford graduate course by its December or January 2027 deadline (for example 6 January 2027 for the MBA and MFE); no separate application.
grants.region: Nationals of listed developing and emerging economies, including India; applicants should intend to return home after study
grants.amount: Full course fees plus a living-costs grant
grants.description: Full scholarships for graduate study at Oxford in courses relevant to public service and development, many in the social sciences (public policy, economics, development studies, education, law), combined with a leadership programme.

grants.name: Ertegun Graduate Scholarship in the Humanities (Oxford)
grants.funder: Ertegun Graduate Scholarship Programme, University of Oxford
grants.deadlineNote: Apply with the Oxford graduate application by the course's early-January deadline (January 2027 for 2027-28 entry); a supporting statement is required.
grants.amount: Full course fees plus a living-costs grant (GBP 21,805 in 2026-27)
grants.description: Up to about 15 scholarships a year for new full-time master's and DPhil students in Oxford humanities subjects such as history, philosophy, classics, languages, theology, music and Asian and Middle Eastern Studies.

grants.name: EUI Max Weber Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Main 2027-28 deadline (16 October 2026) has passed; late applications for the Department of Economics accepted until 1 March 2027, 14:00 CET.
grants.amount: EUR 2,500 per month plus health insurance and a research fund
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships in economics, history, law, and political and social sciences at the EUI in Florence. Applicants must be within five years of completing the PhD.

grants.name: EUI Jean Monnet Fellowships (Robert Schuman Centre)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual, closing in late October (23 October 2026 for 2027-28).
grants.amount: Monthly grant
grants.description: One-year fellowships at the Robert Schuman Centre for researchers who obtained their doctorate more than five years earlier, working on European and global governance, political economy and related social science themes.

grants.name: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
grants.deadlineNote: The 2026-27 cycle is closed; the next cycle opens in early 2027. Past cycles closed on 31 March, with earlier country-level deadlines.
grants.region: Nationals of listed developing countries, including India
grants.amount: 50% grant and 50% loan; a guarantor is required
grants.description: Postgraduate scholarships, mainly for master's study, for outstanding students from selected developing countries who have no other means of financing their studies.

grants.name: British Academy International Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 round expected to open in early to mid-January 2027 and close in early March 2027. Each UK institution may submit at most 8 applications, so host universities run earlier internal deadlines.
grants.region: Early-career researchers based outside the UK (must have been outside the UK for the year before the deadline); requires a UK sponsor at an eligible UK host
grants.amount: Funding for living and research costs at the UK host
grants.description: Fellowships for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based outside the UK to spend time at a UK institution with a named sponsor. Applicants need no more than five years of full-time postdoctoral experience and must pass their viva before 1 June 2027.

grants.name: Endangered Archives Programme Grants
grants.funder: British Library Endangered Archives Programme (funded by Arcadia)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The Round 22 preliminary deadline was 6 November 2026; the next call usually opens in September with a preliminary deadline in early November.
grants.region: Material anywhere outside the UK, Western Europe and North America; host institution can be anywhere, and applicants based in the project country are particularly welcomed
grants.amount: Pilot projects up to GBP 15,000; major projects up to GBP 60,000
grants.description: Grants to locate, digitise and make openly available archives, manuscripts, photographs, sound recordings and other heritage material at risk. Principal applicants can be faculty, archivists or librarians, or postgraduate researchers with project-management experience.

grants.name: ELDP Endangered Language Documentation Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rapid Grants are rolling (results in about two months). Small, Major and Legacy Materials grants have an annual round from mid-June to 1 October.
grants.region: Language documenters of any nationality, for projects anywhere in the world
grants.amount: Rapid up to EUR 5,000; Small and Legacy up to EUR 10,000; Major projects above EUR 10,000
grants.description: Grants for documenting endangered languages through recording, transcription and archiving, and for digitising legacy recordings at risk. India's many minority and tribal languages are within scope.

grants.name: Paul Mellon Centre Grants and Fellowships (Spring 2027 round)
grants.funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art
grants.deadlineNote: Spring 2027 round opens 30 November 2026 and closes 18 January 2027, 11:59 pm GMT; decisions by 16 April 2027.
grants.region: Most schemes are open to international applicants (Junior Fellowships require enrolment at a non-British university)
grants.amount: Varies by scheme, for example Research Support Grants up to GBP 2,000
grants.description: Grants and fellowships for research on British art and architectural history, including Junior Fellowships for doctoral researchers, early-career fellowships, research support grants and the Rome Fellowship. Colonial and South Asian connections to British art are within scope.

grants.name: Hague Academy of International Law Summer Course Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: Registration and scholarship applications for the 2027 Summer Courses open 1 November 2026 and close 31 January 2027.
grants.region: Open internationally; doctoral scholarships are for PhD candidates from non-OECD states such as India
grants.amount: Regular scholarships cover registration fees, travel and EUR 600 for accommodation; doctoral scholarships EUR 2,250 plus half of travel up to EUR 910
grants.duration: Public international law 5-23 July 2027; private international law 26 July-13 August 2027
grants.description: Scholarships to attend the Hague Academy's summer courses in public or private international law. Applicants need a law degree; preference goes to those with a master's or higher.

grants.name: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science Fellowships
grants.funder: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (MPIWG), Berlin
grants.deadlineNote: Two deadlines a year, 15 January and 15 September (23:59 CET); fellowships start about four months later at the earliest.
grants.region: Postdoctoral, research and senior fellows must be based outside Germany; predoctoral fellows may be from Germany or abroad
grants.amount: EUR 1,650 (predoctoral), EUR 3,000 (postdoctoral), EUR 3,600 (research) or EUR 4,200 (senior) per month
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Berlin for research on the history of science, technology, medicine and knowledge across all periods and regions. Self-funded research stays are also possible.

grants.name: MPIWG First Research Article Fellowship
grants.funder: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (MPIWG), Berlin
grants.deadlineNote: Apply by 15 January 2027, 23:59 CET; decisions by 1 April 2027.
grants.region: Doctoral students enrolled at institutions in Asia, Africa or Latin America (including India)
grants.amount: Monthly stipend under Max Planck Society guidelines
grants.description: Six-month fellowships in Berlin for advanced PhD students in the history of science, technology and medicine or science and technology studies to write their first single-authored research article in English. Applicants must have completed their thesis research.

grants.name: Clark Art Institute Research and Academic Program Fellowships
grants.funder: Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Applications for 2028-29 open 1 July 2027 and close 15 October 2027.
grants.region: Fellows may come from any country and need not be US citizens
grants.amount: Stipend plus housing in Williamstown, Massachusetts
grants.duration: Usually one semester; full-year, summer and two-month fellowships also offered
grants.description: Residential fellowships for scholars, critics, curators and artists working on art history, visual culture and related fields. Dissertation research is not funded.

grants.name: UNU-WIDER Visiting PhD Fellowship
grants.funder: United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER)
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year: applications open 1 March and 1 September and close 31 March and 30 September (23:59 UTC+3).
grants.region: PhD students worldwide; preference for those from developing countries
grants.amount: Travel and living costs during the stay
grants.description: Visiting fellowships at UNU-WIDER in Helsinki for doctoral students in development economics and related social sciences to work on their thesis alongside WIDER researchers.

grants.name: IGC India Sustainable Growth Hub Research Grants
grants.funder: International Growth Centre (LSE and University of Oxford)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2025 call closed 6 July 2025; no date for the next call has been announced. Check the page for a new round.
grants.region: Lead PI must be based at an Indian institution; co-PIs can be anywhere
grants.amount: Full grants up to GBP 40,000; small grants up to GBP 15,000
grants.description: Research grants for policy-relevant economics and social science research conducted in India on sustainable growth. The lead PI must hold or be pursuing a PhD.

grants.name: Fulbright-Nehru Master's Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual, usually closing in mid-May for study starting the following year (the 2026-27 cycle closed 14 May 2025).
grants.amount: Tuition, living costs, travel and health insurance
grants.description: Fellowships for Indian professionals to pursue a master's degree at US universities in fields that include economics, public administration, international affairs, journalism, arts and culture management, and environmental and urban policy.

grants.name: John Carter Brown Library Fellowships
grants.funder: John Carter Brown Library, Brown University
grants.deadlineNote: Long-term and short-term fellowships for 2027-28 are due 4 January 2027.
grants.region: Open regardless of nationality (long-term fellowships require a PhD)
grants.amount: Short-term USD 2,500 per month; long-term USD 5,000 per month
grants.description: Fellowships for research on the history of the colonial Americas, including Atlantic and global connections, using the JCB's collections. Short-term fellowships are open to doctoral candidates, postdoctoral and independent researchers.

grants.name: American Antiquarian Society Short-Term Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: One- to two-month fellowships for 2027-28 due 15 January 2027.
grants.region: International scholars welcome, but AAS does not sponsor visas; the long-term AAS-NEH fellowship requires US citizenship or three years' US residence
grants.amount: USD 2,400 per month
grants.description: Short-term residential fellowships for research in American history and culture to 1900 using the AAS library. Open to doctoral candidates and postdoctoral scholars.

grants.name: Bodleian Visiting Fellowships in Special Collections
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027-28 due 27 November 2026, 5 pm GMT, by email plus an online form; two references must arrive by the same date.
grants.region: Researchers outside the University of Oxford at any postdoctoral level; overseas applicants arrange their own UK visa
grants.amount: Up to GBP 2,200 per month toward research-visit costs
grants.duration: At least one month, within 1 August 2027 to 31 July 2028
grants.description: Fellowships for research in the Bodleian's special collections, including its South Asian manuscripts and archives. Doctoral students may apply if their thesis is submitted before the deadline.

grants.name: Rothermere American Institute Fellowships-in-Residence
grants.funder: Rothermere American Institute, University of Oxford
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027-28 due 1 February 2027, 12 pm UK time.
grants.region: Academics based outside Oxford, including overseas; fellows arrange their own visa
grants.amount: Non-stipendiary (Bodleian access, desk space, university email)
grants.description: Residencies in Oxford for academics, typically on sabbatical, researching American history, politics, international relations, literature or culture. A doctorate is required.

grants.name: Wenner-Gren Conference and Workshop Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Deadlines 1 December (events from 1 July of the next year) and 1 June (events from 1 January of the next year); portals open two months before.
grants.region: No nationality or location requirement; broad international participation is favoured
grants.amount: Up to USD 20,000
grants.description: Grants to organise conferences and workshops in anthropology and related fields. The lead organiser must hold a doctorate in anthropology or a related discipline; funds mainly support international participants.

grants.name: Wenner-Gren Hunt Fellowship in Public Writing
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Letter of interest due 15 October; invited full proposals due 15 December.
grants.description: One fellowship a year for an anthropologist to write a book or other work for a broad public audience. It replaces the former Hunt Postdoctoral Fellowship.

grants.name: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship
grants.funder: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (administered by Campus France)
grants.deadlineNote: French host institutions submit nominations by 6 January 2027; students must apply through the institution earlier, by its own internal deadline. Results from 12 April 2027.
grants.region: Foreign nationals, including Indian citizens; age limit 29 (master's) or 35 (PhD)
grants.amount: Monthly allowance plus travel, health insurance and cultural activities
grants.description: Government scholarships for international students on master's programmes and for PhD mobility at French institutions, in priority fields that include law, economics, management and political science as well as the sciences and engineering.

grants.name: Rotary Peace Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2028-29 application opens online in February 2027; the last cycle ran 1 February to 15 May 2026.
grants.region: Open worldwide; a new Rotary Peace Center at Symbiosis International University, Pune, serves applicants from Asia
grants.amount: Tuition, fees, room and board, travel and field-study costs
grants.duration: Master's degree (15-24 months) or a one-year professional certificate
