grants.description: Fully funded fellowships for peace and development professionals to study peace and conflict resolution at Rotary Peace Centers at partner universities. Applicants need relevant work experience.

grants.name: IIAS Asia in the World Fellowship
grants.funder: International Institute for Asian Studies (IIAS), Leiden
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The latest window ran 1 July to 10 September 2026 for cohorts starting September 2027 and March 2028. Self-funded visiting researchers can apply year-round.
grants.region: Open internationally, including scholars based in Asia
grants.amount: Fellowship support and research facilities in Leiden
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Leiden for researchers in the humanities and social sciences working on Asia and its global connections.

grants.name: Rockefeller Foundation Bellagio Center Residency
grants.deadlineNote: Annual open call. Expressions of interest for 2027 residencies were due 20 March 2026; the next call is expected in early 2027.
grants.region: Open worldwide (applicants 18 or older; no Bellagio residency in the past five years)
grants.amount: Residency with room and board at Lake Como, Italy
grants.description: Residencies for academics, artists, writers, policymakers and practitioners whose work addresses pressing global problems. Scholars in the humanities and social sciences are among those selected each year.

grants.name: CRASSH Visiting Fellowships (Cambridge)
grants.funder: Centre for Research in the Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (CRASSH), University of Cambridge
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027-28 due 3 February 2027, 17:00 UTC; references due 10 February 2027; results by end of March 2027.
grants.region: Any scholar from outside the University of Cambridge with a PhD
grants.amount: Self-funded (no stipend); affiliation, workspace and library access
grants.duration: One or more terms between October 2027 and June 2028, plus summer places
grants.description: Visiting fellowships at Cambridge for scholars in the arts, humanities and social sciences, with access to CRASSH's seminars and the university's libraries.

grants.name: CRASSH Visiting Fellowships for Scholars from the Global South
grants.funder: Centre for Research in the Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (CRASSH), University of Cambridge
grants.deadlineNote: Applications due 22 January 2027, 12:00 UTC, for Lent Term 2028. Late applications are not accepted.
grants.region: Scholars at higher education institutions in the Global South; preference for those whose PhD and career are in the Global South (check the call for country eligibility)
grants.amount: Accommodation at Wolfson College plus a weekly allowance for food and local travel (GBP 140 a week in the 2025 round)
grants.description: Funded term-long fellowships at Cambridge for established humanities and social science scholars from the Global South. Applicants need a PhD awarded at least five years before applying.

grants.name: IASH Visiting Research Fellowships (Edinburgh)
grants.funder: Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities, University of Edinburgh
grants.deadlineNote: Portal opens November 2026; applications and references due 26 February 2027, 17:00 GMT.
grants.region: Researchers from anywhere in the world; a named mentor at the University of Edinburgh is required
grants.amount: Unfunded (office space and library access; no stipend or accommodation)
grants.description: Visiting fellowships at Edinburgh's humanities institute for researchers in the humanities and related social sciences. Applicants need a doctorate or equivalent professional qualification.

grants.name: Library Company of Philadelphia Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Postdoctoral, dissertation and short-term fellowships for 2027-28 due 17 January 2027; decisions by 2 April 2027.
grants.region: Postdoctoral fellowships open to citizens of any country (no visa sponsorship); the Barra Foundation International Research Fellowship is reserved for non-US citizens living outside the US
grants.amount: Barra International fellowship USD 2,500 plus up to USD 1,000 travel; other awards vary
grants.duration: One month (short-term) to an academic year (postdoctoral)
grants.description: Fellowships for research in early American history and culture, including the Atlantic world and visual culture, using the Library Company's collections.

grants.name: Dumbarton Oaks Fellowships
grants.funder: Dumbarton Oaks Research Library and Collection, Harvard University
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Academic-year fellowships close 1 November (1 November 2026 for 2027-28).
grants.region: No citizenship restriction found; J-1 visa sponsorship available
grants.amount: USD 35,000 (fellows) or USD 25,000 (junior fellows) for the academic year, plus housing
grants.description: Residential fellowships in Washington, DC for Byzantine studies, Pre-Columbian studies, and garden and landscape studies. Junior fellowships support dissertation writing.

grants.name: Huntington Library Fellowships
grants.funder: The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2027-28 deadline was 15 November 2026; expect mid-November in 2027.
grants.region: No citizenship restriction stated; about a quarter to a third of applicants come from outside the US
grants.amount: Long-term USD 50,000 for nine months; short-term USD 4,000 per month
grants.description: Fellowships for research in the Huntington's collections in British and American history, literature, art history and the history of science and medicine. Travel grants also support research in archives outside the US and Canada.

grants.name: Endangered Language Fund Language Legacies Grants
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 request for proposals is open; see the guidelines for the closing date (past rounds closed in mid-March).
grants.region: Community members and researchers from any country (no degree required)
grants.amount: Around USD 2,000 on average
grants.description: Small grants for documenting and revitalising endangered languages, including archiving of recordings, with priority for projects that benefit both the speaker community and linguistics.

grants.name: Chevening Scholarships (India)
grants.funder: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Applications for 2027-28 are closed; the next round usually opens in August and closes in early autumn for study starting the following year.
grants.region: Indian citizens who meet Chevening's eligibility criteria (including work experience) and will return to India
grants.amount: Full tuition, living allowance, travel to the UK and visa costs
grants.duration: One-year taught master's degree in the UK
grants.description: UK government scholarships for future leaders to take a one-year master's at any UK university, with many scholars in public policy, law, economics, development, media and the humanities. Partner-funded Chevening awards are also offered.

grants.name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call, usually published early in the year with a deadline in spring; applicants need an offer from an Irish institution before applying.
grants.region: Students domiciled outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK, including India
grants.amount: EUR 10,000 for one year (2026 call)
grants.description: Sixty scholarships a year for international students starting a master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD at an eligible Irish higher education institution, in any discipline.

grants.name: CIMPA Research Schools (call for projects)
grants.funder: Centre International de Mathematiques Pures et Appliquees (CIMPA)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; projects for 2028 schools closed 4 October 2026 (selection February 2027). The next call, for 2029 schools, is expected to close in early October 2027.
grants.region: Schools held in IMU developing countries; external co-organiser from France, Germany, Norway, Spain or Switzerland
grants.amount: EUR 10,000-20,000 per school (at most half the budget)
grants.description: CIMPA co-funds research schools in mathematics held in developing countries, organised by a local mathematician with a co-organiser in a CIMPA partner country. At least half the support must go to participants from other developing countries.

grants.name: CIMPA Schools: participant funding
grants.funder: Centre International de Mathematiques Pures et Appliquees (CIMPA)
grants.deadlineNote: Each school sets its own deadline; open 2027 schools include Algeria (Geometry and Dynamics, 23 Jan 2027), Colombia (Algebraic Geometry, 21 Feb 2027), Kenya (Density Functional Theory, 28 Feb 2027) and Morocco (Modelling and AI for health and environment, 5 Mar 2027).
grants.region: Participants based in IMU developing countries
grants.amount: Travel (usually up to EUR 1,000) and accommodation; no registration fee
grants.description: CIMPA research schools are two-week courses for Master's students, PhD students and young researchers. Participants from developing countries can request travel and living support when applying through applications.cimpa.info.

grants.name: CIMPA-ICTP Fellowships Research in Pairs
grants.funder: CIMPA and the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2027 visits call closed on 24 April 2026. Next call expected around April 2027 for visits in 2028.
grants.region: Mathematicians working in developing countries visiting a host in Germany, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway or Switzerland
grants.amount: Up to EUR 10,000
grants.description: Funds a stay of at least five weeks in Europe for a mathematician from a developing country to work on a joint project with a European colleague, plus a recorded mini-course for students. Applicants need a PhD at least three years old and five years at an institution in a developing country; check with CIMPA whether India is on the eligible list.

grants.name: ICERM Semester Programs (long-term participants and faculty fellowships)
grants.funder: Institute for Computational and Experimental Research in Mathematics (ICERM), Brown University
grants.deadlineNote: Applications through ICERM's portal for each semester program; the Fall 2027 program (Applied and Computational Complex Analysis, 8 Sep to 10 Dec 2027) is listed.
grants.region: International; participants travel to Providence, USA
grants.amount: Travel (up to USD 2,000 from Asia) and lodging support where available; faculty fellowships of USD 30,000 per semester
grants.description: ICERM runs semester-long programs in computational and experimental mathematics and accepts applications from faculty, postdocs and graduate students worldwide. Some travel and lodging support is available but not guaranteed; graduate students must stay at least six weeks.

grants.name: IPAM Long Programs (core participants)
grants.funder: Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics (IPAM), UCLA
grants.deadlineNote: Each long program has its own application; upcoming programs include Artificial Intelligence in Materials Science (13 Sep to 17 Dec 2027) and Frontiers of Quantum Advantage (6 Mar to 9 Jun 2028). Core participant deadlines usually fall a few months before the start.
grants.region: International; participants travel to Los Angeles, USA
grants.amount: Housing and travel support for participants
grants.description: IPAM long programs bring researchers at all career stages to UCLA for a semester-length program in applied mathematics and computing. IPAM offers housing and travel support to accepted participants.

grants.name: IHES Invited Researchers (visiting programme)
grants.deadlineNote: Selection twice a year (June and December); deadline for the December 2026 selection is 29 November 2026, results by end of January 2027.
grants.amount: Per diem, office and free accommodation in the IHES residence
grants.description: IHES invites mathematicians and theoretical physicists for research visits, selected by its Scientific Council on excellence alone. Visitors get a per diem, an office, housing at the Ormaille residence and weekday lunch.

grants.name: IHES Postdoctoral Positions
grants.deadlineNote: Deadline 29 November 2026 for positions starting in the 2027-28 academic year; results by end of January 2027.
grants.amount: Salaried postdoctoral position
grants.description: Two-year postdoctoral positions (with a possible one-year extension) at IHES in mathematics and theoretical physics, including non-specific mathematics positions. Applications need a CV, publication list, research summary and two to three letters.

grants.name: IHP Research in Paris
grants.deadlineNote: Twice-yearly call: 15 May for stays in January to June of the following year, 15 October for July to December. Both 2027 rounds have closed; next expected 15 May 2027.
grants.region: International; small groups working at IHP, Paris
grants.amount: Accommodation and travel costs for the group, per budget
grants.description: Supports small groups of researchers (typically two to four) to work together at IHP for one to six weeks on a research project in mathematics, theoretical physics or theoretical computer science.

grants.name: ICTS Program Proposals
grants.funder: International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS-TIFR), Bengaluru
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the last call closed 31 January 2026 for programs from April to September 2027. A similar call is expected in early 2027.
grants.region: Proposers from India or abroad; programs held at ICTS Bengaluru
grants.amount: Financial and administrative support for the program, guest house accommodation
grants.description: ICTS invites proposals for research or training programs of two weeks or more in mathematical, physical and computational sciences, including theoretical computer science and machine learning. Approved programs get funding, venue and housing for participants.

grants.name: CMI Computer Science Summer Internship 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Apply through CMI's online form by 31 January 2027. (Mathematics internships go through the Academies' summer fellowship portal.)
grants.region: Students at Indian institutions, usually after second year of college
grants.amount: Fellowship covering hostel food; on-campus accommodation; no travel support
grants.description: Summer research internships of at least one month with CMI computer science faculty, mainly in algorithms, logic and automata theory. Applicants need programming experience and some exposure to algorithms or automata.

grants.name: IMSc Summer Research Programme
grants.funder: The Institute of Mathematical Sciences (IMSc), Chennai
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; applications usually open early in the year for May to July. Check the field-specific forms on the page.
grants.amount: Second-class return train fare, Rs 200 per day and hostel accommodation if available
grants.description: Summer projects with IMSc faculty in mathematics, theoretical computer science, theoretical physics and computational biology. Open to pre-final and final year BSc/BE/BTech students and first-year MSc/ME/MTech students.

grants.name: TIFR Visiting Students' Research Programme (Mathematics)
grants.funder: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), School of Mathematics
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; the 2026 deadline was 6 March 2026 for a programme from 18 May to 18 June. Expect a similar cycle in 2027.
grants.amount: Honorarium of Rs 9,000 and accommodation
grants.description: A one-month summer programme of courses and reading projects at the TIFR School of Mathematics in Mumbai for motivated Master's students and exceptional BSc/BTech students.

grants.name: Marktoberdorf Summer School
grants.funder: Summer School Marktoberdorf (TU Munich and partners)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual two-week school in August; the 2026 application deadline was 15 May 2026. The 2027 edition is not yet announced.
grants.amount: Participation fee about EUR 500 plus EUR 600 living costs; limited grants for those in need
grants.description: A two-week summer school on software verification, logic and dependable systems for PhD students in computer science, held in Bavaria since 1970. Limited grants help participants who cannot cover the fee and living costs.

grants.name: USENIX Student Grants Program
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling by conference; each USENIX event (Security, OSDI, ATC, NSDI, FAST and others) posts a grant application under Attend once registration opens. USENIX Security '27 is 11 to 13 August 2027.
grants.amount: Free registration and partial travel and hotel funding
grants.description: USENIX funds students to attend its systems and security conferences, with preference for students from institutions not often represented. An advisor statement is required and postdocs are not eligible.

grants.name: ACL Diversity and Inclusion Subsidies
grants.deadlineNote: Each ACL-sponsored conference (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, EACL, AACL) runs its own call, usually about six weeks before the event; the ACL 2026 call closed 15 May 2026.
grants.region: International; priority to those facing financial barriers
grants.amount: Registration waivers and reimbursement of travel, caregiving, bandwidth and VPN costs
grants.description: Subsidies for students and researchers from under-represented communities to attend ACL conferences in person or online. Priority goes to presenting authors, first-time attendees and applicants without other support.

grants.name: CVPR Broadening Participation Travel Grants
grants.funder: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; applications open in spring before the June conference with rolling decisions. Check the CVPR 2027 site.
grants.amount: Travel grants and registration waivers
grants.description: CVPR supports students from communities that do not usually attend the conference with travel funding and waived registration. Need, contribution to the conference and travel origin are considered.

grants.name: Ethereum Foundation Ecosystem Support Program (ESP)
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; funding through published Wishlist items and RFPs.
grants.amount: Varies by project
grants.description: Grants for open-source public goods in the Ethereum ecosystem, including research in cryptography, protocol design, privacy and security. Funding is tied to wishlist items and requests for proposals posted by EF teams.

grants.name: Zcash Community Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling applications via GitHub; funded through November 2028.
grants.amount: Varies; program total about 100,000 ZEC
grants.description: Funds independent teams doing open development, research and education for the Zcash privacy-preserving cryptocurrency, including wallets, core protocol and cryptography work.

grants.name: EATCS Presburger Award for Young Scientists
grants.funder: European Association for Theoretical Computer Science (EATCS)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations usually due in March (13 March in 2026).
grants.region: International; nominees at most 35 years old or within 6 years of PhD
grants.amount: EUR 1,000 and an invited lecture at ICALP
grants.description: Recognises outstanding contributions in theoretical computer science by a young scientist. Nominations come from colleagues.

grants.name: EATCS Distinguished Dissertation Award
grants.funder: European Association for Theoretical Computer Science (EATCS)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; for theses defended in the previous calendar year, deadline usually end of February (28 February in 2026).
grants.amount: EUR 1,000 each for up to three theses
grants.description: Awards up to three outstanding PhD theses in theoretical computer science defended in the preceding year.

grants.name: ACM Doctoral Dissertation Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations by the PhD-granting department usually due 31 October (30 November when a translation is needed), for theses accepted between 1 October and 30 September.
grants.amount: USD 20,000 for the winner
grants.description: ACM's award for the best PhD dissertation in computer science and engineering. Each department may nominate one or two theses.

grants.name: ACM India Doctoral Dissertation Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations usually due 31 August for theses defended between 1 July of the previous year and 30 June.
grants.amount: Cash prize and certificate
grants.description: Recognises the best doctoral dissertations in computer science and engineering from Indian institutions.

grants.name: Ackermann Award (EACSL Outstanding Dissertation Award for Logic in Computer Science)
grants.funder: European Association for Computer Science Logic (EACSL)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations usually due 1 July for theses accepted in the previous calendar year.
grants.amount: Certificate, invitation to present at CSL and funding to attend
grants.description: Recognises an outstanding PhD thesis in logic in computer science (topics of CSL and LICS). Nominated by the candidate or supervisor via EasyChair.

grants.name: E.W. Beth Dissertation Prize
grants.funder: Association for Logic, Language and Information (FoLLI)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations usually due mid-April (15 April in 2026) for degrees awarded in the previous calendar year.
grants.amount: EUR 3,000 and certificate
grants.description: Awards outstanding PhD dissertations in logic, language and computation, presented at ESSLLI.

grants.name: Simons Institute Long-Term Visitors: Diffusion Generative Modeling (Fall 2027)
grants.funder: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing, UC Berkeley
grants.deadlineNote: Applications considered until 1 December 2026 for the program running 30 Aug to 17 Dec 2027.
grants.region: International; active researchers beyond the postdoctoral stage
grants.amount: Not stated on the application page; contact the Institute
grants.description: Applications to visit the Simons Institute for more than 30 days (full semester preferred) during its Fall 2027 program on diffusion generative modeling. Submit a cover letter with proposed dates and a CV with publication list.

grants.name: Programming Languages Mentoring Workshop (PLMW) Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: Held at POPL, PLDI, ICFP and SPLASH; applications open on each conference site 3-4 months before the event. The PLMW@POPL 2027 deadline (19 Oct 2026) has passed; PLMW@PLDI 2027 is expected to open in early 2027.
grants.amount: Economy travel up to a cap, registration and five shared hotel nights
grants.description: PLMW introduces students to programming languages research and careers, with talks and mentoring before a major SIGPLAN conference. Scholarships prioritise students who could not otherwise attend; no PL background is required.

grants.name: NBHM Research Project Grants
grants.funder: National Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM), Department of Atomic Energy
grants.deadlineNote: Periodic call; check the NBHM site for the current round.
grants.region: Faculty at Indian universities and institutions
grants.amount: Project funding (equipment, books, research staff, travel)
grants.description: NBHM invites research project proposals in mathematics from faculty members at Indian institutions.

grants.name: Women in Machine Learning (WiML) Workshop Travel Funding
grants.deadlineNote: Twice a year: the WiML Workshop at NeurIPS (travel funding deadline mid-September; 16 Sep in 2026) and the WiML Symposium at ICML (late May).
grants.region: International; presenters must be women or non-binary
grants.amount: Reimbursement of transport, accommodation, meals, poster printing and visa costs
grants.description: WiML funds presenters at its workshop co-located with NeurIPS and its symposium at ICML. Funding is paid as a reimbursement after the event and recipients may be asked to volunteer.

grants.name: CODS Student Travel Grants
grants.funder: ACM India IKDD (Conference on Data Science, CODS)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; for CODS 2026 the Stage 1 deadline was 20 Sep 2026 and Stage 2 (accepted authors) in October.
grants.region: Full-time students, mainly at Indian institutions
grants.amount: Up to INR 6,000 plus free shared accommodation in one tier
grants.description: Travel grants for full-time students to attend IKDD's annual data science conference in India in person. A second stage is reserved for authors of accepted papers.

grants.name: ACM FAccT Fee Waivers and Travel Grants
grants.funder: ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; applications open after paper decisions, around April (27 April deadline in 2026).
grants.amount: Registration waivers and travel reimbursement
grants.description: Financial support to attend FAccT, weighted by contribution to the conference and widening access for groups historically under-represented. Students need an advisor letter.

grants.name: Astra Fellowship (AI safety)
grants.deadlineNote: Cohort-based; the current cohort runs Sep 2026 to Feb 2027. Next cohort not yet announced; register interest on the page.
grants.region: In person in Berkeley, USA (London hub for UK-based fellows); supports J-1 and F-1 visas
grants.amount: USD 8,400 per month stipend plus up to USD 15,000 per month compute
grants.description: A fully funded, in-person fellowship pairing fellows with senior mentors for empirical or strategy research on AI safety.

grants.name: EMBO Young Investigator Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline 1 April.
grants.region: Group leaders in EMBC Member States or Global Partners; India is eligible as an EMBC associate member (DBT).
grants.amount: Four years of networking funding, training and lab-member support (amount not stated)
grants.description: Supports life scientists who have led an independent group for less than four years. Young Investigators get networking funds, training, mentoring and access to the EMBO network.

grants.name: EMBO Conferences, Practical Courses and Global Lecture Courses (organiser funding)
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year; 1 March and 1 July 2027, 12:00 CET.
grants.region: Global Lecture Courses can take place in India, Singapore or Taiwan; conferences and practical courses per EMBO eligibility rules.
grants.amount: Basic meeting funding plus promotion and registration support
grants.description: Scientists can apply to EMBO for funding to organise a conference, a hands-on practical course or a lecture course in the life sciences. Global Lecture Courses are designed for EMBC global partner countries, including India.

grants.name: EMBO Travel Grants and Registration Fee Waivers (EMBO events)
grants.deadlineNote: Request when registering for each EMBO Conference or Practical Course; deadlines set per event.
grants.region: Any nationality; additional grants for participants working in labs in India, Chile, Singapore or Taiwan.
grants.amount: Travel grant or fee waiver (amount set per event)
grants.description: Participants selected for EMBO Conferences and Practical Courses can request travel support and fee waivers, awarded by organisers on abstract quality. Researchers in Indian labs are eligible for extra grants.

grants.name: Schmidt Ocean Institute Expedition Proposals (R/V Falkor (too) ship time)
grants.deadlineNote: Expressions of interest for 2029 expeditions due 15 December 2026; EOIs reviewed twice a year.
grants.region: International; expeditions must fall in the vessel's operating area for that year and need permission from the coastal state.
grants.amount: Free ship time with full lab facilities, ROV and technical support; berths for up to 25 scientists
grants.description: Collaborative, multidisciplinary teams can propose expeditions on the research vessel Falkor (too). Investigators fund their own salaries, travel and analysis. Submit a 3-page written or 10-minute video expression of interest.

grants.name: National Geographic Society: The Human Thread RFP
grants.deadlineNote: Apply by 1 December 2026 via the National Geographic Funding Portal. NGS now funds through time-bound RFPs with their own deadlines.
grants.region: International (applicants 18+); project start at least six months after the deadline.
grants.amount: Set per RFP
grants.description: Open request for storytelling projects that capture the range of human experience, funded with Lilly Endowment support. National Geographic replaced its Level I/II grants with themed RFPs; check the grants page for new calls in science and conservation.

grants.name: Hubble Space Telescope Cycle 35 Call for Proposals
grants.funder: Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI) / NASA and ESA
grants.deadlineNote: STScI planned timeline: call released 16 December 2026, proposals due 1 April 2027, 8pm ET.
grants.region: Open to astronomers worldwide; grant funding only for US-based investigators.
grants.amount: Observing time (and archival/theory programmes); no funding for non-US PIs
grants.description: Annual competition for Hubble observing time and archival research. Researchers at Indian institutions can propose as PI; selected programmes start in November 2027.

grants.name: JWST General Observer Call for Proposals
grants.funder: Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI) / NASA, ESA and CSA
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Cycle 6 closed 30 September 2026; the Cycle 7 call is expected around July 2027 with a deadline in autumn 2027.
grants.region: Open to astronomers worldwide; grant funding only for US-based investigators.
grants.amount: Observing time on JWST
grants.description: Annual call for JWST observing, archival and theory proposals. Any researcher, including those at Indian institutions, can lead a proposal.

grants.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory Call for Proposals
grants.funder: Chandra X-ray Center (Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory) / NASA
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. Cycle 28 closed 18 March 2026; the Cycle 29 call usually opens in December with a deadline in March.
grants.region: Open to astronomers worldwide; grant funding only for US-based investigators.
grants.amount: X-ray observing time
grants.description: Annual peer-reviewed competition for Chandra observing time, including joint programmes with other observatories. Non-US scientists may apply for time.

grants.name: XMM-Newton Announcement of Opportunity (observing time)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. AO-26 closed 9 October 2026; the next AO is expected to open around August 2027 with an October deadline.
grants.amount: X-ray observing time
grants.description: ESA's yearly call for observing proposals with the XMM-Newton X-ray observatory. Proposals are submitted through the XIPS tool to the Science Operations Centre.

grants.name: India@DESY Beamtime at PETRA III
grants.funder: DST, Government of India and DESY (administered by JNCASR)
grants.deadlineNote: Submit with the PETRA III regular calls (1 March and 1 September); results in May and November.
grants.amount: Synchrotron beamtime at PETRA III, Hamburg; travel costs reimbursed under the DST-DESY project
grants.description: Indian users can apply for X-ray beamtime at DESY's PETRA III synchrotron under the India-DESY agreement, with proposals reviewed by an Indian panel. Travel for scheduled experiments is reimbursed by JNCASR.

grants.name: AstroSat Announcement of Opportunity (observing time)
grants.deadlineNote: Yearly AO cycle; the call and deadline are posted on the ISSDC and AstroSat Science Support Cell websites, typically in the first quarter of the year.
grants.region: International; a majority share (about 55%) of time is reserved for Indian proposers.
grants.amount: Observing time on India's multi-wavelength space observatory
grants.description: ISRO invites proposals for AstroSat observations each AO cycle through the AstroSat Proposal Processing System at ISSDC. Indian scientists have reserved time.

grants.name: IAU Office of Astronomy for Development Annual Call for Proposals
grants.funder: International Astronomical Union (IAU) Office of Astronomy for Development
grants.deadlineNote: Annual. The 2026 call (for 2027 projects) closed 31 May 2026; the next call usually opens in April with a Stage 1 deadline in May.
grants.amount: Typically about EUR 5,000 per project
grants.description: Funds projects that use astronomy to address sustainable development goals, such as education, skills and outreach. Two-stage application.

grants.name: Biology Open Global South Conference Travel Grants
grants.deadlineNote: 20 Nov 2026 (travel after 21 Dec 2026), 18 Jun 2027 (travel after 19 Jul 2027), 19 Nov 2027 (travel after 31 Dec 2027).
grants.region: Early-career researchers based in Global South countries; India is on the eligible list. The meeting must be in another country.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 3,000
grants.description: Supports PhD students, postdocs and unfunded new group leaders from the Global South to attend international meetings in Biology Open's subject areas. No retrospective applications.

grants.name: Company of Biologists Scientific Meeting Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Quarterly deadlines: 29 Jan, 30 Apr, 30 Jul and 29 Oct 2027.
grants.region: No nationality restriction; applicant must be on the organising committee.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 3,000 (sliding scale by meeting size); small meeting grants up to GBP 400
grants.description: Contributes to the costs of meetings, workshops and conferences in developmental biology, cell biology, experimental biology and disease models. A companion fund supports sustainable conferencing ideas (up to GBP 2,500).

grants.name: Microbiology Society Research Visit Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Round 1 opens 1 March, closes 1 May; Round 2 opens 1 August, closes 1 October.
grants.region: Society members of at least one year, any country; host lab anywhere in the world.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 3,000
grants.description: Funds PhD students, postdocs and new lecturers to spend one to three months in another laboratory to learn techniques or start a collaboration. Applicants must be paid-up members of at least one year.

grants.name: Microbiology Society External Event Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Round 1: 1 Jan to 1 Feb 2027 (events Apr to Sep 2027); Round 2: 1 Jun to 1 Jul 2027 (events Oct 2027 to Mar 2028).
grants.region: Society members of at least one year, any country.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 750 (half of presenting costs)
grants.description: Helps members present their work at microbiology meetings not run by the Society. Society meetings are covered by a separate Society Events Grant.

grants.name: SEB Company of Biologists Travel Grant
grants.funder: Society for Experimental Biology (SEB), funded by The Company of Biologists
grants.deadlineNote: Quarterly deadlines: 31 Mar, 30 Jun, 30 Sep, 31 Dec.
grants.region: Student and early-career SEB members, any country (second year of membership); priority to low and middle income countries.
grants.amount: Up to GBP 800 for travel beyond home continent; up to GBP 250 for virtual events and training
grants.description: Supports early-career members to attend conferences, courses and lab visits in animal, plant and cell biology. Medical research is out of scope.

grants.name: Royal Society of Chemistry Prizes 2027 (nominations)
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations opened 21 October 2026 and close 13 January 2027, 17:00 GMT. Some journal lectureships (e.g. Biomaterials Science Lectureship) close 31 January 2027.
grants.region: Many research and innovation prizes and journal lectureships accept nominees from any country; check each prize's eligibility.
grants.amount: Prizes typically GBP 3,000-5,000 with a medal and lecture tour
grants.description: The RSC's annual round of research, innovation, education and journal prizes across the chemical sciences, including early-career, mid-career and open prizes. Nominations are made by a nominator, not by self-application for most prizes.

grants.name: ISIS Neutron and Muon Source: Indian Access (DST-JNCASR)
grants.funder: STFC ISIS Neutron and Muon Source (UK) with DST, Government of India via JNCASR
grants.deadlineNote: No autumn 2026 call because of a 2027 shutdown; the next ISIS call is expected in March 2027 with an April 2027 deadline for beamtime from November 2027. A new five-year ISIS-JNCASR agreement starts November 2027.
grants.region: Researchers at Indian institutions (Indian Access route); proposals go through normal ISIS peer review.
grants.amount: Neutron and muon beamtime at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory, UK
grants.description: Under India's agreement with ISIS, coordinated by JNCASR, Indian researchers can apply for neutron scattering and muon spectroscopy time for materials, chemistry and nanoscience. Rapid and Xpress access routes are also available.

grants.name: 3.6m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT) Call for Proposals
grants.funder: Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), Nainital
grants.deadlineNote: DOT-2027-C1 (1 Feb to 31 May 2027) is open; the observing policy sets the C1 deadline as 1 December and the C2 deadline in early August. Submit via the DOPSES portal.
grants.region: Astronomers at Indian institutions (with partner shares per DOT policy).
grants.amount: Observing time on India's largest optical telescope
grants.description: Twice-yearly call for observing time on the 3.6m DOT with its imaging and spectroscopy instruments. Proposals are reviewed by the DOT time allocation committee.

grants.name: Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT) Call for Proposals
grants.deadlineNote: Three cycles a year: 1 March (May-Aug), 1 July (Sep-Dec), 1 November (Jan-Apr).
grants.amount: Observing time on the 2m HCT at Hanle (HFOSC, TIRSPEC, HESP)
grants.description: IIA calls for proposals three times a year for the 2m Himalayan Chandra Telescope at the Indian Astronomical Observatory, Hanle. Observations can be run remotely from CREST, Hosakote.

grants.name: Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste: Indo-Italian Access Programme
grants.funder: Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste with DST, Government of India and Italy's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAECI)
grants.deadlineNote: Elettra semester calls usually close mid-March and mid-September; crystallography beamlines also accept monthly proposals. Check the VUO portal, since regular calls may be paused during the Elettra 2.0 upgrade.
grants.amount: Free beamtime with travel and accommodation support
grants.description: Indian researchers can use Elettra synchrotron beamlines, including those run with the Indian community, under an India-Italy agreement. Apply to Elettra with a scientific proposal and separately to DST (via the IISc contact) for support.

grants.name: Takemi Program in International Health (Takemi Fellowship)
grants.funder: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027-28 cohort close 31 December 2026, midnight EST.
grants.region: Open internationally; aimed at mid-career health professionals and researchers, mainly from low- and middle-income countries
grants.amount: No stipend; fellows must show their own funding (at least US$36,410 for the J-1 visa)
grants.description: Residential research fellowship for mid-career health researchers with a graduate degree and publications, who spend a year at Harvard analysing data they have already collected. The programme provides academic affiliation, mentoring and seminars; fellows bring their own funding.

grants.name: IAF Emerging Space Leaders (ESL) Grant Programme
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 call (for IAC 2027 in Poznan) is open; past deadlines fell in late January or mid February. Check the 2027 handbook for the exact date.
grants.region: Worldwide, any nationality; age 21 to 35; applicants from emerging space nations encouraged
grants.amount: Flights, budget accommodation, per diem and registration for the International Astronautical Congress and associated events
grants.description: Grants for students and young professionals in space engineering, science, policy or law to attend the International Astronautical Congress, plus the Space Generation Congress or the UN/IAF Workshop, with mentoring and a presentation workshop.

grants.name: INAE Innovative Student Projects Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations usually close 31 July (31 July 2026 for the last cycle). From 2026-27 only projects completed in that academic year are eligible.
grants.amount: Rs 15,000 (PhD), Rs 10,000 (Master's), Rs 10,000 per team (Bachelor's)
grants.description: Annual award for innovative BE/BTech projects, ME/MTech/MS theses and PhD theses in engineering. Nominations come from the head of department, dean or principal of the institution; up to 10 awards per level.

grants.name: INAE Young Innovator and Entrepreneur Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; nominations usually close in spring (15 May 2026 for the last cycle). No self-nominations.
grants.region: Indian citizens aged 45 or under (50 for women) on 1 January of the award year
grants.amount: Rs 1 lakh and a citation (up to four awards a year)
grants.description: Recognises young engineers whose innovation has led to a product, process or venture of societal or commercial value. An individual or a group of up to three may be nominated.

grants.name: Engineering for Change (E4C) Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; the 2027 call is not yet open. The first application phase for 2026 closed 15 February 2026.
grants.region: Worldwide, fully remote; early-career technical professionals (under 10 years' experience) and final-year undergraduates
grants.amount: Stipend varying with cost of living and expertise, paid on milestones
grants.duration: May to September, 20-25 hours per week
grants.description: Part-time remote fellowship in which early-career engineers work on development and sustainability projects with partner organisations, with training in human-centred design and global development.

grants.name: IEEE MTT-S Undergraduate Scholarships and Graduate Fellowships
grants.funder: IEEE Microwave Theory and Technology Society (MTT-S)
grants.deadlineNote: Undergraduate/pre-graduate scholarships: 15 April and 15 October each year. Graduate fellowships (microwave engineering, and medical applications): 15 October each year. The portal opens about a month before each deadline.
grants.amount: US$2,500 (undergraduate/pre-graduate scholarship); US$6,000 (graduate fellowship)
grants.description: Up to 20 scholarships a year for BS and MS students in electrical engineering, and up to 18 fellowships for graduate students in microwave engineering, including microwave engineering for medical applications.

grants.name: IEEE Signal Processing Society Scholarship Program
grants.deadlineNote: Applications open 1 March and close 30 June each year.
grants.region: Worldwide; award value varies by region
grants.amount: Up to US$7,000 over up to three years
grants.description: Scholarships for full-time undergraduate and graduate students in signal processing who have completed at least three signal processing courses. Recipients receive complimentary IEEE and SPS membership in the first year and must keep it afterwards.

grants.name: IEEE Life Members Graduate Study Fellowship in Electrical Engineering
grants.funder: IEEE Life Members Committee / IEEE Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; the deadline for 2026-27 was 4 May 2026. Expect the next call with a deadline in early May 2027.
grants.region: Worldwide; first-year graduate students at an engineering school of recognised standing
grants.amount: US$10,000 per year, renewable for a second year
grants.description: Fellowship for a first-year Master's student (or first-year PhD student whose PhD is the first graduate degree) in electrical engineering who holds a Bachelor's in electrical engineering. Students in the penultimate year of a combined BS/MS programme may also apply.

grants.name: IEEE CASS Pre-Doctoral Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Usually two rounds a year (2026 rounds closed 15 February and 1 July).
grants.region: Worldwide; CASS members for at least two years
grants.amount: US$2,500 plus up to US$1,000 travel to a CASS flagship conference
grants.description: Up to 10 grants a year for PhD students in circuits and systems to carry out interdisciplinary research at another research department. Applicants need endorsements from a faculty member and a host who are CASS members, and must be at least a year from graduating.

grants.name: IET Postgraduate Research Awards
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for 2027 are open; the closing date is on the IET awards platform (the 2026 round closed 2 April 2026).
grants.region: Open to IET members of at least one year (Student, Member or Fellow), any nationality
grants.amount: One award of GBP 10,000, three of GBP 5,000 and up to three of GBP 2,500
grants.description: One-off awards to support PhD or EngD research in engineering and technology, for example equipment, travel or collaboration. MSc and MRes students are not eligible, and a person can win only once during their PhD.

grants.name: ASME Turbo Expo Student Advisory Committee Travel Award (SACTA) 2027
grants.deadlineNote: Apply by 7 January 2027 for Turbo Expo 2027 (Calgary, 21-25 June 2027).
grants.region: Worldwide; degree-seeking students with an accepted Turbo Expo 2027 paper or poster
grants.amount: Reimbursement of up to US$2,000 of travel, accommodation and registration
grants.description: Up to 20 travel awards for students presenting at ASME Turbo Expo, the main conference on turbomachinery and gas turbines. Recipients take part in the Student Advisory Committee annual meeting and the poster session.

grants.name: James Dyson Award
grants.deadlineNote: Annual; 2026 entries ran 11 March to 15 July. The 2027 dates are not yet announced.
grants.region: Students in participating countries including India, and graduates of the last four years
grants.amount: National winner about Rs 6.5 lakh; international and sustainability winners about Rs 36.5 lakh each
grants.description: International design competition for current and recent students of engineering, product design and industrial design who submit a product that solves a clear problem. Individual and team entries are accepted.

grants.name: UICC Yamagiwa-Yoshida Memorial International Cancer (YY) Study Grants
grants.funder: Union for International Cancer Control (UICC), supported by the Japan National Committee for UICC
grants.deadlineNote: Current call runs 16 September to 20 November 2026; visits take place in 2027. Annual call each autumn.
grants.amount: Up to US$10,000
grants.duration: 3 months (extendable by up to 2 months with other funding)
grants.description: Grants for cancer researchers, clinicians, epidemiologists and public health professionals with a PhD at least two years old to carry out a bilateral research project at a host institution abroad. It is not a clinical training fellowship.

grants.name: EPICS in IEEE Project Grants
grants.funder: IEEE Educational Activities (EPICS in IEEE), with IEEE societies (AP-S, IMS, RAS, SSCS, IAS) and IEEE SA
grants.deadlineNote: Calls open twice a year (spring, from 1 March, and autumn; the October 2026 call ran 1 September to 1 October 2026).
grants.region: Worldwide; at least one IEEE member on the team and students must be included
grants.amount: Up to US$10,000 per project for supplies, plus mentoring
grants.description: Funds student teams working with a non-profit or NGO community partner on engineering solutions to local problems, completed within a year. Society-specific tracks cover antennas and sensing, instrumentation, robotics, integrated circuits, AI literacy and medical technology.

grants.name: ICMR SEHAT Mission Expressions of Interest on Occupational Health of Agricultural Workers
grants.funder: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), ICMR-NIOH, under the ICMR-ICAR SEHAT Mission
grants.deadlineNote: All three EoIs close 20 November 2026.
grants.amount: Project funding (not stated in the EoI)
grants.description: Three ICMR calls for expressions of interest on intervention research: reducing dust exposure among combine harvester workers, preventing occupational biohazards among agricultural allied workers, and assessing and reducing occupational pesticide exposure among agricultural workers.

grants.name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
grants.funder: Research Grants Council of Hong Kong
grants.deadlineNote: 2027/28 round: initial application to RGC for a reference number and full applications to the chosen universities both close 1 December 2026 (noon and 11:59pm Hong Kong time respectively).
grants.region: Open to all nationalities; tenable at eight Hong Kong universities (HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU, CityU, HKBU, Lingnan, EdUHK)
grants.amount: HK$344,400 per year stipend plus HK$14,400 per year conference and research travel allowance (2026/27 rates)
grants.description: Fellowships for new full-time PhD students at Hong Kong's publicly funded universities, in any field. Applicants first obtain an HKPFS reference number from the RGC and then apply to up to two universities quoting it.

grants.name: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Burslari)
grants.deadlineNote: The general application period runs each year from about 10 January to 20 February; the separate Research Scholarship has four quarterly windows. Confirm 2027 dates on the portal.
grants.region: Open to international applicants including Indian nationals
grants.amount: Full tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, return flight and a one-year Turkish language course
grants.description: Government scholarships for bachelor's, master's and PhD study at Turkish universities in all fields, with university placement included. There is also a Research Scholarship for academics and doctoral researchers to spend time at a Turkish institution.

grants.name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
grants.funder: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and Dutch universities (Study in NL)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications go through each participating Dutch institution; deadlines for 2027-28 are set by the institution, commonly 1 February or 1 May.
grants.region: Non-EEA nationals without a prior Dutch degree
grants.amount: EUR 5,000 in the first year of study
grants.description: A partial scholarship for international students starting a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch university or university of applied sciences.

grants.name: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027/28 call is expected to open in late 2026; the online deadline is usually mid-January (15 January 2026 for the previous round), and Indian applicants must also be nominated by the University Grants Commission, whose deadline may be earlier.
grants.region: India is a sending partner; Indian nationals apply via UGC nomination
grants.amount: Tuition waiver, monthly stipend, accommodation support and medical insurance
grants.description: Hungarian government scholarships for bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's and doctoral study at Hungarian universities across all fields. Applications are made online to Tempus and the chosen universities, with the home-country partner nominating candidates.

grants.name: France Excellence Charpak Master's Scholarship
grants.funder: Embassy of France in India / Campus France India
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; applications open in early spring after students apply for admission in France, with interviews in April (13-30 April in 2026). The 2027 call has not been announced.
grants.region: Indian citizens or OCI holders aged 30 or under, preferably with an Indian degree
grants.amount: EUR 860 per month living allowance plus French government scholar status (visa fee waiver, Campus France fee waiver, student social security)
grants.description: Scholarship for Indian students admitted to a full-time master's programme taught in France. It does not cover exchanges, internships or PhD study.

grants.name: France Excellence Charpak Summer Training Scholarship
grants.funder: Embassy of France in India / Campus France India
grants.deadlineNote: Call currently closed. In past cycles applications opened in mid-November and closed in late January for internships between May and July.
grants.region: Indian nationals resident in India, aged 30 or under, enrolled at bachelor's or master's level in an Indian institution
grants.amount: EUR 700 per month for up to 2 months, plus visa and Campus France fee waivers
grants.description: Funding for a short summer research internship or project at a French laboratory or institution. Applicants must secure an invitation letter from the host lab themselves.

grants.name: Invest Your Talent in Italy
grants.funder: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAECI), ICE and Uni-Italia
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026-27 call ran 20 April to 11 May 2026. The site says new applications open in 2027.
grants.amount: Scholarship for master's or postgraduate study plus an internship at an Italian company (about 200 awards in 2026-27)
grants.description: Scholarships for English-taught master's and postgraduate courses at Italian universities in engineering and advanced technologies, architecture and design, and economics and management, with Italian language study and a mandatory company internship.

grants.name: Ulam NAWA Programme
grants.funder: Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2026 call closed 15 May 2026 with residencies starting from February 2027. The next call is usually announced in spring.
grants.region: Researchers with a doctorate working abroad, of any nationality, who have not worked or studied in Poland in the preceding 3 years
grants.amount: Monthly stipend plus mobility and family allowances
grants.description: Funds research stays in Poland for researchers holding a PhD who are based abroad, in any discipline. The Polish host institution submits the application on the researcher's behalf.

grants.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
grants.funder: World Bank and Government of Japan
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 windows for developing-country nationals: Window 1 runs 18 January to 26 February 2027; Window 2 runs 29 March to 21 May 2027. Applicants need unconditional admission to a participating master's programme first.
grants.region: Nationals of eligible World Bank developing member countries (India is on the list); must study outside home country
grants.amount: Tuition, health insurance, monthly living allowance, economy airfare and US$600 travel allowance per trip
grants.description: Master's scholarships in development-related fields at 44 participating programmes in the US, Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan, for mid-career professionals with at least 3 years of development-related work experience. Scholars must return home after graduation.

grants.name: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (ADB-JSP)
grants.funder: Asian Development Bank and Government of Japan
grants.deadlineNote: Applications go to the designated partner universities in Asia and the Pacific; each sets its own deadline, often between July and April before the intake.
grants.region: Nationals of ADB borrowing member countries (India included), aged 35 or under, resident in home country
grants.amount: Full tuition, monthly subsistence and housing allowance, books, medical insurance and travel
grants.description: Master's scholarships in development-related fields such as economics, management, science and technology at designated institutions in the Asia-Pacific region. Applicants need two years of work experience and must return home to work for two years afterwards.

grants.name: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
grants.funder: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (FCDO)
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027/28 CSC window closed 20 October 2026; nominators submit candidates by December 2026. The next round usually opens in September, with the Indian nominating agency (Ministry of Education) setting an earlier deadline.
grants.region: Citizens and permanent residents of eligible Commonwealth countries including India who cannot otherwise afford UK study
grants.amount: Full tuition, return airfare, monthly stipend of GBP 1,712 (GBP 2,000 in London) and a study travel grant
grants.description: Fully funded one-year taught master's study at a UK university. Candidates must be nominated by their national nominating agency or an approved NGO and also apply through the CSC online system.

grants.name: Michigan Society of Fellows Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; the application opens 1 August and closes in mid-September (14 September 2026 for the 2027-2030 term).
grants.region: Open internationally; the Society sponsors visas (normally J-1)
grants.amount: About US$63,000 per year stipend plus research funds
grants.description: Three-year fellowships combining a postdoctoral appointment in the Society with an assistant professor appointment in an affiliated department, for recent PhDs in the humanities, arts, sciences and professions.

grants.name: ETH Zurich Postdoctoral Fellowships (ETH Fellows)
grants.deadlineNote: Two calls a year, closing 1 March and 1 September at 17:00 Swiss time (moved to the Monday if on a weekend). The call opens about a month before each deadline.
grants.region: Open internationally; fellowship held at ETH Zurich with an ETH professor as host
grants.amount: Full postdoctoral salary at ETH rates plus CHF 12,000 per year for research and travel
grants.description: Fellowships for researchers within two years of their PhD (or completing it within six months of the deadline) to carry out their own project at ETH Zurich in any of its fields. Applicants need at least one peer-reviewed publication or a thesis prize.

grants.name: Radcliffe Institute Fellowship
grants.funder: Harvard Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; for 2027-28, applications in the humanities, social sciences, creative arts and journalism were due 10 September 2026, and in science, engineering and mathematics 1 October 2026. Expect similar dates in 2027.
grants.region: Open to scholars, scientists and artists worldwide
grants.amount: US$78,000 stipend plus US$5,000 project expenses
grants.description: A residential fellowship at Harvard for about 50 scholars, scientists, writers, journalists and artists each year to pursue an individual project. Applicants apply in their field category with a project proposal.

grants.name: Harvard Society of Fellows Junior Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Candidates are nominated, usually by their advisers; nominations open in early July and close in early August (4 August 2026 for fellowships starting in 2027).
grants.region: Open internationally by nomination; fellowship held at Harvard
grants.amount: Annual stipend plus housing and research support
grants.description: Three-year fellowships for scholars at the start of their careers, in any field, to pursue independent research at Harvard without formal degree requirements. Candidates cannot apply themselves and must be nominated.

grants.name: Trinity College Cambridge Junior Research Fellowships
grants.deadlineNote: Annual competition; applications close in late August (27 August 2026 for October 2027 starts), with shortlisting in October and election in January.
grants.region: Open to applicants of any nationality for whom this would be a first substantial academic post
grants.amount: GBP 46,928 per year (stipend plus housing allowance)
grants.description: Research fellowships in all subjects for doctoral students near completion and recent PhDs, offering a period of independent research at Trinity College, Cambridge. Shortlisted candidates submit their dissertation for assessment.

grants.name: Princeton Society of Fellows in the Liberal Arts Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual competition posted in May; applications close in early August (4 August 2026 for 2027-2030).
grants.region: Open internationally; fellowship held at Princeton
grants.amount: Salary as Associate Research Scholar and Lecturer with research funds
grants.description: Three-year postdoctoral fellowships in the humanities and humanistic social sciences, combining independent research with half-time teaching. Applicants must have received the PhD recently or complete it before the fellowship starts.

grants.name: Azrieli International Postdoctoral Fellowship
grants.deadlineNote: Annual call; the 2027-28 round ran 9 August to 11 November 2026. Expect the next call to open in August 2027.
grants.region: PhD holders from any country except Israel, without an Israeli degree; held at an Israeli academic institution
grants.amount: ILS 168,000 per year plus ILS 20,000 per year for research and travel
grants.description: Up to 24 postdoctoral fellowships a year for recent PhDs to do research at an Israeli university or academic institution. A faculty sponsor at the host institution is required at the time of application.

grants.name: Taiwan Scholarship (Ministry of Education)
grants.funder: Ministry of Education, Taiwan (via Taipei Economic and Cultural Center in India)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; the 2026 application deadline to TECC New Delhi was 31 March 2026, with results in May. The 2027 guide is usually published in January or February. Applicants must also apply separately to Taiwanese universities.
grants.region: Indian nationals; applications through the Taipei Economic and Cultural Center in New Delhi
grants.amount: Tuition and fees up to NTD 40,000 per semester plus a monthly stipend of NTD 15,000 (bachelor's) or NTD 20,000 (master's and PhD)
grants.duration: Up to 4 years (bachelor's), 2 years (master's) or 4 years (PhD)
grants.description: Taiwanese government scholarships for Indian students to take a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree at a Taiwanese university in any field.

grants.name: Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (Mandarin study in Taiwan)
grants.funder: Ministry of Education, Taiwan (via Taipei Economic and Cultural Center in India)
grants.deadlineNote: Annual cycle; the 2026 round opened 1 February and closed 17 April 2026. Expect a similar window in 2027.
grants.region: Indian nationals over 18 with at least a senior secondary qualification
grants.amount: NTD 28,000 per month
grants.description: Scholarships for Indians to study Mandarin Chinese at university-affiliated language centres in Taiwan. Open to students and graduates of any discipline.

grants.name: Ernst Mach Grant (worldwide)
grants.funder: Austrian Agency for Education and Internationalisation (OeAD)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for research stays in the 2027/28 academic year close 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET. Earliest start September 2027.
grants.region: Researchers of all nationalities except Austrian, aged 35 or under
grants.amount: Monthly grant set by OeAD (see grant regulations)
grants.description: Grants for doctoral candidates enrolled outside Austria, recent graduates and early postdocs to carry out a research stay at an Austrian university or research institution in any discipline.

grants.name: HKU Presidential PhD Scholar Programme
grants.deadlineNote: Main round for 2027/28 admission runs 1 September to 1 December 2026; later clearing rounds depend on vacancies. Applicants are encouraged to apply for the HKPFS at the same time.
grants.region: Open to all applicants to HKU's full-time PhD programme
grants.amount: Up to about HK$445,800 in year 1: monthly scholarship of HK$28,700, fee waiver, cash award, travel allowance and first-year hall place
grants.description: HKU's flagship PhD scholarship for outstanding research students in any field. All full-time PhD applicants are considered automatically; shortlisted candidates may be interviewed.

grants.name: KAUST Visiting Student Research Program (VSRP)
grants.funder: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
grants.deadlineNote: Rolling; applications accepted year-round with flexible start dates.
grants.region: Open internationally; third- and fourth-year bachelor's students and master's students with GPA 3.5/4 or equivalent
grants.amount: US$1,000 per month stipend, housing and return airfare
grants.description: Research internships in KAUST labs in Saudi Arabia for undergraduate and master's students in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Applicants need a faculty recommendation letter.

grants.name: Caltech Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications and recommendation letters due 22 February 2027. Applicants must first agree a project with a Caltech faculty mentor.
grants.region: Open to visiting undergraduates from other universities, including international students (on-campus projects only; JPL placements are US-only)
grants.amount: US$8,354 for the ten-week fellowship (2027)
grants.description: Summer research fellowships for undergraduates to work with a Caltech faculty mentor on a project they propose. Visiting applicants need a GPA of at least 2.5/4, a research proposal and two recommendation letters.

grants.name: Jacobs Foundation Research Fellowship Program
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027 call opens on 25 November 2026; calls usually close in early February. Check the page for the exact 2027 deadline.
grants.region: Worldwide; PhD awarded within the last 10 years
grants.amount: Partial salary plus research costs (assistants, equipment, travel), paid to the host institution
grants.description: Fellowships for early- and mid-career researchers whose work improves the learning and development of children and youth, across education sciences, psychology, economics, neuroscience and related fields.

grants.name: RAI Emslie Horniman Anthropological Scholarship Fund
grants.deadlineNote: Closes 31 March each year; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in late May or early June.
grants.region: Nationals of the UK, Ireland or any Commonwealth country (Indian nationals eligible)
grants.amount: Up to GBP 10,000 per project
grants.description: Fieldwork grants for MPhil or PhD research in anthropology, with preference for fieldwork outside the UK. Holders of a doctorate and undergraduate or master's projects are not eligible.

grants.name: Spencer Foundation Small Research Grants on Education
grants.deadlineNote: Normally two rounds a year. Spencer will not open new competitions from January to June 2027 and expects to announce its new schedule in June 2027.
grants.region: US and international; PI must hold a doctorate and the grant is administered by a non-profit or public institution
grants.amount: Up to USD 50,000 (plus up to USD 10,000 course release in some cases)
grants.description: Grants for education research projects from any discipline. Proposals are accepted from the US and internationally; graduate students cannot be PI.

grants.name: Belfer Center Research Fellowships (2027-28)
grants.funder: Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs, Harvard Kennedy School
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 1 December 2026; recommendation letters due 15 December 2026.
grants.region: International applicants accepted for most programmes; some fellowships are tied to specific countries
grants.amount: Stipend for most residential fellowships (amount not listed)
grants.description: Residential fellowships for predoctoral candidates, recent PhDs and junior faculty in programmes such as International Security, Managing the Atom, Technology and Geopolitics, Energy and Climate Policy, and the Arctic Initiative.

grants.name: International Law Seminar (Geneva)
grants.funder: United Nations Office at Geneva and the International Law Commission
grants.deadlineNote: The application period for the 61st session opens in spring 2027; the session usually runs in late May to July. Recommendation letters must be dated 2027.
grants.region: Worldwide; fellowships available on request, mainly for participants from developing countries
grants.amount: Fellowships may cover travel and living costs in Geneva
grants.description: Annual seminar held alongside the session of the International Law Commission for postgraduate students, young scholars, government officials and young lawyers in public international law.

grants.name: LAMP Fellowship (Legislative Assistants to Members of Parliament)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027-28 cohort open on 29 November 2026; the deadline is announced on the PRS site.
grants.region: Indian citizens aged 25 or below with at least a bachelor's degree
grants.amount: Monthly stipend
grants.duration: About 11 months, from the Monsoon session to the end of the Budget session
grants.description: Fellows work full-time with a Member of Parliament on legislative research and policy analysis, with training from PRS.

grants.name: SPSSI Grants-in-Aid
grants.funder: Society for the Psychological Study of Social Issues (SPSSI)
grants.deadlineNote: Two rounds a year, 15 May and 15 October; time-sensitive projects can apply at any time by email.
grants.region: SPSSI members at any type of institution; membership is open internationally
grants.amount: Up to USD 1,000 for graduate students; up to USD 2,000 for PhD holders
grants.description: Small grants for scientific research on social problems in line with SPSSI's goals. Graduate student applicants need a faculty sponsor and are usually at the dissertation stage.

grants.name: Regional Studies Association Research and Travel Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Expressions of interest for the Early Career, Membership and Fellowship Research Grants close 3 March 2027; travel grant rounds close 8 March and 15 September 2027.
grants.region: RSA members worldwide; Start-Up Grants and conference bursaries target researchers in emerging economies and the Global South
grants.amount: Early Career Research Grant up to GBP 11,000; Membership Research Grant up to GBP 5,500; travel grants up to GBP 550
grants.description: Grants for members working on regional and urban studies, including early career research grants for researchers within 5 years of their doctorate, research network grants and travel grants.

grants.name: Atlantic Fellows for Social and Economic Equity (AFSEE), 2027-28 cohort
grants.funder: International Inequalities Institute, London School of Economics
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 11 January 2027, 5.00pm UK time.
grants.region: Worldwide; most Fellows come from the Global South; at least 7 years of relevant experience
grants.amount: Funded fellowship (residential track includes the LSE MSc in Inequalities and Social Science)
grants.description: Fellowship for researchers, activists and practitioners working against inequality, with a residential track (MSc at LSE) and a non-residential track (postgraduate certificate).

grants.name: Mercatus Fellowship (Hayek Program)
grants.funder: Mercatus Center at George Mason University
grants.deadlineNote: The 2027-28 dates are not yet posted. The last cycle had an early decision deadline of 1 January and a final deadline of 30 March.
grants.region: Any nationality, enrolled in or affiliated with an accredited institution anywhere; payment to international fellows depends on legal and tax rules
grants.amount: Stipend up to USD 4,000, plus readings and travel to in-person colloquia
grants.description: Year-long reading and colloquium programme in political economy and the Austrian and Virginia traditions for graduate students, early-career scholars and practitioners. It replaces several earlier named Mercatus fellowships such as the Adam Smith Fellowship.

grants.name: Hague Academy of International Law Doctoral Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for summer 2027 close 31 January 2027, 23:59 The Hague time.
grants.region: PhD candidates from non-OECD countries living in their home country (India eligible)
grants.amount: EUR 2,250 plus half of travel costs up to EUR 910
grants.duration: Two months (July and August) in The Hague
grants.description: Scholarships for doctoral candidates in international law to research their thesis at the Peace Palace Library during the summer, with access to the General Course and a related Special Course. Candidates must expect to defend by 31 December of the following year.

grants.name: Wenner-Gren Engaged Research Grant
grants.deadlineNote: Annual deadline 1 August for projects starting no earlier than 1 April of the following year; the portal opens two months before.
grants.amount: Up to USD 25,000
grants.description: Grants for collaborative anthropological research done in long-term partnership with communities who have historically been subjects of research. The applicant of record must hold or be pursuing a doctorate in anthropology, and teams must include community members as core partners.

grants.name: United Nations International Law Fellowship Programme
grants.funder: Codification Division, UN Office of Legal Affairs
grants.deadlineNote: Annual summer course at the Peace Palace, The Hague. The 2026 deadline was 30 March 2026; the 2027 call is expected on a similar schedule.
grants.region: Professionals from developing countries and emerging economies, mainly government officials and teachers of international law
grants.amount: Stipend for local living costs; no fees
grants.description: Training programme in public international law for up to 20 participants, combining Codification Division lectures with the Hague Academy summer session.

grants.name: UNU-WIDER Visiting Scholars Programme
grants.funder: United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER)
grants.deadlineNote: One round a year: the online form opens 1 September and closes 30 September (23:59 UTC+3).
grants.region: Worldwide; early-career, female and developing-country researchers particularly encouraged
grants.amount: Monthly stipend of EUR 3,375 plus medical insurance; supplementary travel grant for fares above EUR 1,200
grants.description: Sabbatical visits at UNU-WIDER for PhD holders in economics or development-related disciplines to write papers for the WIDER working paper series and give a seminar.

grants.name: Glushko Dissertation Prizes in Cognitive Science (2027)
grants.funder: Cognitive Science Society and the Glushko-Samuelson Foundation
grants.deadlineNote: Nominations and letters of support due 19 January 2027; PhD awarded between 18 January 2025 and 19 January 2027.
grants.amount: USD 15,000 plus three years of society membership
grants.description: Annual prizes for outstanding dissertations that cut across the fields of cognitive science (psychology, computer science, philosophy, linguistics, anthropology, neuroscience, education). Winners must attend the annual conference in person.

grants.name: Cognitive Science Society Student Travel Grants (CogSci 2027)
grants.funder: Cognitive Science Society and the Robert J. Glushko and Pamela Samuelson Fund
grants.deadlineNote: Students opt in when submitting a paper to the conference; submissions open 30 November and close 1 February. Awards are announced in mid-May.
grants.region: Worldwide; student first authors of full papers
grants.amount: About 45 awards of USD 750 to 1,500 depending on travel distance (undergraduate Sayan Gul Award: USD 750 plus registration)
grants.description: Travel support for undergraduate and graduate students who are first authors of full-length papers at the annual Cognitive Science Society conference, selected on need and paper quality.

grants.name: IPSA World Congress 2027 Travel Grants and Global South Awards
grants.deadlineNote: Applications for the Stein Rokkan Travel Grant and the Margaret A. Vogt Award for Global South Scholars close 1 March 2027. The Congress is in Rome, 24 to 28 July 2027.
grants.region: IPSA members; Vogt Award for Global South scholars; Stein Rokkan grant for graduate students
grants.amount: USD 1,000 each
grants.description: Travel support to attend the 29th IPSA World Congress of Political Science. IPSA also runs a Global South Solidarity Fund for political scientists from developing countries in financial need.

grants.name: AI and the Workforce (IHS Request for Proposals)
grants.deadlineNote: Applications close 15 December 2026; decisions announced 15 January 2027.
grants.region: Academic scholars; the page sets no country restriction
grants.amount: Up to USD 20,000; larger awards possible for exceptional projects
grants.description: Research grants on how artificial intelligence affects employment, productivity, occupational change, economic opportunity and innovation. Covers research travel, assistants, datasets and publishing costs, but not living costs, hardware or overhead.

grants.name: Max Planck Institute for Comparative and International Private Law Scholarships for International Researchers
grants.funder: Max Planck Institute for Comparative and International Private Law, Hamburg
grants.deadlineNote: One application round a year; the round for 2027 closed on 15 August 2026. Expect the next round on a similar date in 2027.
grants.region: Legal scholars whose main residence is outside Germany
grants.amount: Monthly scholarship funded by the Max Planck Society
grants.description: A limited number of scholarships for research stays at the Hamburg institute in comparative law, private international law and commercial law, with use of its library.

grants.name: Khyentse Foundation Academic Development Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Two windows a year: 15 March to 15 June and 15 September to 15 December (23:59 US Eastern). Submit an indication of interest first.
grants.region: Global; applications must come from a university or academic institution
grants.amount: Varies by project
grants.description: Grants to universities for programmes that strengthen academic Buddhist studies and research, including teaching posts and outreach to students and the public. Conferences, construction and overheads are not funded.

grants.name: Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Program in Buddhist Studies
grants.deadlineNote: Public Impact Grants close 20 Nov 2026; New Professorships 1 Feb 2027; Buddhism Public Scholars 2 Apr 2027. Dissertation and Early Career Research Fellowships usually close in late October.
grants.region: Global competitions with no citizenship or residence restriction (Public Scholars need work authorisation in the host country); scholars in Asia encouraged
grants.amount: Public Impact Grants USD 10,000 to 50,000; fellowships and professorship grants vary
grants.description: Global competitions supporting Buddhist studies: dissertation and early career fellowships, grants to create new professorships, public impact grants, and public scholar placements. Applications are in English.

grants.name: Barakat Trust Grants and Scholarships
grants.deadlineNote: 2027 cycle opens 1 January 2027; most deadlines are 31 March (Major Awards need an expression of interest by mid-February).
grants.region: International; some studentships and Oxford scholarships are reserved for applicants from the Islamic world
grants.amount: Travel awards up to GBP 2,500; Major Awards up to GBP 10,000; publication grants up to GBP 6,000
grants.description: Grants for the study of Islamic art, architecture, archaeology and conservation, including early career travel awards, major research awards for scholars and curators, and publication grants. Funds are paid to an institution, not a personal account.

grants.name: Max van Berchem Foundation Research Grants
grants.deadlineNote: Applications by email by 31 March 2027; decisions in July.
grants.region: International; applicants must hold a doctorate
grants.amount: No fixed limit; detailed budget required
